text: What is a computer peripheral?
options: The main processor inside a computer
A device connected to and working with a computer
The power supply unit of a computer
explanation: A peripheral is a device that connects to and works with a computer to extend its capabilities.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is an INPUT peripheral?
explanation: The keyboard sends data into the computer so it is an input peripheral.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is an OUTPUT peripheral?
explanation: The printer produces output (printed documents) from the computer so it is an output peripheral.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A microphone is classified as which type of peripheral?
explanation: A microphone captures sound and sends it into the computer; it is an input device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A speaker is classified as which type of peripheral?
explanation: A speaker receives audio signals from the computer and plays them out; it is an output device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral allows you to convert a printed photo into a digital image?
explanation: A scanner digitises physical documents and images so they can be used on a computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following correctly pairs a peripheral with its type?
explanation: A speaker produces sound output from the computer; the other pairs are all wrong.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is used to record your voice into a computer?
explanation: A microphone records audio (voice) and sends it to the computer as input.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The printer is connected to a computer mainly to perform which task?
explanation: A printer's primary job is to produce hard-copy (printed) output from digital documents.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is used mainly to point and click on items on the screen?
explanation: The mouse is a pointing device used to navigate and interact with on-screen elements.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Audio speakers are usually plugged into which port on a computer cabinet?
explanation: Speakers connect to the audio-out jack — the 3.5 mm green socket on the back of the cabinet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is NOT an input peripheral?
explanation: The speaker receives and plays audio from the computer — it is an output device; all others send data into the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is NOT an output peripheral?
explanation: The scanner sends data into the computer; it is an input device. The others all produce output.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to listen to music from her computer. Which peripheral does she need?
explanation: Speakers are output devices that play audio; she needs speakers to hear the music.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A teacher wants to print a worksheet. Which peripheral does she use?
explanation: The printer produces hard-copy paper output from digital files.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to save a hand-drawn map as a digital file. Which peripheral does he use?
explanation: The scanner converts the physical drawing into a digital image file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following best describes what a scanner does?
options: It plays sounds from the computer
It converts physical documents into digital files
It sends keystrokes to the computer
explanation: A scanner captures a physical document or image and converts it into a digital file stored on the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What type of peripheral is a computer keyboard?
explanation: The keyboard sends typed data into the computer; it is an input device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which two peripherals listed are BOTH input devices?
explanation: The keyboard and mouse both send data into the computer; they are both input peripherals.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which two peripherals listed are BOTH output devices?
explanation: The printer produces paper output and the speaker produces audio output; both are output peripherals.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral uses ink cartridges or toner?
explanation: Printers use ink cartridges (inkjet) or toner cartridges (laser) to print onto paper.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Voice Recorder app on a computer do?
explanation: The Voice Recorder (also called Sound Recorder) uses the microphone to capture and save audio as a digital file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After recording audio with the Voice Recorder app; where is the recording saved?
options: It is saved as a digital audio file on the computer
It is sent to the speaker only
It is displayed as text on screen
explanation: The Voice Recorder saves the recording as a digital audio file on the computer's storage.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which step is correct when plugging in a speaker to a desktop computer?
options: Plug the speaker cable into the USB keyboard port
Plug the speaker cable into the green audio-out jack on the cabinet
Plug the speaker cable into the monitor
Plug the speaker cable into the power socket
explanation: Desktop computer cabinets have a 3.5 mm audio-out jack (usually green) specifically for speakers.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student records his voice using the microphone and Voice Recorder app. What kind of file is produced?
explanation: The Voice Recorder app saves the captured audio as a sound file (e.g. .m4a or .wma).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral produces BOTH visual and audio output simultaneously?
explanation: A monitor with built-in speakers produces both visual output (display) and audio output (sound) at the same time.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A class wants to hear the teacher's audio explanation from the computer. Which peripheral is NEEDED?
explanation: Speakers are required to hear audio output from the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of these statements about a printer is CORRECT?
options: A printer sends images into the computer
A printer is an input device
A printer produces hard-copy output on paper
explanation: A printer receives digital data from the computer and produces physical (hard-copy) printed output.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of these statements about a scanner is CORRECT?
options: A scanner converts physical documents to digital files
explanation: A scanner digitises physical documents or images so they can be used and stored on the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A keyboard and a mouse are connected to which common port type on modern computers?
explanation: Modern keyboards and mice connect to the computer via USB ports.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is used to type text into a document?
explanation: The keyboard is the primary input peripheral for typing text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the function of the mouse scroll wheel?
options: To scroll up and down a page
explanation: The scroll wheel allows the user to scroll vertically through documents and web pages.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral would a student use to make a video call and be heard by others?
explanation: A microphone captures the student's voice and sends it as audio input during a video call.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The back of a desktop computer cabinet contains various ports. The GREEN port is typically used for?
explanation: The green 3.5 mm jack on a desktop cabinet is the audio-out port used to connect speakers.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral converts a drawing from paper into a digital image the computer can display?
explanation: The scanner captures the physical drawing and converts it into a digital image file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student right-clicks with the mouse. What does the right-click usually do?
explanation: Right-clicking with the mouse typically opens a context menu with options relevant to the item clicked.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is described as: 'a device that produces a paper copy of information stored in a computer'?
explanation: This description matches the printer; it produces hard-copy paper output from digital data.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What type of peripheral is a flatbed scanner?
explanation: A flatbed scanner is an input device — it captures a physical image and sends it into the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is the correct definition of an OUTPUT peripheral?
options: A device that sends data into the computer
A device that stores data permanently
A device that receives data from the computer and presents it to the user
explanation: An output peripheral receives processed data from the computer and presents it in a usable form (e.g. printed page; sound).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is the correct definition of an INPUT peripheral?
options: A device that presents processed data to the user
A device that sends data or instructions into the computer
A device that stores files on a disk
A device that connects computers in a network
explanation: An input peripheral sends data or instructions INTO the computer for processing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student plugs a USB microphone into his laptop. To record his voice he should open which application?
explanation: The Voice Recorder / Sound Recorder app uses the connected microphone to capture and save audio recordings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral can act as BOTH an input device and an output device?
explanation: A touch-screen monitor displays output AND accepts touch input; it is both input and output.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When connecting speakers to a desktop computer; the cable colour that matches the audio-out jack is?
explanation: The audio-out jack (line-out) on desktop computers is colour-coded green.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does a peripheral need in order to work with a computer?
options: It must be the same brand as the computer
It must be connected to the computer (via cable or wirelessly)
It must be stored inside the computer case
It must have its own power supply
explanation: A peripheral must be physically or wirelessly connected to the computer to communicate with it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is an input device that detects movement on a surface and moves the on-screen pointer?
explanation: The mouse detects physical movement and translates it into pointer movement on screen — it is an input device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following tasks requires a PRINTER?
options: Producing a paper copy of a class timetable
explanation: Producing a paper copy (hard copy) requires a printer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following tasks requires a SCANNER?
options: Saving a hand-drawn diagram as a digital file
explanation: A scanner is needed to convert a physical drawing into a digital file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following tasks requires a MICROPHONE?
explanation: A microphone is required to capture audio input such as a voice message.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A peripheral that is NOT plugged directly into the computer but communicates via radio waves is called?
explanation: Peripherals that connect without a physical cable — using Bluetooth or Wi-Fi — are called wireless peripherals.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The microphone jack on a desktop computer cabinet is usually colour-coded?
explanation: The microphone-in jack is colour-coded pink on desktop computer cabinets.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Arrange these steps in the correct order to record audio using Voice Recorder on Windows 10: (1) Click the record button; (2) Open the Voice Recorder app; (3) Click stop; (4) Name and save the file
explanation: You must first open the app; then click record; then stop; then the file is saved.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to share a physical certificate with a friend by email. Which TWO peripherals does she need?
explanation: She needs the scanner to convert the physical certificate to a digital file; and the keyboard (and mouse) to compose and send the email.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral listed is used to move the cursor AND to select/drag items on screen?
explanation: The mouse moves the on-screen cursor and its buttons are used to click; select; and drag items.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A printer that sprays tiny droplets of ink onto paper is called a(n)?
explanation: An inkjet printer sprays microscopic ink droplets onto paper to form text and images.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A printer that uses a beam of light to fuse toner powder onto paper is called a(n)?
explanation: A laser printer uses a laser beam and heat to fuse toner (fine powder) onto paper.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which type of printer is most commonly found in homes and small offices for everyday colour printing?
explanation: Inkjet printers are affordable and produce good colour output; making them popular for home and small-office use.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'DPI' stand for in the context of printers and scanners?
explanation: DPI (Dots Per Inch) measures the resolution of a printer or scanner — higher DPI means finer detail.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A scanner with a higher DPI setting will produce an image that is?
options: More detailed and higher in resolution
explanation: Higher DPI means more dots are captured per inch; resulting in a more detailed (higher-resolution) image.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The Voice Recorder app is found on which operating system discussed in Book 4?
explanation: Book 4 is based on Windows 10/11; and the Voice Recorder app is a built-in Windows application.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student accidentally disconnects the speaker cable during a song. What will happen?
options: The song file will be deleted
The audio will stop playing through the speaker
explanation: Disconnecting the speaker stops the audio output; the song continues playing on the computer but cannot be heard.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is described as: 'an input device that converts physical images and text into digital format'?
explanation: This is the definition of a scanner.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is described as: 'an output device that converts digital audio signals into sound waves'?
explanation: This is the definition of a speaker.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is described as: 'an input device that captures audio and converts it into a digital signal'?
explanation: This is the definition of a microphone.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to produce a poster for a school display. She designs it on the computer. Which peripheral produces the final paper poster?
explanation: The printer produces the physical (paper) copy of the digitally designed poster.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is an EXTERNAL peripheral? (i.e. not built into the main computer unit)
explanation: The keyboard is an external peripheral connected to the outside of the computer; RAM; CPU and internal hard drives are inside the main unit.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student records 30 seconds of audio using Voice Recorder. After stopping the recording; where can she find the saved file?
options: In the Voice Recorder app's saved recordings list
explanation: The Voice Recorder app automatically saves recordings and lists them within the app so users can play them back.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens when you click the 'Record' button in the Voice Recorder app?
options: A document is sent to the printer
explanation: Clicking Record starts the microphone input; the app records audio until you click Stop.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is the BEST reason to use a wireless keyboard?
options: It is always faster to type on
It eliminates the need for a cable; allowing more freedom of movement
It can also act as a scanner
explanation: A wireless keyboard uses Bluetooth or a wireless receiver; freeing the user from a cable and allowing more flexible positioning.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student has both a keyboard and a mouse connected. She wants to open a file. Which peripheral is MOST efficient for double-clicking the file icon?
explanation: Double-clicking a file icon to open it is done with the mouse; which is designed for precise on-screen pointing and clicking.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The scroll wheel on a mouse is located?
options: Between the left and right buttons
explanation: The scroll wheel is positioned between the left and right mouse buttons for convenient thumb-operated scrolling.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A left-handed student wants to swap the functions of the mouse buttons. Where does she go to change this setting?
options: Mouse settings in Control Panel / Settings
explanation: Mouse button configuration (including swapping buttons for left-hand use) is changed in the Mouse section of Windows Settings or Control Panel.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral sends information FROM the user TO the computer?
explanation: The scanner captures a physical document and sends that information into the computer; making it an input peripheral.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral sends information FROM the computer TO the user?
explanation: The printer receives data from the computer and produces a physical output for the user; making it an output peripheral.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student drops a USB keyboard. She plugs it back in and it works immediately. This is because USB is?
explanation: USB is a hot-pluggable (plug-and-play) interface — devices can be connected and disconnected without restarting the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How many buttons does a standard computer mouse typically have?
explanation: A standard mouse has three main controls: left button; right button; and a scroll wheel that also acts as a middle button.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A flatbed scanner works by?
options: Using a moving light source to capture an image of the document
explanation: A flatbed scanner uses a moving lamp and sensors to capture a digital image of the document placed on its glass surface.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following could be used instead of a microphone to input text?
explanation: A keyboard can be used to type (input) text into a computer; serving as an alternative to voice/microphone input.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student's microphone is not working. She uses the keyboard instead. What type of input does she now produce?
explanation: Typing on the keyboard produces typed text input; not audio.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A computer receives an email with a voice attachment. To HEAR the voice message the student needs?
explanation: The speaker (output peripheral) is needed to play the audio voice attachment so the student can hear it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is NOT typically connected via the audio jack?
explanation: A USB keyboard connects via a USB port; not an audio jack. Headphones; speakers; and microphones use the 3.5 mm audio jack.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student scans a page from her textbook. The scanner produces a?
explanation: The scanner outputs a digital image file of the physical page.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'USB' stand for?
explanation: USB stands for Universal Serial Bus; a standard interface for connecting peripherals to computers.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student connects a wired mouse. The first thing the operating system does is?
options: Detect and install the device driver
explanation: When a USB device is connected; the OS detects it and loads or installs the appropriate device driver so it can communicate with the peripheral.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is used to input data by pressing keys?
explanation: The keyboard is an input device where each key press sends a character or command to the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The 'clicking' action on a mouse is performed using?
options: The mouse buttons (left or right click)
explanation: Mouse buttons (left and right) are clicked to select; open; or access context menus on screen.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Book 4; which two types of peripherals are introduced in Chapter 1?
explanation: Chapter 1 of Terabytes Book 4 introduces and classifies input peripherals and output peripherals.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student notices her speaker is making no sound. Which should she check FIRST?
options: Whether the speaker cable is plugged into the audio-out jack
Whether the scanner glass is clean
explanation: The most common reason for no speaker output is the cable not being connected to the correct audio-out port.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A printer is to OUTPUT as a scanner is to?
explanation: A printer is an output device; correspondingly; a scanner is an input device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: A keyboard is an output device
A speaker is an input device
A scanner is an input device
A printer is an input device
explanation: A scanner captures physical documents and sends them into the computer — it is an input device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: A microphone is an input device
A printer is an output device
A speaker is an input device
A keyboard is an input device
explanation: A speaker is an OUTPUT device; it plays audio FROM the computer. The statement 'a speaker is an input device' is false.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student has a wired headset (headphones + microphone combined). The headset acts as?
options: Both an input and an output device
explanation: The headphones in the headset are output (playing sound) and the built-in microphone is input (capturing voice); so it is both.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral is most suitable for a visually-impaired student who needs to navigate the computer?
explanation: A keyboard combined with screen-reader software allows visually-impaired users to navigate a computer using audio feedback without relying on the visual display.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the 'Enter' key on the keyboard?
options: It confirms a command or moves the cursor to a new line
explanation: The Enter/Return key confirms entries; executes commands; or moves the text cursor to a new paragraph line.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is the correct sequence to use the Voice Recorder app on Windows 10?
options: Start Menu → Voice Recorder → Record → Stop
explanation: On Windows 10 you open Voice Recorder from the Start Menu; click the microphone/Record button; then click Stop to end and auto-save the recording.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A scanner connected via USB but not recognised by the computer most likely needs?
options: A device driver to be installed
The microphone to be turned off
explanation: If a peripheral is not recognised; the correct device driver (software that lets the OS communicate with the hardware) needs to be installed.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Two students argue: Ama says a monitor is an output device; Kofi says it is an input device. Who is correct?
options: Neither; it is a storage device
Both; it is both input and output
explanation: Ama is correct. A standard monitor DISPLAYS (outputs) information from the computer; making it an output device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral stores NO data permanently and simply allows the user to type commands?
explanation: The keyboard is a pure input device — it sends keystrokes to the computer but stores nothing itself.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student uses the mouse to drag a file icon from one folder to another. This action is called?
explanation: Holding the left mouse button and moving the mouse to reposition an object is called 'drag and drop.'
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which peripheral in Book 4 Chapter 1 is used to bring SOUND into the computer?
explanation: The microphone is the input peripheral that captures sound and brings audio data into the computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student's printer runs out of ink in the middle of printing. The page will?
options: Print in a different colour automatically
Partially print or produce faded/blank areas
explanation: When ink runs low or runs out; the printer either stops mid-print or produces very light; faded; or blank areas on the page.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Book 4 states that peripheral devices are divided into two categories. These are?
explanation: Chapter 1 of Terabytes Book 4 classifies peripheral devices into INPUT devices and OUTPUT devices.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Logo command FD stand for?
explanation: FD stands for Forward; it moves the turtle forward by the number of steps given.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Logo command BK stand for?
explanation: BK stands for Back; it moves the turtle backward by the number of steps given.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Logo command RT stand for?
explanation: RT stands for Right Turn; it rotates the turtle clockwise by the given angle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Logo command LT stand for?
explanation: LT stands for Left Turn; it rotates the turtle anti-clockwise by the given angle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Logo command PU stand for?
explanation: PU stands for Pen Up; it lifts the pen so the turtle moves without drawing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Logo command PD stand for?
explanation: PD stands for Pen Down; it lowers the pen so the turtle draws as it moves.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; the object that moves on screen and draws lines is called a?
explanation: The Logo turtle is the triangular on-screen object that moves and draws lines.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Logo command would you use to move the turtle forward 50 steps?
explanation: FD 50 moves the turtle forward 50 steps in the direction it is currently facing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Logo command would you use to turn the turtle right 90 degrees?
explanation: RT 90 rotates the turtle 90 degrees clockwise (to the right).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To draw a square in Logo; you need to repeat which two commands?
explanation: A square is drawn by repeating FD (move forward) and RT 90 (turn right 90°) four times.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What Logo command draws a square with side 50?
explanation: REPEAT 4 [FD 50 RT 90] repeats the forward-and-right-turn sequence four times to close a square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How many times must the sequence [FD 60 RT 90] be repeated to draw a complete square?
explanation: A square has 4 sides and 4 corners; so the sequence must be repeated 4 times.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the sum of all exterior angles in any closed polygon drawn in Logo?
explanation: The turtle always turns a total of 360° to return to its starting direction; regardless of the polygon.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command draws a circle in Logo (from Terabytes Book 4)?
explanation: REPEAT 360 [FD 1 RT 1] moves the turtle forward 1 step and turns 1° a total of 360 times; creating a circle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In REPEAT 360 [FD 1 RT 1]; what does the number 360 represent?
options: The number of times the sequence is repeated
explanation: 360 is the REPEAT count — the sequence [FD 1 RT 1] is executed 360 times.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In REPEAT 360 [FD 1 RT 1]; what does RT 1 do?
options: Turns the turtle right by 1 degree
explanation: RT 1 turns the turtle 1 degree to the right each iteration; accumulating 360° of turning to make a circle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The general formula for a regular polygon in Logo is REPEAT n [FD length RT ___].
explanation: Each exterior angle of a regular n-sided polygon is 360° ÷ n; so the turn is RT (360/n).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Using REPEAT n [FD length RT (360/n)]; which command draws an equilateral triangle (3 sides) with side 80?
explanation: 360 ÷ 3 = 120°; so REPEAT 3 [FD 80 RT 120] draws an equilateral triangle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Using REPEAT n [FD length RT (360/n)]; which command draws a regular hexagon (6 sides) with side 60?
explanation: 360 ÷ 6 = 60°; so REPEAT 6 [FD 60 RT 60] draws a regular hexagon.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does REPEAT 5 [FD 70 RT 72] draw?
explanation: 360 ÷ 5 = 72°; so REPEAT 5 [FD 70 RT 72] draws a regular pentagon (5 sides).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does REPEAT 8 [FD 40 RT 45] draw?
explanation: 360 ÷ 8 = 45°; so REPEAT 8 [FD 40 RT 45] draws a regular octagon (8 sides).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To draw a square using LT (left turns) instead of RT; you would write?
explanation: LT 90 turns left 90° — repeating four times still closes a square; just drawn anti-clockwise.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What Logo command resets the screen and returns the turtle to the centre?
explanation: CS (ClearScreen) clears the drawing area and returns the turtle to the home position.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What Logo command returns the turtle to its starting (home) position without clearing the screen?
explanation: HOME moves the turtle back to the centre without erasing the drawing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does HIDETURTLE (HT) do in Logo?
options: Makes the turtle invisible but it still draws
explanation: HT (HideTurtle) makes the turtle icon disappear from the screen; it still moves and draws normally.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does SHOWTURTLE (ST) do?
options: Makes the pen draw thicker lines
explanation: ST (ShowTurtle) makes the turtle icon visible again after it has been hidden with HT.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which pair of commands is used to move the turtle without drawing a line?
options: PU and then movement commands; then PD
explanation: PU lifts the pen (no line drawn); the turtle is moved; then PD lowers the pen to resume drawing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student types REPEAT 4 [FD 50 RT 90]. After the command finishes; where is the turtle?
options: Back at the starting point; facing the same direction
explanation: After REPEAT 4 the turtle has completed a full square (360° total turn) and is back where it started.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to draw a pattern of 6 squares around a centre point. Between each square she rotates the turtle 60°. Which command rotates between squares?
explanation: 360° ÷ 6 squares = 60° per step; so RT 60 is used to rotate between drawing each square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To make a Logo procedure (named command); you use which keyword to start?
explanation: The keyword TO starts a procedure definition in Logo; e.g. TO SQUARE.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A Logo procedure ends with which command?
explanation: END closes a procedure definition in Logo.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is a correct Logo procedure for a square?
explanation: TO SQUARE ... END defines the procedure; REPEAT 4 [FD 50 RT 90] is the body that draws the square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; what is the purpose of SETPENCOLOR (or SETPC)?
options: It changes the colour of the line drawn
explanation: SETPC (SetPenColor) changes the colour of the line the turtle draws.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does SETPENSIZE [5] do in Logo?
options: Makes the pen draw lines 5 units thick
explanation: SETPENSIZE sets the thickness (width in pixels) of the line drawn by the turtle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; FD 100 moves the turtle how far?
options: 100 pixels/steps in the direction it faces
explanation: FD 100 moves the turtle 100 steps (pixels) forward in its current heading direction.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the heading of the turtle when it points straight up (North) in Logo?
explanation: In standard Logo; heading 0 means the turtle points straight up (North).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After RT 90 from heading 0 (North); the turtle faces?
explanation: RT 90 from heading 0 (North) rotates the turtle 90° clockwise; so it now faces East (right).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After LT 90 from heading 0 (North); the turtle faces?
explanation: LT 90 from heading 0 (North) rotates the turtle 90° anti-clockwise; so it faces West (left).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command draws a very small circle (almost a point)?
explanation: A very small step (FD 0.1) with RT 1 for 360 repeats gives a very tiny circle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How many sides does the shape drawn by REPEAT 12 [FD 30 RT 30] have?
explanation: REPEAT 12 means the sequence is executed 12 times; giving 12 sides. 12 × 30° = 360° ✓
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student runs REPEAT 3 [FD 80 RT 120]. What shape is drawn?
explanation: RT 120 = 360°/3; three sides of equal length — this draws an equilateral triangle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens if the turtle reaches the edge of the screen in many Logo versions?
options: It wraps around to the opposite edge (or bounces)
explanation: In most Logo implementations the turtle wraps to the opposite edge of the screen when it reaches the boundary.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command makes the turtle go backwards 30 steps?
explanation: BK 30 moves the turtle backward (opposite to its current heading) by 30 steps.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants the turtle to draw 4 separate squares in 4 corners. What command separates the squares (moves without drawing)?
options: PU; move to new position; PD
explanation: PU lifts the pen; the turtle is repositioned; then PD lowers the pen to draw the next square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the minimum number of FD commands needed to draw an equilateral triangle?
explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 sides; so exactly 3 FD commands are needed (one per side).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student types FD 50 RT 90 FD 50 RT 90 FD 50 RT 90 FD 50 RT 90. What has she drawn?
explanation: Four FD 50 RT 90 sequences make a complete 360° turn — this draws a square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command would produce a spiral effect in Logo?
explanation: Increasing the FD distance each iteration while turning the same angle creates an outward spiral.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What angle must the turtle turn each time to draw a regular 9-sided polygon (nonagon)?
explanation: 360° ÷ 9 = 40°; so the turtle turns RT 40 at each vertex.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command in Logo clears all drawings but keeps the turtle where it is?
explanation: CS (ClearScreen) wipes the drawing area; it also returns the turtle to the home position in most implementations.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The Logo REPEAT command follows which format?
explanation: The syntax is REPEAT count [action]; e.g. REPEAT 4 [FD 50 RT 90].
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student runs REPEAT 360 [FD 2 RT 1]. Compared to REPEAT 360 [FD 1 RT 1]; the new circle is?
explanation: Doubling FD (from 1 to 2) doubles the step size each iteration; resulting in a circle with twice the radius.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; the PRINT command is used for?
options: Displaying text or values on screen
explanation: PRINT outputs text or the value of an expression to the Logo console/output area.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student defines TO TRIANGLE ... END and then types TRIANGLE. What happens?
options: An error occurs because procedures cannot be called by name
The turtle draws the shape defined inside the TRIANGLE procedure
explanation: Once defined with TO...END; a Logo procedure is called simply by typing its name.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the correct way to draw an octagon (8 sides) in Logo?
explanation: 360° ÷ 8 = 45°; so REPEAT 8 [FD 50 RT 45] draws a regular octagon.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What angle does RT 360 rotate the turtle?
options: No rotation (or a full 360° back to start)
explanation: RT 360 rotates the turtle a full 360°; it ends up facing the same direction as before — effectively no visible change.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When BK is used; the turtle moves in which direction?
explanation: BK moves the turtle in the direction opposite to its current heading.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; which arithmetic would you perform to find the RT angle for a regular 10-sided polygon?
explanation: Each exterior angle = 360° ÷ number of sides = 360 ÷ 10 = 36°.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of these Logo commands has NO effect on the drawing?
options: PU followed immediately by PD (no movement in between)
explanation: PU lifts the pen and PD immediately puts it down; with no movement in between no visible change occurs.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the command SETXY 0 0 do in Logo?
options: Moves the turtle to the coordinates (0; 0) — the centre of the screen
Draws a line to the origin
Sets both FD and BK to 0
explanation: SETXY (or SETPOS) moves the turtle to specified absolute coordinates; (0; 0) is typically the screen centre.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; what does the variable :SIDE typically represent in a procedure?
options: A parameter for side length passed into the procedure
explanation: In Logo procedures; :SIDE is a conventional parameter name for the length of a shape's side.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the result of running REPEAT 4 [FD 60 RT 90] followed by REPEAT 3 [FD 60 RT 120]?
explanation: The first command draws a square (4 sides; RT 90); the second draws a triangle (3 sides; RT 120).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: If a student wants to draw 10 concentric circles of increasing sizes; which approach is best?
options: REPEAT 10 [PU FD increasing distance PD REPEAT 360 [FD 1 RT 1]]
explanation: PU/FD/PD repositions the starting point further out for each circle; then draws the circle from there.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What colour does the pen start with by default in most Logo implementations?
explanation: The default pen colour is black in most Logo environments; including the one used in Terabytes Book 4.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student draws a square and a circle. She wants the circle to be centred inside the square. She needs to?
options: Use PU; HOME; PD before drawing the circle
Use CS between the two shapes
explanation: PU; HOME; PD lifts the pen; moves the turtle to the centre; puts the pen down — ready to draw the circle from centre.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The Logo programming language was created primarily for?
options: Educational programming and teaching geometry concepts
explanation: Logo was designed by Seymour Papert as an educational tool to teach programming and geometry to children.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The turtle in Logo represents which concept from mathematics?
options: A geometric point with position and heading
explanation: The turtle is a geometric entity with a position (x; y) and a heading (direction); used to explore geometry.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Logo command can be used to change the background colour of the drawing area?
explanation: SETBG (SetBackground) changes the background colour of the Logo drawing area.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To draw a regular polygon with 100 sides (which looks like a circle); you would use?
explanation: 360 ÷ 100 = 3.6°; so REPEAT 100 [FD 2 RT 3.6] draws a 100-sided polygon that looks circular.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student types REPEAT 0 [FD 50 RT 90]. What happens?
explanation: REPEAT 0 executes the block 0 times; so nothing is drawn.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following would produce the LARGEST circle?
explanation: Larger FD values produce larger radii; REPEAT 360 [FD 5 RT 1] has the largest step giving the largest circle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Logo chapter; students learn to draw regular shapes using the REPEAT command. The key insight is that the total turning angle is always?
explanation: For any closed polygon; the turtle turns a total of 360° — this is the exterior angle theorem in action.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does REPEAT 6 [FD 50 RT 60] draw?
explanation: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°; six sides of 50 steps — this is a regular hexagon.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The command REPEAT 4 [FD 80 RT 90] differs from REPEAT 4 [FD 50 RT 90] in what way?
options: The sides are longer (80 vs 50) but both are squares
explanation: Both draw squares (4 sides; RT 90 each); only the side length differs — 80 vs 50.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student runs FD 100 LT 90 FD 100 LT 90 FD 100 LT 90 FD 100 LT 90. What is drawn?
explanation: Four FD 100 LT 90 commands make a 360° anti-clockwise turn; drawing a square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How does Logo teach mathematical concepts?
options: By allowing students to experiment with turtle movements and discover geometric rules
explanation: Logo's turtle graphics approach lets students discover geometry (angles; polygons) through hands-on experimentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Book 4 chapter introduces Logo programming to students?
explanation: Chapter 2 of Terabytes Book 4 introduces students to the Logo programming language and turtle graphics.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is printed by the command PRINT 2 + 3 in Logo?
explanation: PRINT evaluates the expression and outputs the result; 2 + 3 = 5.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; which command checks if the turtle's pen is up or down?
explanation: PEN? (or PENSTATE in some versions) returns whether the pen is currently up or down.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After drawing a square with REPEAT 4 [FD 50 RT 90]; the turtle's heading is the same as before because?
options: The turtle turned 4 × 90° = 360° — a full rotation
The turtle used BK not FD
The RT command doesn't change heading
explanation: 4 right turns of 90° each = 360° total; the turtle faces its original direction.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What kind of shape does REPEAT 72 [FD 5 RT 5] draw?
explanation: 72 iterations × 5° = 360° total turn; with equal steps — this draws a circle-like polygon.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Logo command would you use to erase a mistake and start fresh?
explanation: CS (ClearScreen) erases the drawing and resets the turtle to the home position — a fresh start.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To draw a star in Logo; a student uses REPEAT 5 [FD 100 RT 144]. Why is 144° used?
options: 144 produces the crossing needed for a 5-pointed star (exterior angle of a pentagram)
explanation: A 5-pointed star requires 2 × 360°/5 = 144° turns; the turtle traces each point of the star.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student is in Logo and types FD 50 RT 90 FD 50 RT 90. Has she drawn a complete square?
options: Yes; all four sides are done
No; she has drawn only two sides and two turns — need two more repetitions
Yes; two sides make a square
No; she needs RT 360 to finish
explanation: A square has four sides; only two FD + RT sequences have been executed — she needs to continue twice more.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What symbol denotes a variable in Logo (MSWLogo / FMSLogo)?
explanation: In Logo; variable names are preceded by a colon (e.g. :SIDE) when their value is being referenced.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following best describes Logo?
options: An educational programming language using turtle graphics
explanation: Logo is an educational programming language developed to help students learn programming and mathematics through turtle graphics.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How does changing the RT angle in REPEAT n [FD 50 RT angle] change the shape?
options: It changes the number of sides
It changes the size of the shape
It determines how many sides the polygon has (n = 360/angle)
explanation: The turn angle determines the polygon: angle = 360/n sides; e.g. RT 60 → hexagon; RT 90 → square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student runs REPEAT 3 [FD 60 LT 120]. This draws an equilateral triangle that goes?
explanation: LT (left turn) instead of RT makes the turtle turn anti-clockwise; the triangle is drawn anti-clockwise.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Logo; PENSIZE affects?
options: The thickness of the lines drawn
explanation: PENSIZE (or SETPENSIZE) controls the pixel width of the lines drawn by the turtle.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command makes the turtle turn completely around (180°) to face the opposite direction?
explanation: RT 180 (or LT 180) rotates the turtle 180° so it faces the exact opposite direction.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Book 4 Logo; students draw a circle using REPEAT 360 [FD 1 RT 1]. If FD is changed to FD 3; the circle becomes?
explanation: Each step is 3× as long; so the circumference and radius are approximately 3× larger.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the pen's default state when Logo first opens?
explanation: The turtle's pen is down (PD) by default when Logo starts; ready to draw from the first movement.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the name of the Windows program used to browse and manage files and folders?
explanation: File Explorer (also called Windows Explorer) is the built-in Windows application for navigating and managing files and folders.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which part of File Explorer shows the full path (location) of the current folder?
explanation: The Address Bar at the top of File Explorer displays the full path of the current folder location.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which pane in File Explorer shows the tree structure of drives and folders on the left?
explanation: The Navigation Pane on the left side of File Explorer shows a tree of drives and folders for easy browsing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which part of File Explorer displays the files and folders inside the currently selected folder?
explanation: The File List Pane (main content area) shows all the files and subfolders inside the currently open folder.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which area in File Explorer shows information about a selected file such as size and date modified?
explanation: The Details Box (Details Pane) at the bottom or side of File Explorer shows metadata about the selected file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the Search Box in File Explorer?
options: To search for files and folders by name or content
explanation: The Search Box allows users to search for files and folders by name or content within the current folder.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which buttons in File Explorer allow you to switch between views such as Large Icons; Details; and List?
explanation: The View Buttons (in the View ribbon/toolbar) let users switch between display modes like Large Icons; Details; and List.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a folder in computer terms?
options: A container used to organise files
explanation: A folder is a container (directory) used to organise and group related files together on a storage device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a file in computer terms?
options: A named collection of data stored on a computer
explanation: A file is a named collection of data (text; images; programs; etc.) stored on a computer's storage medium.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To open a file or folder with a single mouse click in File Explorer (default Windows setting); you must?
options: Single click it (if single-click option is set); otherwise double-click
explanation: By default; Windows requires a double-click to open a file or folder; though single-click can be enabled in settings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which key do you hold while clicking multiple files in File Explorer to select them all at once?
options: Shift (for a range) or Ctrl (for individual)
explanation: Shift+click selects a continuous range; Ctrl+click selects individual non-contiguous files.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens to a deleted file in Windows by default?
options: It is moved to the Recycle Bin
It is sent to the Downloads folder
explanation: When you delete a file in Windows; it is moved to the Recycle Bin where it can be restored or permanently deleted.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the Recycle Bin?
options: A folder on the Desktop where deleted files are temporarily stored
A cleaning program for the hard drive
explanation: The Recycle Bin is a special Desktop folder that holds recently deleted files until they are permanently deleted or restored.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To restore a file from the Recycle Bin; you?
options: Double-click the Recycle Bin and press Ctrl+Z
Open the Recycle Bin; select the file; and click Restore
explanation: Right-clicking a file in the Recycle Bin and choosing Restore (or clicking the Restore button) returns it to its original location.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To permanently delete files from the Recycle Bin; you click?
explanation: 'Empty Recycle Bin' permanently deletes all files stored in it; freeing up hard drive space.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut sends a selected file directly to the Recycle Bin?
explanation: Pressing the Delete key sends the selected file(s) to the Recycle Bin.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To permanently delete a file WITHOUT sending it to the Recycle Bin; you press?
explanation: Shift+Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes the file immediately.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut copies a selected file?
explanation: Ctrl+C copies the selected file(s) to the clipboard.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut cuts (moves) a selected file?
explanation: Ctrl+X cuts the file to the clipboard ready to be pasted (moved) to another location.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut pastes a copied or cut file?
explanation: Ctrl+V pastes the file from the clipboard to the current location.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut undoes the last action in File Explorer?
explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the most recent file operation (e.g. move; rename; delete).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To rename a file in File Explorer; you?
explanation: Right-click → Rename or pressing F2 allows you to rename the selected file or folder.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which key is used to rename a selected file with one key press?
explanation: Pressing F2 with a file selected activates the rename mode for that file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A file extension tells you?
options: The date the file was created
The type of file and which program opens it
explanation: A file extension (e.g. .docx; .jpg; .mp3) identifies the file format and typically determines which application opens it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which file extension is associated with a Microsoft Word document?
explanation: .docx is the extension for Microsoft Word documents (Open XML format).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which file extension is associated with a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet?
explanation: .xlsx is the extension for Microsoft Excel workbooks.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which file extension is associated with a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation?
explanation: .pptx is the extension for Microsoft PowerPoint presentations.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is a valid file name in Windows?
explanation: Windows file names cannot contain / \ : * ? < > | " characters; 'Holiday Photos 2024' is valid.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which character is NOT allowed in a Windows file name?
explanation: The forward slash / (and back slash \) are not allowed in Windows file names as they are path separators.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a file path?
options: The physical cable connecting a storage device
The address that shows the location of a file in the folder hierarchy
explanation: A file path (e.g. C:\Users\Student\Documents\report.docx) shows the exact location of a file in the storage hierarchy.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In the path C:\Users\Student\Documents\report.docx; what is 'Documents'?
explanation: 'Documents' is a folder (directory) in the path hierarchy.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the C: in a Windows file path represent?
explanation: C: refers to the primary hard drive (or its partition) in Windows — typically where the operating system is installed.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When you create a new folder in File Explorer; what name is given to it by default?
explanation: Windows names a newly created folder 'New Folder' by default; ready for the user to rename.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut creates a new folder in File Explorer (Windows 10/11)?
explanation: Ctrl+Shift+N creates a new folder in the current directory in File Explorer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: If you want to move a file from one folder to another; the quickest method using the keyboard is?
options: Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V at the destination
Ctrl+X then Ctrl+V at the destination
explanation: Ctrl+X cuts the file; navigating to the destination and pressing Ctrl+V pastes (moves) it there.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The status bar at the bottom of File Explorer shows?
options: Information about selected items (count; total size)
explanation: The Status Bar shows the number of items selected and their total size.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which view in File Explorer shows the most detail about each file (name; date; size; type)?
explanation: Details view shows files in a list with columns for Name; Date modified; Type; and Size.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which view in File Explorer shows files as large thumbnail previews?
explanation: Large Icons view displays large thumbnail previews of each file — useful for image files.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To sort files by date modified in File Explorer; you click?
options: The 'Date Modified' column header in Details view
explanation: Clicking a column header (e.g. Date Modified; Name; Size) in Details view sorts the files by that attribute.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to find all .jpg image files in her Documents folder. She should type in the Search Box?
explanation: Typing *.jpg in the Search Box uses the wildcard * to match any file name ending in .jpg.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which panel in File Explorer shows a preview of the selected file's contents without opening it?
explanation: The Preview Pane (View → Preview pane) displays a preview of the selected file on the right side.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To select ALL files in a folder at once; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+A (Select All) selects every file and folder in the current directory.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the difference between 'Copy' and 'Cut' when managing files?
options: Copy removes the original; Cut keeps it
Copy keeps the original; Cut removes it from its current location after pasting
explanation: Copy leaves the original in place and creates a duplicate; Cut removes the original once pasted elsewhere.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student empties the Recycle Bin by mistake. Can she recover the deleted files?
options: No; permanently deleted files cannot normally be recovered
explanation: Once the Recycle Bin is emptied; files are permanently deleted and cannot normally be recovered through Windows tools.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which drive letter is usually assigned to a USB flash drive in Windows?
explanation: Windows assigns the next available drive letter (usually D:; E:; etc.) to a USB flash drive when it is plugged in.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the Ribbon in File Explorer?
options: A toolbar at the top providing commands like Copy; Paste; Delete; and New Folder
explanation: The Ribbon (introduced in Windows 8/10 File Explorer) is a tabbed toolbar giving quick access to file management commands.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which is the CORRECT order to copy a file from the Desktop to the Documents folder using keyboard shortcuts?
options: Select file → Ctrl+X → open Documents → Ctrl+V
Select file → Ctrl+C → open Documents → Ctrl+V
Open Documents → Ctrl+C → select file → Ctrl+V
Select file → Ctrl+V → open Documents → Ctrl+C
explanation: The correct sequence is: select the file → Ctrl+C (copy) → navigate to destination → Ctrl+V (paste).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'Properties' option (right-click → Properties) show about a file?
options: Name; type; location; size; creation date and permissions
explanation: The Properties dialog shows full details: name; type; location; size; dates (created; modified; accessed); and permissions.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which part of File Explorer do you type in to go directly to a specific folder location?
explanation: You can type a path directly into the Address Bar and press Enter to navigate to that exact folder.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which icon on the Desktop represents the storage for deleted files?
explanation: The Recycle Bin icon on the Windows Desktop represents the temporary storage for deleted files.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In File Explorer; what does the folder icon with an arrow (shortcut icon) indicate?
options: It is a shortcut that points to a folder or file elsewhere
explanation: A small arrow on an icon indicates it is a shortcut — a link that points to the actual file or folder stored elsewhere.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student saves a file called 'Project.docx' in her Documents folder. What is the FULL path?
explanation: The full path includes the drive; user folder; and each subfolder leading to the file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which file type stores only plain text with no formatting?
explanation: .txt (plain text) files store text without any rich formatting such as fonts; colours; or tables.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'file size' measure?
options: The physical dimensions of the file on paper
The amount of storage space the file uses; measured in KB; MB; or GB
The number of pages in a document
explanation: File size measures how much disk space a file occupies; expressed in kilobytes (KB); megabytes (MB); or gigabytes (GB).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: 1 MB (megabyte) is approximately equal to?
explanation: 1 MB = 1;024 KB; and 1 KB = 1;024 bytes — these are the standard binary storage units.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student's file is 2 MB. Her USB drive has 512 MB free. Can she save the file?
options: Yes; 2 MB is much less than 512 MB
No; USB drives only hold .txt files
Yes; but only if she empties the Recycle Bin first
explanation: 2 MB is much smaller than 512 MB of free space; so the file can easily be saved.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of a file extension?
options: To make the file name longer
To identify the file format and associate it with the correct application
To protect the file with a password
To show the file's creation date
explanation: File extensions (e.g. .docx; .jpg; .mp3) identify the file format so Windows knows which app to use to open it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To navigate UP one folder level in File Explorer; you click?
options: The back arrow or the parent folder name in the Navigation Pane
explanation: The back arrow (or the parent folder in the Navigation Pane / Address Bar breadcrumb) moves you up one level in the folder hierarchy.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens when you try to save a file with a name that already exists in the same folder?
options: An error permanently deletes the old file
Windows asks if you want to replace the existing file
The file is saved with a number added to its name
explanation: Windows prompts the user to confirm whether to replace (overwrite) the existing file with the same name.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Windows folder is the default save location for most documents?
explanation: The Documents folder (inside the user's profile) is the default save location for most applications.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is the LARGEST unit of file storage?
explanation: GB (gigabyte) is larger than MB and KB; and much larger than a single byte.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to organise her class photos into separate folders for each month. She should?
options: Save all photos in one folder and rename them
Create a new folder for each month inside the Pictures folder and move the photos
Use File Explorer search to separate them
explanation: Creating subfolders (one per month) and moving photos into them is the correct way to organise files.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 3; which application is the focus of file management lessons?
explanation: Chapter 3 of Terabytes Book 4 teaches students to manage files and folders using Windows File Explorer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the keyboard shortcut to open File Explorer in Windows 10/11?
explanation: Windows key + E opens File Explorer directly from anywhere in Windows.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student sees the message 'This folder is empty' in the File List Pane. This means?
options: The folder exists but contains no files or subfolders
explanation: The message confirms the folder exists on disk but currently contains no files or subfolders.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command in the Home ribbon quickly creates a new folder in the current location?
explanation: The New Folder button in the Home ribbon (or the shortcut Ctrl+Shift+N) creates a new folder instantly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How do you show hidden files in File Explorer (Windows 10)?
options: File Explorer → View → Hidden Items (check box)
explanation: In File Explorer; go to the View ribbon and check 'Hidden items' to show files and folders marked as hidden.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does it mean if a file icon appears faded/transparent in File Explorer?
explanation: Faded or semi-transparent icons in File Explorer indicate that the file or folder is set as 'Hidden'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which is the correct sequence to move a file from Desktop to Documents using mouse?
options: Drag the file from the Desktop and drop it into the Documents folder in the Navigation Pane
explanation: Dragging and dropping a file from one location to another folder in the Navigation Pane moves (not copies) it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'Details' pane (bottom of File Explorer window) display?
options: The contents of the selected file
Metadata such as dimensions; size; author; and date for the selected file
A list of recently opened files
explanation: The Details pane shows file metadata (properties) like dimensions; size; date created; and author.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the breadcrumb trail in the Address Bar allow you to do?
options: Navigate directly to any parent folder by clicking it
explanation: The breadcrumb trail shows the path as clickable links; letting you jump to any parent folder instantly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: If a student accidentally cuts (Ctrl+X) a file and wants to cancel the operation; she presses?
explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action; restoring the cut file to its original location before it was pasted.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which folder in Windows stores files downloaded from the internet by default?
explanation: The Downloads folder is the default location where browsers and other applications save files downloaded from the internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student creates a folder called 'Science' inside 'School' which is inside 'Documents'. The path is?
explanation: The full path in Windows uses backslashes and follows the hierarchy from drive root to the target folder.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the Navigation Pane's 'Quick Access' section?
options: Shows recently opened and pinned folders for fast access
explanation: Quick Access (at the top of the Navigation Pane) shows frequently used and pinned folders for fast navigation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Book 4 Chapter 3; students learn to manage files on which operating system?
explanation: Terabytes Book 4 is based on Windows 10/11 for all file and application activities.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to send a file to a classmate via email. She should?
options: Attach the file to an email
Copy the file to the Recycle Bin
Print the file and scan it
explanation: Files are shared via email by attaching them to a message; the recipient can then download and open them.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens if a student tries to cut and paste a file to the same folder it is already in?
options: Windows may keep the file in place or ask to replace (no change if same name)
explanation: Pasting a file to the same folder with the same name prompts a Replace dialog; the file effectively stays as is.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which feature of File Explorer lets you search not just by file name but also by content inside files?
options: File content search (using indexed search with 'content:' keyword)
explanation: Windows Search can be set to index file content; allowing searches like 'content:photosynthesis' to find files containing that word.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The file system organises files using a structure shaped like a?
explanation: File systems use a hierarchical (tree) structure with a root at the top and branches of folders and subfolders below.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To quickly see how much free space is left on the C: drive from File Explorer; you?
options: Open each folder and count files
Right-click the C: drive in Navigation Pane → Properties
explanation: Right-click on a drive → Properties shows the total size and free space remaining on that drive.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Save As' do compared to 'Save'?
options: They do exactly the same thing
Save As allows you to save a copy with a new name; type; or location
explanation: Save overwrites the existing file; Save As lets you save a copy under a new name; in a different format; or to a different location.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4; Chapter 3 introduces students to the concept of?
options: Managing files and folders using File Explorer
explanation: Chapter 3 of Terabytes Book 4 is dedicated to file management: creating; copying; moving; renaming; and deleting files using File Explorer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is a hidden system folder in Windows that students should NOT delete?
explanation: The C:\Windows folder contains core operating system files — deleting it would break Windows.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which action is performed when a file is 'archived'?
options: The file is compressed and stored for long-term backup
The file is sent to the Recycle Bin
explanation: Archiving compresses and stores files (e.g. in a .zip) for backup or space saving; they are not deleted.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What type of file is a .zip file?
options: A compressed archive containing one or more files
explanation: A .zip file is a compressed archive that can contain multiple files and/or folders; saving storage space.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student accidentally deletes a folder. The FIRST thing she should try is?
explanation: Ctrl+Z immediately undoes the last action in File Explorer; including accidental deletions.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the maximum number of characters allowed in a Windows 10/11 file name (standard path)?
options: 255 characters (filename); up to 260 for the full path
explanation: Windows supports file names up to 255 characters and full paths up to 260 characters (extendable with long-path support).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following best describes a 'shortcut' on the Windows Desktop?
options: A link (alias) that points to the original file or application
explanation: A shortcut is a small link file that points to the original program; file; or folder — it is NOT the actual file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In File Explorer; what does the 'Refresh' button (or F5) do?
options: Updates the file list to show the most current contents
explanation: Pressing F5 or clicking Refresh reloads the current folder view to show any newly added or changed files.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following file extensions indicates an image file?
explanation: .jpg (JPEG) is a common image format; .docx is Word; .mp3 is audio; .exe is a program.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the Desktop in Windows?
options: The physical surface of the table where the computer sits
The main screen you see after logging in to Windows
explanation: The Desktop is the main working area of the Windows screen that appears after you log in.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a wallpaper in Windows?
options: A physical sticker on the computer
The background image displayed on the Desktop
explanation: Wallpaper (or desktop background) is the image or colour displayed as the background of the Windows Desktop.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a screensaver?
options: An image that protects the monitor when the computer is idle
The background image of the Desktop
explanation: A screensaver is an animated image or pattern that appears on screen when the computer has been idle for a set time; originally to prevent screen burn-in.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a GUI?
options: Graphical User Interface — a visual way to interact with a computer
explanation: GUI (Graphical User Interface) lets users interact with computers using visual elements like icons; windows; and menus.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is an example of a GUI operating system?
explanation: Windows 10/11 uses a GUI with icons; windows; and menus — unlike command-line interfaces.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Small pictures on the Desktop that represent programs; files; or folders are called?
explanation: Icons are small graphical images on the Desktop (and elsewhere in Windows) that represent applications; files; or folders.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Where is the Taskbar located by default in Windows?
options: At the top of the screen
In the centre of the screen
At the bottom of the screen
explanation: By default; the Windows Taskbar appears at the bottom of the screen; containing the Start button; open apps; and system tray.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Start button in Windows open?
explanation: Clicking the Start button (Windows logo) opens the Start Menu where you can access apps; settings; and power options.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The area at the bottom-right of the Taskbar that shows the clock; volume; and notifications is called?
explanation: The System Tray (Notification Area) at the far right of the Taskbar shows the clock; battery; Wi-Fi; volume; and app notifications.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the Desktop wallpaper in Windows 10/11; you right-click the Desktop and choose?
explanation: Right-clicking the Desktop and selecting 'Personalise' opens the Personalisation settings where wallpaper can be changed.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Windows Settings category contains options for Wallpaper; Colours; and Screensaver?
explanation: Personalisation settings (Settings → Personalisation) contain options for background; colours; lock screen; screensaver; and themes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Where do you change the screensaver settings in Windows 10/11?
options: Settings → Personalisation → Lock Screen → Screen saver settings
explanation: Screensaver settings are found under Settings → Personalisation → Lock Screen → Screen saver settings link.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student sets a 5-minute wait time for the screensaver. This means the screensaver starts after?
options: The computer is turned on for 5 minutes
explanation: The wait time is the period of user inactivity after which the screensaver activates.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a screensaver today?
options: To prevent screen burn-in on old CRT monitors and add privacy/aesthetics
explanation: Modern screensavers are mostly aesthetic/privacy features; originally they protected CRT monitors from burn-in.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a theme in Windows Desktop settings?
options: A pre-set combination of wallpaper; colours; sounds; and screensaver
explanation: A Windows theme bundles wallpaper; colour scheme; sounds; and screensaver settings into a single named package.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of a window in a GUI?
options: To display a web page only
A rectangular area on screen where a program's content is displayed
A physical component of the monitor
explanation: In a GUI; a window is the rectangular frame in which a program runs and displays its content.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Minimise button do in a window?
options: Shrinks the window to the Taskbar (hidden but still running)
explanation: Minimise (–) hides the window from view; the program continues running and its button appears in the Taskbar.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Maximise button do in a window?
options: Expands the window to fill the entire screen
Moves the window to the Taskbar
explanation: Maximise (□) expands the window to fill the entire screen; when maximised it changes to a Restore button.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Close button (X) do in a window?
options: Closes (exits) the window and its program
explanation: The Close (X) button exits the program and closes its window entirely.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The three buttons at the top-right of most Windows windows are (in order)?
explanation: The three window control buttons are always Minimise (–); Maximise/Restore (□); and Close (X).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To move a window to a different position on screen; you?
options: Drag the title bar of the window
explanation: You can reposition a window by clicking and dragging its title bar to any location on the screen.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To resize a window; you hover over its edge or corner until the cursor becomes a double-headed arrow; then?
explanation: When the resize cursor appears at the edge/corner of a window; clicking and dragging resizes it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Right-clicking an icon on the Desktop shows?
options: A context menu (shortcut menu) with options like Open; Delete; Rename
explanation: Right-clicking an icon opens a context menu with relevant options such as Open; Run as Administrator; Delete; Rename; and Properties.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How do you create a new shortcut on the Desktop to a program?
options: Copy the entire program files to the Desktop
Right-click Desktop → New → Shortcut; then choose the target program
Drag the program from the hard drive
explanation: Right-click → New → Shortcut opens a wizard to create a Desktop shortcut linking to any program or file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To arrange Desktop icons automatically into a neat grid; you right-click the Desktop and choose?
explanation: Right-click Desktop → View → 'Auto arrange icons' snaps all icons into an ordered grid layout.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut shows the Desktop by minimising all open windows?
explanation: Windows key + D minimises (or restores) all open windows to show the Desktop instantly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does Alt+Tab do in Windows?
explanation: Alt+Tab displays a thumbnail switcher; holding Alt and pressing Tab repeatedly cycles through open windows.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Task Manager?
options: Ctrl+Alt+Delete (then choose Task Manager) or Ctrl+Shift+Esc
explanation: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager directly; Ctrl+Alt+Delete shows a menu from which Task Manager can be opened.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What information does the Taskbar show?
options: Currently open windows/apps; pinned programs; Start button; system tray
explanation: The Taskbar shows the Start button; pinned apps; currently open windows; and the system tray with clock and notifications.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student has 5 windows open but can only see 3. How does she switch to the others without closing anything?
options: Use Alt+Tab or click their buttons in the Taskbar
explanation: Alt+Tab or clicking the program's button in the Taskbar switches to any open window without closing the others.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which screen resolution setting provides SHARPER; more detailed images on a modern monitor?
options: The resolution has no effect on sharpness
explanation: Higher screen resolution (more pixels) produces a sharper; more detailed image on the same size screen.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Where do you change screen resolution in Windows 10/11?
explanation: Screen resolution is changed under Settings → System → Display; scroll down to Display resolution.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Notification Centre (Action Centre) in Windows 10/11 do?
options: Displays notifications from apps and provides quick settings (Wi-Fi; Bluetooth; etc.)
explanation: The Action Centre (notification bell icon in Taskbar) collects app notifications and provides quick toggle buttons for Wi-Fi; Bluetooth; Night Light; etc.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The clock on the Taskbar displays the current?
explanation: The Taskbar clock typically shows the current time and; on hover or click; also shows the full date.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Where is the Recycle Bin icon typically found on the Windows Desktop?
options: At the bottom-right of the Taskbar
explanation: The Recycle Bin icon is placed on the Desktop by default for easy access to deleted files.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To pin a program to the Taskbar for quick access; you?
options: Drag the program to the Start Menu
Right-click the program in the Start Menu or Taskbar → Pin to Taskbar
Copy the program to the Desktop
explanation: Right-clicking a running program's Taskbar button or Start Menu tile and choosing 'Pin to Taskbar' keeps it there permanently.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The term 'window' in computing refers to?
options: A physical window in the building
A rectangular area on screen displaying a program's interface
explanation: A window is the rectangular on-screen frame within which an application or dialog runs.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Multiple windows can be arranged side by side using the Windows Snap feature. To snap a window to the LEFT half; you press?
