explanation: Windows key + Left arrow snaps the active window to the left half of the screen.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Windows feature lets you create multiple virtual Desktops (Task Views)?
explanation: Task View (Windows key + Tab) lets you create and manage multiple virtual desktops; each with its own set of windows.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the Desktop's 'Recycle Bin' icon on the Desktop?
options: To provide easy access to deleted files that can still be restored
explanation: The Recycle Bin icon gives easy access to recently deleted files; which can be restored or permanently removed from there.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Personalisation settings in Windows allow students to customise which of the following?
options: Background wallpaper; colour accents; and screensaver
explanation: Personalisation covers visual settings: background image; colour scheme; lock screen; screensaver; fonts; and themes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The wallpaper can be set to display a picture in which modes? (Select the MOST complete answer)
options: Fill; Fit; Stretch; Tile; Centre; Span
explanation: Windows offers Fill; Fit; Stretch; Tile; Centre; and Span modes for displaying the desktop background image.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To open Settings in Windows 10/11 quickly; you press?
explanation: Windows key + I opens the Settings app directly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Colours' under Personalisation in Windows 10/11 control?
options: The accent colour used for Start Menu; Taskbar; and window borders
explanation: The Colours setting in Personalisation lets users choose an accent colour applied to the Start Menu; Taskbar; and window title bars.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants a photo of her family as her Desktop background. She should go to?
explanation: Settings → Personalisation → Background → Browse lets the user select any image file as the desktop wallpaper.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: On a computer screen; the area NOT covered by the Taskbar is called the?
explanation: The area of the screen above the Taskbar is the Desktop working area where windows open and icons are placed.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: An 'icon' on the Desktop that opens a program is called a?
explanation: Desktop icons represent programs; files; or shortcuts; double-clicking them opens the corresponding application or file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What feature in Windows 10/11 allows the screen to dim and prevent disturbing others at night?
options: Night Light (reduces blue light for night viewing)
explanation: Night Light (Settings → System → Display → Night Light) reduces the screen's blue-light output for more comfortable evening viewing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut locks the Windows Desktop immediately?
explanation: Windows key + L immediately locks the computer; requiring the password to unlock — useful for quick privacy.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which button at the top-right of a window RESTORES it from maximised to its previous size?
explanation: When a window is maximised; the Maximise button changes to a Restore Down button (two overlapping squares) to return the window to its previous size.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 4; students learn to customise the Desktop. The two main cosmetic features covered are?
explanation: Chapter 4 of Terabytes Book 4 focuses on customising the Desktop wallpaper and screensaver.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Dark Mode' do in Windows 10/11?
options: Changes the colour scheme of Windows apps to dark backgrounds with light text
explanation: Dark Mode switches supported apps and Windows chrome to a dark colour scheme; reducing eye strain in low-light environments.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The Start Menu in Windows 10/11 can be opened using which key on the keyboard?
explanation: Pressing the Windows logo key on the keyboard opens the Start Menu (same as clicking the Start button).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to change the colour of the Taskbar to blue. She should go to?
explanation: Settings → Personalisation → Colours lets users choose an accent colour that is applied to the Taskbar and other Windows elements.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a 'widget' in the context of the Windows Desktop?
options: A miniature app displaying information (weather; news; calendar) directly on the Desktop
explanation: Widgets are small interactive apps pinned to the Desktop (or Windows 11 Widgets panel) showing live info like weather or news.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The Windows Desktop is managed by a process called?
explanation: Explorer.exe is the Windows shell process that manages the Desktop; Taskbar; and File Explorer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is TRUE about the Windows Taskbar?
options: It can only be placed at the bottom of the screen
It can be moved to the top; left; or right of the screen
It always shows all running programs
explanation: The Windows Taskbar can be repositioned to the top; left; right; or bottom of the screen by right-clicking it and changing Taskbar settings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Lock screen' in Windows settings control?
options: The physical lock on the computer
The image and information displayed when the computer is locked or at the login screen
explanation: Lock screen settings (Settings → Personalisation → Lock screen) control the image and apps shown on the lock/login screen.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: If a student cannot find her Desktop icons because windows are covering them; she should?
options: Press Windows key + D to show the Desktop
Open a new File Explorer window
explanation: Windows key + D instantly minimises all windows to reveal the Desktop.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Personalisation option allows a student to download and apply a new Desktop theme?
options: Background → Themes → Get more themes online
explanation: In Settings → Personalisation; under Themes; there is a link to 'Get more themes in Microsoft Store' to download additional themes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The Desktop background can be set to a solid colour instead of an image. Where is this done?
options: Settings → Personalisation → Background → Background dropdown → Solid colour
explanation: In Settings → Personalisation → Background; changing the Background dropdown from 'Picture' to 'Solid colour' allows choosing a plain colour background.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Windows feature automatically adjusts the Desktop layout when multiple monitors are connected?
explanation: Settings → System → Display shows all connected monitors and allows configuring their arrangement; resolution; and display mode.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does it mean when an icon on the Taskbar has a dot or glow underneath it?
options: The app is pinned but not running
The app is currently open and running
explanation: A dot or highlight indicator under a Taskbar icon means that application is currently open and running.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Windows 10/11; which search feature lets you find files; apps; and settings from the Taskbar?
explanation: The Search bar (or magnifying glass icon) in the Windows 10/11 Taskbar lets you search for files; apps; and settings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The Personalisation option 'Font' in Settings → Personalisation → Fonts allows you to?
options: Change the system-wide default font for all apps
Only change the font in Notepad
Add or remove font families installed on the computer
explanation: Settings → Personalisation → Fonts shows all installed fonts and allows installing new ones by dragging font files into the window.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What keyboard shortcut is used to take a screenshot of the entire screen in Windows?
explanation: Pressing the Print Screen (PrtSc) key captures the entire screen to the clipboard; ready to be pasted.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Windows key + Print Screen automatically saves a screenshot to which folder?
explanation: Windows key + PrtSc captures the entire screen AND saves it automatically as a file in Pictures → Screenshots.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Windows 10/11 feature shows all running apps and allows you to switch between virtual desktops?
explanation: Task View (Windows key + Tab) shows thumbnails of all open windows and lets you switch between virtual desktops.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does right-clicking the Desktop and choosing 'Display Settings' let you change?
explanation: Right-click → Display Settings opens Settings → System → Display where resolution; orientation; and multi-monitor options are found.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student sets her screensaver to 'On resume; display logon screen'. This means?
options: After the screensaver starts; she must enter a password to get back to the Desktop
explanation: 'On resume; display logon screen' requires the user to log in after the screensaver activates; providing security when away.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4; the chapter on the Desktop teaches students that a GUI makes computers?
options: Easier to use because actions are performed with pictures and clicks rather than typed commands
explanation: A GUI makes computers more accessible and user-friendly because users interact with visual elements rather than memorising commands.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which part of the Windows screen shows the names and buttons for currently open applications?
explanation: The Taskbar displays a button for each open application; allowing quick switching between them.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens when you double-click an icon on the Desktop?
options: It opens the associated file; folder; or application
explanation: Double-clicking a Desktop icon opens the program; file; or folder it represents.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How can a student remove an icon she no longer wants from the Desktop?
explanation: Right-clicking a Desktop icon and choosing Delete removes the shortcut (or file) from the Desktop.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Taskbar's 'Show Desktop' button (far-right edge) do when clicked?
options: Minimises all windows to reveal the Desktop
explanation: Clicking the thin 'Show Desktop' strip at the far right of the Taskbar minimises all open windows.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Book 4 chapter teaches students about the Windows Desktop and customisation?
explanation: Chapter 4 of Terabytes Book 4 focuses on the Windows Desktop; including wallpaper; screensaver; GUI concepts; and icons.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student notices that clicking the same icon on the Taskbar while the window is open minimises the window. This is because clicking an already-active Taskbar button?
options: Toggles the window between open (visible) and minimised
explanation: Clicking a Taskbar button for an already active application toggles it between its visible state and minimised.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Windows key (Windows logo key) do on the keyboard?
explanation: Pressing the Windows logo key opens the Start Menu; pressing it again closes it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the size of Desktop icons; you right-click the Desktop and choose?
options: View → Large icons / Medium icons / Small icons
explanation: Right-click Desktop → View gives options for Large icons; Medium icons; and Small icons to resize Desktop icons.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the notification area also known as?
explanation: The Notification Area is also called the System Tray; it shows background app icons; clock; and status indicators.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student drags the Taskbar to the top of the screen. To move it back; she must?
options: Unlock the Taskbar; drag it back to the bottom; re-lock
explanation: The Taskbar can be moved by right-clicking → Taskbar settings → Taskbar location on screen; or by unlocking and dragging.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following screen elements is ALWAYS visible on the Windows Desktop (cannot be minimised)?
explanation: The Taskbar is always visible at the edge of the screen (unless hidden via auto-hide setting).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Book 4 Chapter 4 introduces the concept of GUI. What does the 'G' in GUI stand for?
explanation: GUI = Graphical User Interface; the G stands for Graphical.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of these is the CORRECT sequence to change the wallpaper in Windows 10/11?
options: Right-click Desktop → Personalise → Background → Choose photo
File Explorer → Pictures → Set as Wallpaper option
explanation: Right-click Desktop → Personalise (or Settings → Personalisation → Background) → Browse for image is the standard path.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What type of image format is MOST commonly used for Desktop wallpapers in Windows?
explanation: JPG and PNG are image formats; both are widely used for Desktop wallpapers.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Windows 10/11 a 'Live Tile' on the Start Menu is?
options: A physical tile on the keyboard
A Start Menu app icon that updates dynamically to show current information
explanation: Live Tiles are animated Start Menu icons that display real-time info (e.g. news headlines; calendar events) without opening the app.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which shortcut switches between open windows/apps without using the Taskbar?
explanation: Alt+Tab cycles through open windows using a thumbnail switcher overlay.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the default name for the user folder that appears in the Desktop's Navigation Pane (File Explorer)?
explanation: The user folder in File Explorer is named after the account's username; containing Documents; Pictures; Downloads; etc.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following tasks can be done via the Desktop in Windows 10/11?
options: Changing the wallpaper; launching apps; and managing files
explanation: From the Desktop; users can launch apps; customise appearance; access files; and manage shortcuts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Book 4 Chapter 4; what does the term 'personalise' mean in the context of the Desktop?
options: Customising the Desktop appearance (wallpaper; screensaver; colours) to suit the user's preferences
explanation: Personalising the Desktop means customising its visual appearance — background; colours; screensaver — to reflect the user's preferences.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student's screensaver is set to 'Blank'. When the screensaver activates; what does the user see?
explanation: The 'Blank' screensaver simply turns the screen black; the simplest way to save energy and add privacy.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does increasing the screen brightness in Windows Display Settings do?
options: Makes the screen emit more light (appears brighter)
explanation: Screen brightness controls how much light the display emits; higher brightness makes the screen look lighter.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Windows 10/11 accessibility feature enlarges a portion of the screen?
explanation: Magnifier (Accessibility → Magnifier in Settings; or Windows key + +) zooms in on part of the screen.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the 'Search' bar in the Windows 10/11 Taskbar?
options: To find files; apps; settings; and web results from a single search box
To search only the Documents folder
explanation: The Taskbar Search bar provides unified search across installed apps; files; settings; and the web.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student notices that clicking the Desktop background (with no windows open) and pressing Ctrl+A selects all the Desktop icons. Why?
options: The Desktop is treated as a folder by Windows
Ctrl+A has no effect on the Desktop
explanation: The Windows Desktop behaves like an ordinary folder; Ctrl+A (Select All) works here just as in File Explorer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the default font in Microsoft Word 2016?
explanation: Calibri is the default body font in Microsoft Word 2016 and later versions.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which tab in Microsoft Word contains the Font and Paragraph formatting groups?
explanation: The Home tab in Word contains the Font group (font; size; bold; italic; etc.) and the Paragraph group (alignment; lists; etc.).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To make selected text BOLD in Microsoft Word; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+B toggles Bold formatting on and off for the selected text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To make selected text ITALIC in Microsoft Word; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+I toggles Italic formatting for the selected text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To UNDERLINE selected text in Microsoft Word; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+U toggles Underline formatting for the selected text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which formatting makes text appear as a smaller character ABOVE the baseline?
explanation: Superscript raises text above the baseline and reduces its size; used for exponents (e.g. x²) and footnotes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which formatting makes text appear as a smaller character BELOW the baseline?
explanation: Subscript lowers text below the baseline; used for chemical formulas (e.g. H₂O).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which formatting draws a horizontal line through the middle of the text?
explanation: Strikethrough draws a line through the selected text; often used to show deleted or crossed-out content.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does BOLD formatting do to text?
options: Makes it thicker/heavier so it stands out
explanation: Bold increases the stroke weight of the text; making it appear heavier and more prominent.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does ITALIC formatting do to text?
options: Slants the text to the right
explanation: Italic formatting slants the text to the right; it is used for titles; emphasis; or foreign words.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the font SIZE control?
options: The height of the characters in points
explanation: Font size (measured in points; pt) controls how tall the characters are — larger numbers mean larger text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the unit used to measure font size?
explanation: Font size is measured in points (pt); where 1 point = 1/72 of an inch.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To increase the font size of selected text by 1 point; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+Shift+> increases the font size of selected text by one step (or by 1pt increment in some versions).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the font colour of selected text; you click?
options: The Font Color button (A with coloured underline) in the Home tab
explanation: The Font Color button (a letter A with a coloured bar underneath) in the Home → Font group changes text colour.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which change case option in Word capitalises the FIRST letter of EVERY word?
explanation: Capitalize Each Word (Title Case) makes the first letter of every word capital; e.g. 'The Quick Brown Fox'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which change case option converts all letters to CAPITALS?
explanation: UPPERCASE converts all selected letters to capital (upper-case) letters.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which change case option converts all letters to small letters?
explanation: lowercase converts all selected letters to small (lower-case) letters.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which change case option capitalises only the FIRST letter of the first word in a sentence?
explanation: Sentence case capitalises only the first letter of the first word; like normal sentence writing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which change case option REVERSES the capitalisation (capitals become small; small become capital)?
explanation: tOGGLE cASE inverts the case of every letter in the selection.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is TEXT ALIGNMENT?
options: The colour scheme of the document
The position of text relative to the left and right margins
The number of columns in a document
explanation: Text alignment sets how text is positioned horizontally between the left and right margins of the document.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which alignment option lines text up along the LEFT margin?
explanation: Left Align (Ctrl+L) aligns text against the left margin; the right edge is ragged — this is the default.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which alignment option places text in the MIDDLE between the left and right margins?
explanation: Centre alignment (Ctrl+E) places each line of text centred between the left and right margins.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which alignment option lines text up along the RIGHT margin?
explanation: Right Align (Ctrl+R) aligns text against the right margin; the left edge is ragged.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which alignment option makes both the left AND right edges of text perfectly straight?
explanation: Justify (Ctrl+J) stretches each line to align with both margins; giving a newspaper-column appearance.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut centres selected text?
explanation: Ctrl+E centres the selected text between the left and right margins.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a bulleted list used for?
options: To list items that do NOT have a specific order; each marked with a bullet symbol
explanation: Bulleted lists display unordered items — each preceded by a bullet symbol — where order does not matter.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a numbered list used for?
options: To list items in no particular order
To show items in a specific sequence or order; numbered 1; 2; 3; etc.
explanation: Numbered (ordered) lists present items in a sequence where the order matters; numbered 1; 2; 3 (or letters/Roman numerals).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To create a new bullet point on the next line in a Word list; you press?
explanation: Pressing Enter at the end of a bulleted or numbered line creates a new list item on the next line.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To end a bulleted list and return to normal text; you press?
options: Enter twice (or click the Bullet button to toggle it off)
explanation: Pressing Enter twice (or clicking the Bullet/Numbering button to deactivate it) ends the list and returns to normal paragraph text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the HIGHLIGHT colour tool do in Word?
options: Applies a coloured background behind selected text (like a highlighter pen)
explanation: Highlighting applies a coloured background to text; simulating the effect of a physical highlighter pen.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Microsoft Word; the 'Clear All Formatting' button removes?
options: All character formatting (font; size; bold; italic; colour) from selected text; returning it to default
explanation: Clear All Formatting resets selected text to the default Normal style; removing all manual font and paragraph formatting.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To select ALL text in a Word document quickly; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+A (Select All) selects all the text and objects in the document at once.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the Format Painter button do in Word?
options: Copies the formatting of selected text and applies it to another section
explanation: Format Painter copies formatting (font; size; colour; style) from one text selection and applies it to another.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The keyboard shortcut to UNDO the last action in Word is?
explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the most recent action in Word (and most other applications).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The keyboard shortcut to REDO a previously undone action in Word is?
explanation: Ctrl+Y redoes an action that was undone with Ctrl+Z.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To SAVE a document in Word; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+S saves the current document; if it has not been saved before it opens the Save As dialog.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To PRINT a document in Word; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+P opens the Print dialog in Word.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To OPEN an existing document in Word; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+O opens the Open dialog to browse for and open an existing file.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To create a NEW document in Word; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+N creates a new blank document.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is LINE SPACING?
options: The vertical distance between lines of text in a paragraph
explanation: Line spacing controls the vertical space between lines of text in a paragraph (e.g. single; 1.5; double).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which command in Word shows or hides non-printing characters (paragraph marks; spaces)?
explanation: The ¶ (Pilcrow) button or Ctrl+Shift+8 toggles the display of non-printing formatting marks like paragraph returns and spaces.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Word; Font size 12pt is considered?
explanation: 12pt is widely used as the standard body text size; 11pt (Calibri 11) is actually Word's default but 12pt is considered standard.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does SUBSCRIPT look like compared to normal text?
explanation: Subscript characters appear below the normal text baseline; e.g. the '2' in H₂O.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does SUPERSCRIPT look like compared to normal text?
explanation: Superscript characters appear above the normal text baseline; e.g. the '2' in x².
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The shortcut to apply Superscript in Word is?
explanation: Ctrl+Shift+= (Ctrl+Shift+Plus) applies Superscript formatting in Word.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The shortcut to apply Subscript in Word is?
explanation: Ctrl+= applies Subscript formatting in Word.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the FONT in word processing?
options: The style/design of the characters (typeface); e.g. Calibri; Arial; Times New Roman
explanation: A font is a complete set of characters in a specific typeface design; e.g. Calibri; Arial; or Times New Roman.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the font of selected text in Word; you click?
options: The Font name dropdown in the Home tab
explanation: The Font name dropdown box in the Home tab allows selecting any installed font to apply to selected text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Paragraph Spacing' control?
options: The space before or after an entire paragraph
The line height within a paragraph
explanation: Paragraph spacing adds extra space before or after paragraphs; different from line spacing which is within a paragraph.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which group in the Home tab contains Bold; Italic; Underline; Font; and Font Size?
explanation: The Font group in the Home tab contains all character-level formatting tools: font; size; bold; italic; underline; colour; etc.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To indent the first line of a paragraph in Word; you press?
options: Tab key at the start of the paragraph
explanation: Pressing Tab at the beginning of a paragraph indents the first line (adds a standard indent).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the Styles Gallery in Word?
options: To apply pre-designed sets of formatting to headings; body text; etc. with one click
explanation: The Styles Gallery (Home tab) provides pre-designed formatting combinations (Heading 1; Normal; Bold; etc.) for consistent document appearance.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'Normal' style in Word represent?
options: The default body text formatting (usually Calibri 11pt)
explanation: The Normal style is the default paragraph style for body text in Word; set to Calibri 11pt by default in Word 2016.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which button in the Paragraph group sets text to a bulleted list?
explanation: The Bullets button (a bullet point icon) in the Home → Paragraph group creates a bulleted (unordered) list.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens when you press Tab inside a numbered list in Word?
options: Increases the indent level; creating a sub-list
explanation: Pressing Tab in a list item demotes it to a sub-level; creating a nested (indented) list.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To copy selected text to another location in Word; the correct keyboard sequence is?
explanation: Ctrl+C copies; navigate to destination; Ctrl+V pastes — the original text is kept.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To MOVE selected text to another location in Word; the correct keyboard sequence is?
explanation: Ctrl+X cuts the text from its current position; navigate to the new location; Ctrl+V pastes it there.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the FIND function (Ctrl+F) do in Word?
options: Locates specific text within the document
explanation: Ctrl+F opens the Find toolbar/dialog in Word to search for specific words or phrases in the document.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does REPLACE (Ctrl+H) do in Word?
options: Finds a specific word and replaces it with another
explanation: Ctrl+H opens Find & Replace; which lets you search for text and automatically substitute it with different text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Word; the RULER at the top of the page is used to?
options: Set indents; tab stops; and margins
explanation: The horizontal Ruler in Word displays indent markers and tab stops; allowing users to adjust paragraph indents and column widths.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is 'Justification' in text formatting?
options: Aligning text so both the left and right edges are straight (like newspaper columns)
explanation: Justified text (Ctrl+J) spreads words so both the left and right edges of each line align with the margins.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To remove Bold from already-bold selected text in Word; you?
explanation: Formatting buttons (Bold; Italic; Underline) in Word are toggles — pressing the shortcut again removes the formatting.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'character spacing' control in Word's Font dialog?
options: The space between individual characters (letters) within text
explanation: Character spacing (Expanded/Condensed in Font → Advanced) adjusts the horizontal space between individual letters.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does text 'Highlighting' in yellow achieve?
options: Applies a yellow background behind the text to draw attention
explanation: Text highlighting in yellow (or other colours) applies a coloured background to the selected text; drawing visual attention to it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the shortcut key to open the Font dialog box in Word?
explanation: Ctrl+D (or Ctrl+Shift+F) opens the Font dialog box giving access to all font and character formatting options.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which tab in the Font dialog box controls Superscript; Subscript; Strikethrough; and Shadow?
explanation: The main Font tab in the Font dialog contains Superscript; Subscript; Strikethrough; Shadow; Outline; and other effects.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student has typed text in UPPERCASE and wants to change it to Sentence case WITHOUT retyping. She uses?
options: Change Case dropdown (in Home tab → Font group)
explanation: Home → Font group → Change Case dropdown (Aa button) offers Sentence case; lowercase; UPPERCASE; Capitalize Each Word; and tOGGLE cASE.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'Aa' button in Word's Font group open?
explanation: The Aa button in the Home → Font group opens the Change Case dropdown with five case options.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is INDENTATION in Word?
options: The left or right margin added to a paragraph to offset it from the page margin
explanation: Indentation adds space between a paragraph and the page margin; commonly used for quotes or list items.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student types '2nd' and notices the 'nd' becomes superscript automatically. This is because of?
options: AutoCorrect / AutoFormat As You Type in Word
explanation: Word's AutoFormat As You Type feature automatically applies Superscript to ordinal suffixes like 1st; 2nd; 3rd.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
explanation: Ctrl+U is the correct shortcut for Underline; Ctrl+B is Bold; Ctrl+I is Italic.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Line Spacing' set to '2.0' mean?
options: Lines are double-spaced (twice the normal single-line space)
explanation: Line Spacing 2.0 (double spacing) inserts a full blank line's space between each line of text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To make text stand out as important in a Word document; which three formatting options are MOST commonly used together?
explanation: Bold; Italic; and Underline are the three most common emphasis formatting options available in the Home → Font group.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'Format Painter' cursor look like when active?
options: A paint brush (cursor with a paintbrush icon)
explanation: When Format Painter is active; the cursor changes to include a small paintbrush icon next to the standard pointer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Book 4 Chapter 5; the textbook teaches students to format text in Microsoft Word. The default font introduced is?
explanation: Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 5 identifies Calibri as the default font in Microsoft Word 2016.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What colour is the default text in Microsoft Word?
explanation: The default text colour in Word is Black (Automatic); meaning it matches the document's colour theme automatically.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The keyboard shortcut to change text to ALL CAPS in Word (toggle) is?
explanation: Ctrl+Shift+A toggles ALL CAPS formatting on and off for the selected text (different from pressing Caps Lock).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of a 'style' in Word?
options: To change the colour of the page
A named set of formatting that can be applied with one click to create consistent document formatting
To insert a table of contents automatically
explanation: A Word style is a saved combination of formatting (font; size; colour; spacing) with a name; applied in one click for consistency.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which tab would you use to insert a picture into a Word document?
explanation: The Insert tab in Word contains commands for inserting images; tables; shapes; SmartArt; and other objects.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following changes font size the fastest using the Quick Access Toolbar or Ribbon?
options: The Font Size box in the Home tab (click and type the size)
explanation: The Font Size box in the Home tab lets you directly type or select the desired size — the fastest method.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants the heading to stand out from the body text. She should?
options: Increase the font size; make it bold; and possibly use a different font
Use the same font and size as body text
explanation: Headings are typically distinguished by larger font size; bold weight; and sometimes a contrasting font style.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Word; paragraph alignment options are found in which group on the Home tab?
explanation: The Paragraph group in the Home tab contains alignment buttons (Left; Centre; Right; Justify) and list and indentation controls.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student highlights some text and presses Ctrl+B; Ctrl+I; and Ctrl+U. What does the text look like?
explanation: Each shortcut applies its formatting independently; so the text ends up Bold AND Italic AND Underlined.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the UNDO button look like in Word's Quick Access Toolbar?
explanation: The Undo button is a curved anti-clockwise arrow in the Quick Access Toolbar at the top-left of Word.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4; students learn that pressing ENTER in Word?
options: Ends the current paragraph and starts a new one
explanation: Pressing Enter (Return) ends the current paragraph and moves the cursor to the start of a new paragraph.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Word Wrap' mean?
options: The text wraps around an image
Text automatically moves to the next line when it reaches the right margin
The document is saved as a ZIP file
explanation: Word Wrap automatically continues text on the next line when it reaches the right margin; so the user never needs to press Enter at the end of a line.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut selects an entire word in Word when the cursor is inside it?
explanation: Double-clicking a word in Word selects the entire word instantly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To remove all bold; italic; and font colour from a selection at once; you click?
options: The Clear All Formatting button (eraser icon) in the Home → Font group
Bold; Italic; and Font Color each separately
explanation: Clear All Formatting (the letter A with an eraser icon) removes all manual character formatting and returns the text to the default Normal style.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the keyboard shortcut to open Print Preview / Print in Word?
explanation: Ctrl+P opens the Print pane (which includes a print preview) in Word 2016 and later.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the font size to EXACTLY 18pt; the quickest way is?
options: Click the Increase Font Size button 18 times
Click the Font Size box; type 18; press Enter
Open the Font dialog; scroll to 18
explanation: Click the Font Size box in the Home tab; type 18; and press Enter to set the size to exactly 18pt.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of text formatting in a Word document?
options: To make the document visually clear; organised; and appropriate for its purpose
explanation: Text formatting improves clarity; emphasis; and professional appearance; making the document easier to read and understand.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To insert a Shape in Microsoft Word; you go to?
explanation: Shapes are inserted via the Insert tab → Illustrations group → Shapes dropdown in Word 2016.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Word; a Shape's FILL colour is?
options: The colour of the shape's border
The colour of the text inside
The background colour of the page
explanation: Shape Fill is the colour or gradient that fills the interior of the shape.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Word; a Shape's OUTLINE (border) colour refers to?
options: The colour of the line forming the shape's border
explanation: Shape Outline controls the colour; weight; and style of the line that forms the shape's border.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change a Shape's fill colour in Word; you right-click the shape and choose?
explanation: Right-click → Format Shape (or Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Styles) gives access to fill; outline; and effects settings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is SmartArt in Microsoft Word?
options: Pre-designed graphical diagrams for presenting information visually (e.g. lists; processes; cycles)
explanation: SmartArt provides ready-made diagrams (lists; processes; hierarchies; etc.) that automatically adjust when text is added.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To insert SmartArt in Word; you go to?
explanation: SmartArt is found under Insert → Illustrations → SmartArt in Word 2016.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category would you choose to show steps in a process (e.g. steps to make tea)?
explanation: The Process category in SmartArt contains diagrams designed to show sequential steps or stages in a process.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category would you choose to show an organisational chart (who reports to whom)?
explanation: The Hierarchy category contains org chart and tree-structure diagrams showing reporting relationships.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category would you choose to show repeating stages in a loop (e.g. seasons)?
explanation: The Cycle category shows circular or continuous processes where stages repeat.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category is best for a simple bulleted list of items?
explanation: The List category contains SmartArt diagrams designed to display lists of items clearly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category shows the relationship between parts (e.g. overlapping circles)?
explanation: The Relationship category includes Venn diagrams and other diagrams that show how items connect or relate.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category shows proportional relationships in a triangular shape?
explanation: The Pyramid category shows proportional; foundational; or hierarchical relationships in a triangle shape.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category uses a grid of four quadrants to show how items relate on two axes?
explanation: The Matrix category displays items in a 2×2 (or similar) grid showing relationship to two axes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is WordArt in Microsoft Word?
options: A type of word processing software
Decorative text with special styles; gradients; and effects for titles or headings
explanation: WordArt creates stylised text with gradients; shadows; reflections; and other visual effects for decorative headings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To insert WordArt in Word; you go to?
explanation: WordArt is inserted from the Insert tab → Text group → WordArt button.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After inserting WordArt; which tab appears to help you format it?
explanation: When WordArt (or any drawing object) is selected; the Drawing Tools → Format contextual tab appears with text effect and style options.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What type of border can be added to a Word document page?
options: Page Borders in a variety of styles; colours; and even art (pictures)
explanation: Word's Page Border feature (Design → Page Borders) offers lines in many styles and colours; plus decorative 'Art' borders made from small pictures.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a page border in Word 2016; you go to?
explanation: Page Borders are accessed via the Design tab → Page Background group → Page Borders in Word 2016.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of a page border in a Word document?
options: To add a decorative or formal frame around the entire page
explanation: A page border frames the entire page with a line or decorative pattern; enhancing the document's visual appeal.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In the Borders and Shading dialog; the 'Box' setting applies a border to?
options: All four sides of the page or selected paragraph
explanation: The 'Box' setting in the Borders and Shading dialog adds a border to all four sides of the selected area.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To print a Word document; you go to?
explanation: File → Print (or Ctrl+P) opens the Print pane where you configure print settings and send the document to the printer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Before printing; it is good practice to use?
options: Print Preview to check the layout before wasting paper
explanation: Print Preview (shown automatically in the File → Print pane) lets you check the document's appearance before printing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In the Print pane (File → Print); the 'Copies' field allows you to?
options: Set how many copies of the document are printed
explanation: The Copies field specifies how many printed copies of the document the printer should produce.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In the Print pane; which option allows you to print only page 3 of a 10-page document?
options: Custom Range (type '3' in the Pages box)
explanation: Entering '3' in the Pages custom range box prints only page 3; you can also print ranges like '2-5' or specific pages like '1;3;7'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In the Print pane; what does the 'Both Sides' option do?
options: Prints the front and back of each sheet (duplex printing)
explanation: 'Print on Both Sides' (duplex printing) prints the document on both sides of each sheet of paper.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To print in LANDSCAPE orientation; you change?
options: The Page Orientation (from Portrait to Landscape) in Layout/Page Setup
explanation: Changing Page Orientation from Portrait (tall) to Landscape (wide) prints the page rotated 90 degrees.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the difference between Portrait and Landscape page orientation?
options: Portrait is wider than tall; Landscape is taller than wide
Portrait is taller than wide (standard); Landscape is wider than tall
Portrait is for photos; Landscape is for text
explanation: Portrait is the standard vertical (taller than wide) orientation; Landscape is horizontal (wider than tall).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Word; the Drawing Tools Format tab appears when?
options: A Shape; WordArt; or other drawing object is selected
explanation: The Drawing Tools Format contextual tab appears only when a drawing object (Shape; WordArt; picture) is selected.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To resize a Shape in Word; you?
options: Drag the sizing handles (small squares/circles) at the corners or edges
explanation: Shapes have sizing handles (white squares/circles) at corners and edges; dragging them resizes the shape.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To move a Shape to a different position in Word; you?
options: Drag the shape to the new position (click the shape interior and drag)
explanation: Click anywhere inside a Shape (not on a handle) and drag to reposition it on the page.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Text Wrapping' for a Shape or image control?
options: How the document text flows around the shape or image
explanation: Text Wrapping (accessed via right-click or Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange) controls how body text wraps around an inserted object.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To group multiple Shapes in Word (so they move as one)?
options: Select all shapes → Drawing Tools Format → Arrange → Group
explanation: Select all the shapes (Ctrl+click each); then in Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange → Group to combine them into a single moveable unit.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which Word feature creates a decorative text heading with gradients and 3D effects?
explanation: WordArt creates visually styled decorative text suitable for headings; titles; and banners.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: SmartArt graphics can be converted to regular shapes in Word by?
options: Right-click SmartArt → Convert → Convert to Shapes
explanation: Right-click the SmartArt → Convert → Convert to Shapes breaks the SmartArt into individual grouped shapes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the colour scheme of a SmartArt graphic quickly; you use?
explanation: The SmartArt Tools Design tab → Change Colors dropdown gives a palette of pre-set colour schemes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the layout of a SmartArt graphic to a different style; you use?
explanation: SmartArt Tools Design → Layouts gallery allows switching between different visual layouts within the same SmartArt category.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'Shadow' text effect do in WordArt?
options: Adds a drop shadow behind the text
explanation: Shadow adds a drop shadow effect behind WordArt or formatted text; giving it a three-dimensional appearance.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add text inside a Shape in Word; you?
options: Insert a separate text box next to the shape
Double-click the shape and type the text
explanation: Double-clicking a shape (or right-clicking → Add Text) places a cursor inside it so text can be typed directly in the shape.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 6; students learn three advanced Word features. These are?
explanation: Chapter 6 of Terabytes Book 4 covers three visual content features: Shapes; SmartArt; and WordArt; plus Borders and Printing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After printing a Word document; the printed paper copy is called a?
explanation: A hardcopy (or hard copy) is the physical printed paper version of a document; as opposed to a softcopy stored digitally.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a 'softcopy' of a document?
options: The digital version stored on a computer or device
explanation: A softcopy is the digital version of a document stored electronically — it can be viewed on screen but is not physically printed.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a Word Art effect to existing text in Word; you first?
options: Type the text in Word then select it and apply WordArt
explanation: You type the text normally; select it; then apply WordArt through Insert → Text → WordArt to add effects.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Rotate' (in Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange → Rotate) do to a shape?
options: Turns the shape at an angle
Moves it to a new position
explanation: Rotate spins the shape to any angle; available via the rotate handle (circular arrow above the shape) or the Arrange → Rotate menu.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is NOT a SmartArt category in Word?
explanation: Equation is not a SmartArt category; the eight categories are List; Process; Cycle; Hierarchy; Relationship; Matrix; Pyramid; and Picture.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The 'Picture' SmartArt category is used to?
options: Create diagrams that combine images with text labels
explanation: The Picture category in SmartArt contains layouts designed to display images alongside descriptive text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Word; the SHAPES gallery includes which types of shapes?
options: Lines; basic shapes; block arrows; equation shapes; flowchart symbols; stars; banners; and callouts
explanation: The Shapes gallery organises many shape types including lines; rectangles; basic shapes; block arrows; flowchart shapes; stars; banners; and callouts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the difference between a Shape and WordArt in Word?
options: Shape is a geometric outline; WordArt is stylised text with visual effects
WordArt is a shape; Shape is text
Shape stores data; WordArt stores images
explanation: Shapes are geometric outlines (rectangles; circles; arrows; etc.); WordArt is a text object with decorative font effects applied to it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To delete a Shape from a Word document; you?
options: Press Backspace while the cursor is inside the shape
Click the shape to select it; then press the Delete key
explanation: Clicking the shape to select it (blue handles appear); then pressing Delete removes it from the document.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To insert a text box as a floating text container in Word; you go to?
explanation: Insert → Text → Text Box allows inserting a floating text box that can be positioned anywhere on the page.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'Bring to Front' option do for overlapping shapes?
options: Moves the shape behind all others
Sends the shape to the back of the drawing layer
Moves the selected shape in front of all other overlapping shapes
explanation: Bring to Front (Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange → Bring to Front) places the selected shape on top of all others in the stacking order.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When printing; what does 'Number of copies: 3' mean?
options: Print the document 3 times (3 identical printed copies)
explanation: Setting Number of copies to 3 tells the printer to produce 3 identical printed copies of the document.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a SHADOW effect to a shape in Word; you use?
options: Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Effects → Shadow
explanation: Shape Effects (Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Effects) includes Shadow; Reflection; Glow; and other visual effects.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What tab appears in Word when SmartArt is selected?
explanation: Selecting a SmartArt object reveals the SmartArt Tools with two tabs: Design (layouts; styles; colours) and Format (shape styles; size).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To reset a SmartArt graphic to its original formatting; you use?
explanation: SmartArt Tools Design → Reset Graphic reverts all customisations (colours; shapes; text position) back to the original SmartArt layout.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student inserts a shape and adds text inside it. She then wants to remove the shape but keep the text. She should?
options: Delete the shape (which deletes the text too) then retype the text
Convert the shape to a text box; copy the text; delete the shape; paste the text
explanation: The safest approach is to convert the shape to a text box (or copy the text first); delete the shape; then paste the text into a regular text area.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the primary purpose of adding a Page Border to a school project document?
options: To add a decorative or professional frame that enhances the document's appearance
explanation: Page borders frame the document neatly; adding a professional or decorative look — common in school projects; certificates; and formal reports.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In the Borders and Shading dialog; the 'Art' option under Page Border allows you to?
options: Use small repeated pictures (like hearts; stars; or Christmas trees) as the border
explanation: The Art dropdown in Borders and Shading → Page Border contains decorative repeated-image borders (stars; apples; etc.).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which key do you hold while clicking multiple shapes in Word to select them all?
explanation: Holding Ctrl (or Shift) while clicking additional shapes adds them to the current selection — useful before grouping.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When would you use SmartArt instead of a plain bulleted list?
options: When you want a visually appealing graphical layout for a process; hierarchy; or relationship
When you need a table of numbers
explanation: SmartArt transforms plain list or process text into professional-looking diagrams that are more visually engaging than plain text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Where is the 'Shape Fill' dropdown found in Word?
options: Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Styles → Shape Fill
explanation: Shape Fill is in Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Styles → Shape Fill (dropdown) allowing solid colours; gradients; textures; or pictures.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Collated' mean in the Print settings?
explanation: Collated printing produces complete sets of documents in order (1-2-3; 1-2-3); Uncollated produces all page 1s then all page 2s; etc.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To quickly format a Shape with a pre-designed combination of fill and outline; you use?
options: Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Styles gallery
explanation: The Shape Styles gallery in Drawing Tools → Format provides pre-designed combinations of fill; outline; and effects for quick formatting.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Page Setup' in Word let you configure?
explanation: Page Setup (File → Print → Page Setup; or Layout → Page Setup group) controls margins; paper size; and orientation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 6; students insert Shapes and learn two key customisation options. These are?
explanation: Chapter 6 focuses on Shape Fill (interior colour) and Shape Outline (border colour/thickness) as the two main customisation options.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt type would be BEST for showing a company's organisational chart?
explanation: The Hierarchy → Organisation Chart layout in SmartArt is specifically designed for showing reporting structures.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the advantage of using SmartArt over manually drawing shapes?
options: SmartArt is faster; automatically aligns shapes; and updates layout when text is added
SmartArt works in older versions of Word only
explanation: SmartArt saves time because it auto-arranges and aligns shapes and connectors; and updates the layout automatically as text is added.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After inserting a SmartArt diagram; to add more items to it you?
options: Click a shape in the diagram and press Enter to add a new shape at the same level
explanation: Pressing Enter inside a SmartArt shape adds a new sibling shape at the same level in the diagram.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'More SmartArt graphics' option at the bottom of the Layouts gallery do?
options: Opens the full Choose a SmartArt Graphic dialog with all categories and layouts
Saves the SmartArt as an image
explanation: The Choose a SmartArt Graphic dialog lists all SmartArt layouts organised by category for full selection.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the weight (thickness) of a Shape's outline in Word; you use?
options: Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Styles → Shape Outline → Weight
explanation: Shape Outline → Weight (in Drawing Tools → Format → Shape Styles) lets you choose the thickness of the shape's border line.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which printing option allows printing multiple document pages on a single sheet of paper?
options: Pages per Sheet (e.g. 2 or 4 pages per sheet)
explanation: Pages per Sheet (in the Print pane → Settings) reduces each document page and prints multiple on one physical sheet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When should you use the 'Draft' print quality setting?
options: For quick text-only proofs where ink saving matters
explanation: Draft quality uses less ink and prints faster — suitable for checking text layout; not for final documents or images.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a Drop Shadow to WordArt text in Word; you use?
options: Drawing Tools → Format → WordArt Styles → Text Effects → Shadow
explanation: Text Effects → Shadow (in Drawing Tools → Format → WordArt Styles) applies shadow effects to WordArt text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the correct path to insert shapes in Microsoft Word 2016?
explanation: The correct path is Insert tab → Illustrations group → Shapes dropdown to see all available shapes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Page Border Art' use as the repeating border element?
options: Small clip-art style images (e.g. trees; stars; hearts)
explanation: Page Border Art uses repeated small pictures (clip-art style) as decorative border elements in Word's Borders and Shading dialog.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To select a shape and COPY it (create an identical duplicate) in Word; you?
options: Click the shape then press Ctrl+D
explanation: Ctrl+D (Duplicate) or Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V creates an identical copy of the selected shape.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Book 4 Chapter 6; the eight SmartArt categories taught are?
options: Arrow; Circle; Box; Oval; Star; Triangle; Diamond; Pentagon
List; Process; Cycle; Hierarchy; Relationship; Matrix; Pyramid; Picture
Graph; Chart; Diagram; Map; Tree; Flow; Web; Grid
Shape; Art; Word; Border; Column; Row; Cell; Table
explanation: The eight SmartArt categories in Word are List; Process; Cycle; Hierarchy; Relationship; Matrix; Pyramid; and Picture.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student creates a WordArt heading but decides she wants it to look like a normal text heading instead. She should?
options: Delete it and retype it as regular text
Convert or copy the text; delete the WordArt; and apply normal heading styles
Change the font colour to black
explanation: The simplest approach is to copy the text from the WordArt; delete the WordArt; paste the text in a normal paragraph; and apply a heading style.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 6; what type of software is Microsoft Word categorised as?
explanation: Microsoft Word is a word processor — software designed primarily for creating; editing; formatting; and printing text documents.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student prints a 5-page document but only 4 pages come out of the printer. The MOST likely reason is?
options: The printer ran out of paper after page 4
The screen resolution is too low
explanation: Running out of paper mid-print is the most common reason for a print job to stop before all pages are printed.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To make printed text larger on the page WITHOUT changing the font size in the document; you change?
options: The Page Scaling (in Print → Settings → Scale to Paper Size)
explanation: Print scaling (or 'Scale to Paper Size') adjusts how the document is rendered on the physical paper without changing the document's font sizes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of using a Page Border on a school certificate template?
options: To protect the file from viruses
To frame the certificate professionally and make it look official
explanation: Page borders are widely used on certificates; awards; and formal documents to create a neat professional frame.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which keyboard shortcut duplicates (makes an instant copy of) a selected shape in Word?
explanation: Ctrl+D instantly duplicates the selected object; placing the copy slightly offset from the original.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: After inserting a SmartArt graphic; a student wants to show it in 3D style. She uses?
options: SmartArt Tools → Design → SmartArt Styles → 3D styles
explanation: SmartArt Tools Design → SmartArt Styles gallery includes flat and three-dimensional style options.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the text you type inside a SmartArt shape called in the Text pane?
options: Bullet point in the Text pane
explanation: SmartArt's Text pane shows the content as an outline with bullet points — each bullet corresponds to a shape in the diagram.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following BEST describes the SmartArt 'Hierarchy' category?
options: Shows data in a triangular shape
Shows a tree-like structure of authority or classification
explanation: Hierarchy diagrams show who or what is at the top and who reports to or belongs under them — e.g. organisational charts or family trees.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to add a decorative coloured frame only around a single paragraph (not the whole page). She uses?
options: Paragraph Borders (Home → Paragraph → Borders dropdown → Box)
explanation: Paragraph borders are applied from the Borders dropdown in the Home → Paragraph group and frame only the selected paragraph.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the advantage of using Print Preview before printing?
options: It lets you check layout and spot errors before wasting paper and ink
explanation: Print Preview shows exactly how each page will look when printed; helping catch layout issues before committing to paper.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To print only ODD pages of a document in Word; you choose?
explanation: The Print pane's 'Print Odd Pages Only' option prints pages 1;3;5;7... — useful for manual duplex printing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the keyboard shortcut to open the Print dialog in Word?
explanation: Ctrl+P opens the Print pane (File → Print) — the quickest way to print or preview before printing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Microsoft Word; the 'Format Shape' pane includes which sections for a shape?
explanation: The Format Shape pane has three main sections: Fill & Line (colours); Effects (Shadow; Reflection; Glow; Soft Edges; 3D); and Size & Properties.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When a Shape has a DASHED outline in Word; this means?
options: The outline style is set to a dashed or dotted line (e.g. Square Dot or Dash)
explanation: A dashed or dotted outline is achieved by setting Shape Outline → Dashes to a non-solid style such as 'Square Dot'; 'Dash'; or 'Long Dash'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To make a Shape perfectly CIRCULAR in Word; you hold ___ while drawing with the Oval tool?
explanation: Holding Shift while dragging the Oval shape tool constrains it to a perfect circle; similarly Shift constrains Rectangle to a perfect square.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the 'Align' options in Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange?
options: To align selected shapes relative to each other or to the page (e.g. Align Left; Centre; Top)
explanation: Align tools (Align Left; Align Center; Distribute Horizontally; etc.) help position multiple shapes neatly relative to each other or to the page.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category would show how ingredients combine to make a cake (inputs → output)?
explanation: A Process (or Relationship; converging type) SmartArt shows how multiple inputs flow together to produce a single output — ideal for recipes or synthesis diagrams.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4; when printing; 'Print Layout view' is recommended because?
options: It shows the document as continuous text
It shows exactly how the page will look when printed (margins; headers; page breaks)
explanation: Print Layout view (the default view in Word) shows the document as printed pages with margins; headers; footers; and images in position.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens if you press Ctrl+Z after inserting a SmartArt?
options: It undoes the insertion; removing the SmartArt
explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the most recent action — pressing it after inserting SmartArt removes it from the document.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Glow' under Shape Effects add to a shape?
options: A coloured radiated halo/glow effect around the outside of the shape
explanation: The Glow effect (Shape Effects → Glow) adds a soft coloured light radiating outward from the shape's edges.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the FONT inside a shape in Word; you?
options: Click inside the shape to place the cursor;select the text; then use the Home tab Font group
Use the Drawing Tools → Format tab Font options
You cannot change the font inside a shape
explanation: To format text inside a shape; click inside it to enter edit mode; select the text; then apply font changes from the Home tab.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'Reflection' under WordArt text effects do?
options: Creates a mirror-image reflection of the text below or beside it
explanation: The Reflection text effect creates a faded mirror copy of the WordArt below (or beside) the original text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which border style applies the same border to every page EXCEPT the first page?
options: None on first page (Apply to: This section - first page only option)
explanation: In the Borders and Shading dialog; the 'Apply to' dropdown can be set to 'This section - all except first page' to skip the border on the title page.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the Internet?
options: A global network of millions of interconnected computers and devices that share information
explanation: The Internet is a worldwide network connecting millions of computers and devices; enabling them to communicate and share data.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Who is known as the 'Father of the Internet' for his work on TCP/IP protocols?
explanation: Vinton Cerf (along with Robert Kahn) developed TCP/IP; the foundational communication protocols of the Internet; earning him the title 'Father of the Internet'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Who invented the World Wide Web (WWW) in 1989?
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN; proposing a system of hypertext documents linked by URLs.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What was the first computer network; developed in the 1960s; that was the forerunner of the Internet?
explanation: ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network); funded by the US Department of Defense in the 1960s; was the first packet-switched network and the direct predecessor of the Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In which decade was ARPANET developed?
explanation: ARPANET was developed in the late 1960s; with the first message sent in 1969 between UCLA and Stanford Research Institute.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does WWW stand for?
explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web — the system of hypertext documents accessed via the Internet using browsers.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a WEB BROWSER?
options: A device for connecting to the Internet
Software used to access and navigate websites on the World Wide Web (e.g. Google Chrome; Firefox; Safari)
explanation: A web browser is an application that retrieves; renders; and displays web pages — examples include Google Chrome; Mozilla Firefox; Microsoft Edge; and Safari.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is an example of a web browser?
explanation: Google Chrome is one of the most widely used web browsers; along with Firefox; Safari; and Edge.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a WEBSITE?
options: A collection of related web pages belonging to a person; organisation; or business; accessible via the Internet
explanation: A website is a set of interconnected web pages grouped under a single domain name; like www.bbc.com or www.google.com.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a WEB PAGE?
options: A single document on the World Wide Web that can contain text; images; videos; and links
explanation: A web page is one individual document/page within a website; identified by its own URL and displayed in a browser.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does URL stand for?
explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator — it is the web address used to locate a specific resource (web page; file; image) on the Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In the URL 'https://www.bbc.com/news'; what does 'https' represent?
options: The protocol (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) used to transfer data
explanation: HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) is the protocol — the set of rules — for transferring web pages securely between a browser and web server.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does HTTP stand for?
explanation: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol — the original (non-secure) protocol for transferring web pages. HTTPS adds encryption for security.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a HYPERLINK (link) on a web page?
options: Clickable text or image that takes you to another web page or resource
explanation: A hyperlink is clickable text (usually underlined and coloured) or an image that; when clicked; navigates the browser to another page; section; or resource.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a SEARCH ENGINE?
options: A browser that displays web pages
A web tool (like Google) that indexes and searches the Internet to find web pages matching a query
explanation: A search engine indexes millions of web pages and returns results matching a user's search query — examples include Google; Bing; Yahoo; and DuckDuckGo.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is a well-known search engine?
explanation: Google is the most widely used search engine; processing billions of searches per day.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an ISP?
options: Internet Service Provider — a company that provides users with access to the Internet
explanation: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is a company (like Etisalat; du; or BT) that provides individuals and organisations with access to the Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'downloading' mean in the context of the Internet?
options: Sending a file from your computer to a server
Receiving a file or data FROM the Internet TO your device
explanation: Downloading transfers data from a remote server (on the Internet) to your local device — for example saving an image or installing software.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'uploading' mean in the context of the Internet?
options: Sending a file FROM your device TO the Internet (e.g. posting a photo on social media)
explanation: Uploading sends data from your device to a remote server — for example posting a photo to Instagram or submitting an assignment online.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is EMAIL?
options: A paper letter sent by post
Electronic mail — messages sent and received digitally over the Internet
explanation: Email (electronic mail) allows text messages; images; and files to be sent and received instantly over the Internet between any two email addresses.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does '@' in an email address (e.g. student@school.com) separate?
options: The username from the domain name
The file type from the file name
explanation: The '@' symbol in an email address separates the username (student) from the domain name (school.com); indicating where the mailbox is hosted.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is SOCIAL MEDIA?
options: Online platforms (like Facebook; Instagram; TikTok) that allow people to create and share content and connect with others
explanation: Social media platforms allow users to create profiles; post content; and interact with others — examples include Facebook; Instagram; YouTube; Snapchat; and Twitter/X.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is an example of social media?
explanation: Instagram is a social media platform focused on photo and video sharing; owned by Meta.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is CLOUD STORAGE?
options: Storing files on remote servers accessed via the Internet (e.g. Google Drive; Dropbox; OneDrive)
Storing files on a USB flash drive
Storing data in a printed folder
explanation: Cloud storage saves files on remote servers (the 'cloud') accessible from any Internet-connected device — examples include Google Drive; Dropbox; and Microsoft OneDrive.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does WIFI stand for?
options: Wireless Fidelity — a technology for connecting devices to a network wirelessly
explanation: WiFi (Wireless Fidelity) uses radio signals to connect devices to a local network and the Internet without physical cables.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What device in a home connects devices to the Internet wirelessly?
explanation: A wireless router connects to the ISP's broadband line and broadcasts a WiFi signal allowing multiple devices to connect to the Internet simultaneously.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is ONLINE SAFETY?
options: Practising behaviours to protect personal information and stay safe while using the Internet
explanation: Online safety involves keeping personal data private; avoiding strangers online; reporting cyberbullying; and using strong passwords to stay safe on the Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What should you NEVER share online with strangers?
options: Your full name; address; phone number; school name; or passwords
explanation: Personal information such as your full name; home address; phone number; and school name should never be shared with strangers online to prevent harm.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is CYBERBULLYING?
options: Using technology (social media; texts; online games) to repeatedly harass; threaten; or embarrass someone
explanation: Cyberbullying uses digital devices and platforms to bully; threaten; or humiliate others — it is harmful and should be reported to a trusted adult.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: If you experience cyberbullying online; you should?
options: Block the bully and tell a trusted adult (parent; teacher; or school counsellor)
Share the bully's posts with friends
explanation: Blocking the bully to stop contact and telling a trusted adult is the safest response to cyberbullying; they can help address the situation properly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a strong PASSWORD?
options: A combination of uppercase letters; lowercase letters; numbers; and symbols (e.g. P@ssw0rd#7)
explanation: A strong password uses a mix of character types and is at least 8 characters long — it should not be an easily guessed word like your name or birthday.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a VIRUS in computing?
options: Malicious software designed to replicate itself and harm a computer or its data
explanation: A computer virus is malware (malicious software) that copies itself and can delete files; slow down the computer; or steal data.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does ANTIVIRUS software do?
options: Detects; blocks; and removes malicious software (viruses; malware) from your computer
explanation: Antivirus software scans your computer for known malware and removes threats; acting as a digital security guard.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is SPAM email?
options: Unsolicited (unwanted) bulk email; usually sent for advertising or phishing
explanation: Spam emails are unsolicited messages sent in bulk — often advertisements; scams; or phishing attempts to steal personal information.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is PHISHING?
options: A cyber attack where criminals send fake emails or websites to trick people into revealing passwords or personal information
A way to speed up downloads
explanation: Phishing uses deceptive emails or fake websites that look legitimate to trick users into entering passwords; credit card numbers; or other sensitive data.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a DOMAIN NAME in a URL (e.g. google.com)?
options: The human-readable address of a website's server on the Internet
explanation: A domain name (like google.com or bbc.co.uk) is the human-readable address used to find a website; which maps to a numeric IP address.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does '.com' in a domain name typically indicate?
explanation: '.com' is the most common top-level domain (TLD) originally intended for commercial organisations; now used by websites worldwide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does '.edu' in a URL typically indicate?
explanation: '.edu' is a top-level domain (TLD) reserved for educational institutions; primarily universities and schools in the United States.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does '.gov' in a URL typically indicate?
explanation: '.gov' is a TLD used by government bodies — for example; www.whitehouse.gov (US) or www.uae.gov.ae (UAE).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'www' in a URL stand for?
explanation: 'www' stands for World Wide Web — it is a traditional subdomain prefix indicating the resource is part of the World Wide Web.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web?
options: They are exactly the same thing
The Internet is the global network infrastructure; the WWW is a service (websites) that runs ON the Internet
The WWW is faster than the Internet
The Internet is only for email; the WWW is for everything else
explanation: The Internet is the physical/digital network (cables; routers; protocols); the WWW is a service (web pages and hyperlinks) that uses the Internet — other services like email also use the Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an IP ADDRESS?
options: A postal address for a computer
A unique numerical label (e.g. 192.168.1.1) assigned to each device on a network to identify it and allow communication
explanation: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a unique number assigned to every device on a network; allowing data to be routed to the correct destination.
subject: Grade 4 Computing
