text: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web while working at which organisation?
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee was a physicist at CERN in Switzerland when he proposed and developed the World Wide Web in 1989; initially to share research data among scientists.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In which year did Tim Berners-Lee publish his proposal for the World Wide Web?
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee published his proposal 'Information Management: A Proposal' in 1989; describing the hypertext-based information system that became the World Wide Web.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is VIDEO STREAMING?
options: Downloading a video file completely before watching
Watching video content in real time over the Internet without downloading the full file first
explanation: Video streaming (e.g. Netflix; YouTube) delivers video data continuously over the Internet; allowing playback to begin immediately without waiting for a full download.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of these is an example of a video streaming platform?
explanation: YouTube is a video streaming platform where users upload; share; and watch videos — it is one of the most visited websites in the world.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is ONLINE SHOPPING?
options: Buying items from a physical shop
Buying and selling goods or services over the Internet using a website or app
explanation: Online shopping (e-commerce) allows consumers to browse and purchase products through websites like Amazon; Noon; or eBay; paying digitally and receiving delivery.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a COOKIE in web browsing?
options: A small data file stored on your device by a website to remember your preferences and activity
explanation: Web cookies are small text files saved on your device when you visit a website; allowing it to remember your login status; preferences; and browsing activity.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the PADLOCK ICON in a browser's address bar indicate?
options: The website is locked and cannot be viewed
The connection to the website is secure (HTTPS); protecting data from eavesdroppers
explanation: A padlock in the address bar shows the website uses HTTPS; meaning data between your browser and the server is encrypted — look for it when entering passwords or payment details.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is BANDWIDTH?
options: The maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over an Internet connection in a given time (measured in Mbps or Gbps)
The number of web pages on a site
The size of the computer's hard drive
explanation: Bandwidth determines how much data flows through your connection per second — a higher bandwidth (e.g. 100 Mbps vs 10 Mbps) allows faster downloads and smoother streaming.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does it mean when a website is 'DOWN'?
options: The website's server is unavailable; so the site cannot be accessed
The website is slow to load
explanation: A website being 'down' means its server is temporarily unavailable (due to maintenance; overload; or a technical fault); so browsers cannot load its pages.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is ONLINE COMMUNICATION?
options: Using the Internet to communicate with others; including email; video calls; instant messaging; and social media
explanation: Online communication encompasses all digital communication methods using the Internet — email; video calls (Zoom; Teams); instant messaging (WhatsApp); and social media interactions.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is VIDEO CALLING?
options: Sending a video file by email
Real-time visual and audio communication with another person or group over the Internet (e.g. Zoom; FaceTime; Google Meet)
explanation: Video calling uses the Internet to transmit live audio and video between participants — tools like Zoom; Microsoft Teams; and FaceTime make this possible.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is a video calling application?
explanation: Zoom is a popular video calling and online meeting platform used for education; business; and personal communication.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What should you do BEFORE clicking a link in an unexpected email?
options: Check that the email is from a trusted sender and that the URL looks legitimate before clicking; or delete it if unsure
Forward it to all your friends
explanation: Checking the sender's address and hovering over the link to preview its URL helps identify phishing attempts before you inadvertently visit a malicious site.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is NETIQUETTE?
options: Accepted rules of polite and appropriate behaviour when communicating online
explanation: Netiquette (Internet etiquette) is the set of conventions for polite; respectful; and responsible communication online — such as not typing in all capitals (which reads as shouting).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does it mean to 'log out' of a website?
options: End your current session on a website to prevent others accessing your account; especially on shared computers
explanation: Logging out ends your authenticated session so that the next person using the device cannot access your account — especially important on shared or public computers.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a BOOKMARK in a web browser?
options: A saved shortcut to a favourite web page so you can return to it quickly
explanation: Browser bookmarks (also called Favourites) save a web page's URL for easy return — accessible from the bookmarks bar or menu.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does CTRL+D typically do in most web browsers?
explanation: Ctrl+D adds the current page to your bookmarks/favourites in most browsers — a quick way to save a useful website.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To REFRESH a web page (reload it to get the latest content); you press?
explanation: F5 (or Ctrl+R) refreshes (reloads) the current web page; fetching the latest version from the server — useful when a page hasn't loaded properly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an ONLINE FORUM?
options: A type of social media app
A website or section of a website where users post questions and replies in threaded discussions on specific topics
explanation: Online forums (like Reddit or stack-based Q&A sites) are community discussion boards where members post questions; share knowledge; and reply to threads.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'going viral' mean on the Internet?
options: A piece of content (video; post; meme) being shared rapidly by a large number of people across the Internet
explanation: Content 'goes viral' when it is shared at an exponential rate across social media and the Internet; reaching millions of viewers very quickly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of a PASSWORD MANAGER?
options: A software tool that securely stores and manages all your passwords so you only need to remember one master password
explanation: A password manager (like LastPass or 1Password) stores all your passwords in an encrypted vault — you only remember one strong master password to unlock them.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does HTTPS stand for?
explanation: HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) is the secure version of HTTP; using TLS/SSL encryption to protect data transmitted between your browser and the web server.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What happens when you type a URL into a browser and press Enter?
options: The file is saved to your computer
The browser sends a request to the web server at that address; which responds by sending back the web page to display
explanation: Pressing Enter after typing a URL sends an HTTP/HTTPS request to the domain's server; which sends back the web page's HTML; CSS; and other resources for the browser to render.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is NOT a web browser?
explanation: Microsoft Word is a word processor; not a web browser. Chrome; Firefox; and Edge are all web browsers used to access the World Wide Web.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is ONLINE LEARNING (e-learning)?
options: Using the Internet and digital tools to access educational content; courses; and resources from anywhere
explanation: E-learning uses the Internet to deliver educational materials — interactive courses; video lectures; quizzes; and online classrooms — accessible from any location.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 7; students learn about which two pioneers of the Internet and Web?
options: Vinton Cerf (Internet/TCP-IP) and Tim Berners-Lee (World Wide Web)
explanation: Chapter 7 of Terabytes Book 4 highlights Vinton Cerf's role in creating the Internet (TCP/IP protocols) and Tim Berners-Lee's invention of the World Wide Web.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the MAIN difference between downloading and uploading?
options: Downloading brings data TO your device; uploading sends data FROM your device
Downloading requires WiFi; uploading requires cables
explanation: Download = data flows from the Internet to your device (receiving); Upload = data flows from your device to the Internet (sending).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does it mean to SURF THE WEB?
options: To browse through websites and web pages on the World Wide Web
explanation: 'Surfing the web' means casually browsing through websites by clicking links and entering URLs; exploring content online.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a HOMEPAGE of a browser?
options: The default page that opens when you launch the browser or click the Home button
explanation: A browser's homepage is the web page it loads when first opened (or when you click the Home button) — commonly set to a search engine or portal.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an ATTACHMENT in an email?
options: A file (document; image; video) sent along with an email message
explanation: An email attachment is a file sent together with an email — the recipient can open; download; and save the file on their device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does ARPANET stand for?
explanation: ARPANET stands for Advanced Research Projects Agency Network — the first wide-area packet-switched network; funded by DARPA; US Department of Defense.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When was ARPANET first operational?
explanation: ARPANET became operational in 1969 when the first message ('LO' — part of 'LOGIN') was sent between UCLA and Stanford Research Institute.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Vinton Cerf developed TCP/IP with which other scientist?
explanation: Vint Cerf and Robert Kahn co-developed the TCP/IP protocol suite in the early 1970s; which became the standard communication protocol for the Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does TCP/IP stand for?
explanation: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol — the two core protocols governing how data is sent and received across the Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In what year did Tim Berners-Lee publish his proposal for the World Wide Web?
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee submitted his proposal 'Information Management: A Proposal' at CERN in March 1989; which became the blueprint for the World Wide Web.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What was the first WEBSITE ever published on the World Wide Web?
options: info.cern.ch — Berners-Lee's project page at CERN
explanation: The first website was published at info.cern.ch in August 1991 by Tim Berners-Lee; explaining what the World Wide Web was and how to access it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What type of address does every website have that makes it unique on the Internet?
options: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) / web address
explanation: Every website is identified by a unique URL (web address) like www.example.com; which the DNS system maps to a numeric IP address on the server.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which of the following is an example of a URL?
explanation: https://www.google.com is a URL — it specifies the protocol (https); subdomain (www); domain (google.com); which together locate a resource on the Web.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does DNS stand for?
options: Domain Name System — translates human-readable domain names to numeric IP addresses
explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) acts like a phone book for the Internet; converting domain names like google.com into IP addresses like 142.250.80.46 that computers use.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a ROUTER's main job in a home Internet setup?
options: Direct (route) data packets between your devices and the Internet Service Provider
explanation: A router receives data from the ISP's line and directs (routes) it to the correct device on the local network; and sends outbound requests to the wider Internet.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does MODEM stand for?
options: Modulator-Demodulator — a device that converts digital signals to analogue and back for Internet transmission
explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital data from a computer to analogue signals for transmission over phone or cable lines; and converts incoming signals back to digital.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'broadband' mean?
options: A high-speed Internet connection that carries large amounts of data simultaneously
explanation: Broadband is a high-speed Internet connection (as opposed to slow dial-up) that transmits data over a wide band of frequencies; allowing fast downloads and streaming.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is FIBRE OPTIC Internet?
options: Very fast Internet delivered over cables made of thin glass fibres that transmit data as pulses of light
explanation: Fibre optic cables use light signals inside thin glass fibres to transmit data at very high speeds — much faster than traditional copper cables.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a WI-FI HOTSPOT?
options: A location where wireless Internet access is provided to the public (e.g. in a coffee shop; airport; or shopping mall)
explanation: A Wi-Fi hotspot is a physical location offering wireless Internet access; usually in public spaces — provided by the venue or a mobile network carrier.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does MOBILE DATA mean?
options: Data stored on a mobile phone
Internet connectivity provided by a mobile network (3G/4G/5G) via a SIM card; without needing Wi-Fi
explanation: Mobile data allows smartphones and tablets to connect to the Internet using cellular (3G; 4G; or 5G) signals from mobile network towers; without needing a Wi-Fi network.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'S' in HTTPS stand for?
explanation: The 'S' in HTTPS stands for Secure — HTTPS uses TLS encryption to protect data between the browser and the web server from interception.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is MALWARE?
options: Any software designed to harm; disrupt; or gain unauthorised access to a computer system (includes viruses; ransomware; spyware)
explanation: Malware (malicious software) is an umbrella term for harmful programs: viruses; trojans; spyware; ransomware; and adware — all designed to damage or steal data.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does a FIREWALL do?
options: Monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic to block unauthorised access to a computer or network
explanation: A firewall (hardware or software) acts as a security barrier; filtering network traffic and blocking malicious connections or unauthorised access attempts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is RANSOMWARE?
options: Malware that encrypts a victim's files and demands payment (ransom) to restore access
explanation: Ransomware is a type of malware that locks or encrypts files; then displays a message demanding cryptocurrency payment for the decryption key.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is SPYWARE?
options: Malware that secretly monitors and collects personal information from a computer without the user's knowledge
explanation: Spyware secretly tracks users' activity — keystrokes; browsing history; passwords — and sends the data to a third party without the victim's knowledge.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of a CAPTCHA on websites?
options: To verify that a user is human and not an automated bot
explanation: A CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart) presents challenges (identify images; read distorted text) that bots cannot easily solve.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION (2FA) add to account security?
options: A second verification step (e.g. a code sent to your phone) in addition to your password
explanation: 2FA adds a second layer of security — after entering your password; you confirm your identity with a code sent to your phone or generated by an app.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a VPN?
options: Virtual Private Network — a service that encrypts your Internet connection and masks your IP address for privacy and security
explanation: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) encrypts your Internet traffic and routes it through a secure server; hiding your IP address and protecting your data on public Wi-Fi.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What should you do if a pop-up offers you a 'free prize' online?
options: Click immediately to claim your prize
Ignore or close it — it is likely a scam or a phishing attempt
explanation: Unsolicited prize pop-ups are almost always scams or phishing attempts designed to collect personal information or install malware — close them without clicking.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the meaning of 'digital footprint'?
options: The size of your hard drive
The trail of data and information you leave behind when using the Internet (browsing history; posts; searches)
The speed of your Internet connection
explanation: Your digital footprint is the record of your online activities — websites visited; posts made; searches performed — which can be tracked and stored permanently.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is ONLINE PRIVACY?
options: Controlling what personal information you share online and who can access it
Using the Internet without a password
Only using the Internet at home
explanation: Online privacy involves limiting the personal data you share; understanding how websites use your data; and using privacy settings to protect your information.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does STREAMING mean for music (e.g. Spotify)?
options: Listening to music over the Internet in real time without permanently downloading the file
explanation: Music streaming services deliver audio over the Internet continuously — you hear it in real time without downloading a permanent file to your device.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is E-COMMERCE?
options: Buying and selling goods or services over the Internet (online shopping)
explanation: E-commerce (electronic commerce) encompasses all commercial transactions conducted online — browsing; ordering; paying for; and receiving products via Internet platforms.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is BANDWIDTH measured in?
options: Megabits per second (Mbps) or Gigabits per second (Gbps)
explanation: Bandwidth is measured in bits per second (bps); typically in Megabits per second (Mbps) for home broadband or Gigabits per second (Gbps) for high-speed connections.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is Microsoft PowerPoint?
options: A word processor for creating documents
Presentation software used to create slideshows of slides containing text; images; and other media
explanation: Microsoft PowerPoint is presentation software that allows users to create multi-slide presentations combining text; images; charts; animations; and videos.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the file extension for a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation?
explanation: PowerPoint files are saved with the .pptx extension (PowerPoint XML format) in Microsoft Office 2007 and later versions.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A PowerPoint presentation is made up of individual?
explanation: A PowerPoint presentation consists of multiple slides — individual pages that are displayed one after another in sequence during a presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the TITLE SLIDE in a PowerPoint presentation?
options: The first slide; typically showing the presentation title and presenter's name
explanation: The title slide is conventionally the first slide in a presentation; displaying the main title; subtitle; author name; and date to introduce the topic.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a SLIDE LAYOUT in PowerPoint?
options: A template that arranges placeholders on a slide (e.g. Title Only; Title and Content; Blank)
explanation: Slide layouts provide predefined arrangements of placeholders for text; images; and other content — for example 'Title and Content'; 'Two Content'; or 'Blank'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a NEW SLIDE in PowerPoint; you?
options: Click Insert → New Slide; or right-click a slide thumbnail and choose 'New Slide'
explanation: New slides are inserted via Insert → New Slide; or by right-clicking in the Slides panel and selecting 'New Slide'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: The area on the left of the PowerPoint window showing small slide pictures is called the?
explanation: The Slides pane on the left shows thumbnail previews of all slides; allowing you to navigate; reorder; and manage slides easily.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Where do you type SPEAKER NOTES in PowerPoint?
options: In the Notes pane at the bottom of the window
In the Header and Footer dialog
explanation: The Notes pane below the slide editing area allows presenters to type speaker notes — reminders and talking points visible to the presenter but not the audience during a presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the RIBBON in PowerPoint?
options: The strip of tabs and buttons at the top of the window containing all commands and tools
explanation: The Ribbon is the tabbed toolbar at the top of Office applications — tabs include Home; Insert; Design; Transitions; Animations; Slide Show; Review; and View.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add TEXT to a slide; you click inside a?
explanation: Text is typed inside text placeholders (pre-placed by the slide layout) or new text boxes inserted via Insert → Text → Text Box.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT an IMAGE from a file into a PowerPoint slide; you go to?
explanation: Insert → Images → Pictures → This Device (or simply 'Picture from File') opens a file browser to select and insert an image from your computer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT a CLIP ART or ONLINE IMAGE in PowerPoint 2016; you go to?
explanation: Insert → Images → Online Pictures opens Microsoft's online image search (powered by Bing) to find and insert royalty-free images.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a THEME in PowerPoint?
options: A pre-designed set of colours; fonts; and effects that gives the presentation a consistent professional look
explanation: A theme applies a coordinated colour palette; font pairing; and graphic effects across all slides — accessible from the Design tab.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To apply a DESIGN THEME to a presentation; you click the?
explanation: The Design tab contains the Themes gallery and the Variants section for customising the theme's colours; fonts; and effects.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How do you CHANGE THE BACKGROUND colour of a single slide in PowerPoint?
options: Design → Format Background; choose a colour; then click 'Apply' (not 'Apply to All')
explanation: Design → Format Background lets you customise a slide's background with a solid fill; gradient; picture; or pattern — clicking 'Apply' changes only the current slide while 'Apply to All' changes all slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a SLIDE TRANSITION in PowerPoint?
options: A visual effect that plays when moving FROM one slide TO the next during the presentation
A way to rearrange slide order
explanation: Slide transitions (e.g. Fade; Push; Wipe; Morph) are animations that play between slides — set via the Transitions tab.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To apply a TRANSITION to a slide; you use which tab?
explanation: The Transitions tab contains the Transition to This Slide gallery; Duration and Sound settings; and 'Apply to All' to apply the same transition to every slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an ANIMATION in PowerPoint?
options: An effect applied to individual objects ON a slide (e.g. a text box flying in or a picture fading in)
explanation: Animations are effects applied to individual objects on a slide — they control how elements enter; exit; or emphasise during the slide show.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which PowerPoint tab is used to add ANIMATIONS to objects on a slide?
explanation: The Animations tab contains the Animation gallery; Effect Options; and the Animation Pane for managing the order and timing of animations.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the SLIDE SHOW view do in PowerPoint?
options: Plays the presentation in full-screen mode as the audience would see it
explanation: Slide Show view plays the presentation in full screen — press F5 to start from the beginning or Shift+F5 to start from the current slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the keyboard shortcut to start a PowerPoint slide show FROM THE BEGINNING?
explanation: F5 starts the slide show from slide 1; Shift+F5 starts from the currently selected slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: During a slide show; how do you advance to the NEXT slide?
options: Press the Right Arrow key or the Spacebar or click the mouse
explanation: During a slide show; pressing the Right Arrow; Down Arrow; Spacebar; Enter; or clicking the mouse advances to the next slide or animation step.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: During a slide show; how do you go BACK to the PREVIOUS slide?
options: Press the Left Arrow or Backspace key
explanation: During a slide show; pressing the Left Arrow; Up Arrow; or Backspace key returns to the previous slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To END a slide show and return to PowerPoint editing; you press?
explanation: Pressing Escape during a slide show exits full-screen mode and returns to the Normal editing view.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the NORMAL VIEW in PowerPoint?
options: The default editing view showing the slide editing area; Slides pane; and Notes pane
A view showing only slide thumbnails
A view showing only the outline
explanation: Normal view (the default) shows the slide thumbnails pane on the left; the main editing area in the centre; and the Notes pane at the bottom.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is SLIDE SORTER VIEW in PowerPoint?
options: A view that hides all slides
A view that shows all slides as thumbnails in rows; making it easy to reorder; copy; or delete slides
explanation: Slide Sorter view displays all slides as small thumbnails — ideal for rearranging slide order; duplicating; or deleting slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is OUTLINE VIEW in PowerPoint?
options: Shows only the text content of each slide as a text outline; making it easy to organise and edit text structure
explanation: Outline view shows the text from each slide's placeholders in a hierarchical outline — useful for reviewing and editing the presentation's content and structure.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To DELETE a slide from a presentation; you?
options: Right-click the slide thumbnail and choose Delete Slide; or select it and press the Delete key
Click the slide and press Backspace once
explanation: Right-clicking a slide thumbnail → Delete Slide; or selecting a slide and pressing the Delete key removes it from the presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To MOVE a slide to a different position; you?
options: Drag the slide thumbnail to the new position in the Slides pane; or cut and paste it
explanation: In the Slides pane; drag a slide thumbnail up or down to change its position; or use Cut (Ctrl+X) and Paste (Ctrl+V) to relocate it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does CTRL+Z do in PowerPoint?
explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the most recent action in PowerPoint; stepping back through changes one at a time.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does CTRL+S do in PowerPoint?
explanation: Ctrl+S saves the current presentation to its existing file location — always save frequently to avoid losing work.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To COPY an object on a slide; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+C copies the selected object to the clipboard; Ctrl+V pastes it — together they duplicate objects on the same or different slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT a VIDEO file into a PowerPoint slide; you go to?
explanation: Insert → Media → Video → This Device inserts a video file from your computer into the slide; which can play during the presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT a TABLE in a PowerPoint slide; you go to?
explanation: Insert → Tables → Table lets you specify columns and rows; inserting a table directly into the slide for displaying structured data.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a PLACEHOLDER in PowerPoint?
options: A dotted border box on a slide layout that reserves space for specific content (title text; body text; image; etc.)
explanation: Placeholders are boxes defined by the slide layout — click inside one to add your content; whether title text; bullet points; or media.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the DESIGN tab's 'Slide Size' option allow you to change?
options: The physical dimensions of the slides (e.g. Widescreen 16:9 or Standard 4:3)
explanation: Slide Size (Design → Customize → Slide Size) lets you choose between Standard (4:3); Widescreen (16:9); and Custom dimensions — Widescreen is the default in PowerPoint 2013+.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is ASPECT RATIO for slides?
options: The proportional relationship between a slide's width and height (e.g. 16:9 or 4:3)
explanation: Aspect ratio describes a slide's proportions — 16:9 (Widescreen) is standard for modern screens; 4:3 (Standard) matches older screens and projectors.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In PowerPoint; to insert a CHART (bar chart; pie chart; etc.); you go to?
explanation: Insert → Illustrations → Chart opens the Insert Chart dialog where you choose chart type and enter data.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a FOOTER (e.g. slide number or date) to all slides; you go to?
explanation: Insert → Text → Header and Footer opens the dialog for adding slide numbers; dates; and footer text to all or specific slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does clicking 'Apply to All' in the transition or design dialog do?
options: Applies the setting to only the selected slide
Applies the setting to every slide in the presentation
explanation: 'Apply to All' applies the transition; background; or other setting to every slide in the presentation simultaneously.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the SLIDE PANEL (Slides pane) on the left?
options: To show thumbnail previews of all slides; allowing navigation and reordering
explanation: The Slides pane shows small thumbnail images of all slides in order — click any thumbnail to navigate to that slide; and drag to reorder.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 8; students learn the basics of PowerPoint including which view is the default editing view?
explanation: Chapter 8 introduces PowerPoint's Normal view as the standard editing environment with the slide panel; editing area; and notes pane.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the maximum number of text BULLET LEVELS in a PowerPoint text box?
explanation: PowerPoint supports up to 9 levels of indented bullet points in a text placeholder — press Tab to increase the indent level; Shift+Tab to decrease it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the ZOOM slider at the bottom-right of the PowerPoint window do?
options: Increases or decreases the magnification level of the slide editing area
explanation: The Zoom slider in the status bar changes how large the current slide appears in the editing view; without affecting the actual slide content or print size.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT a SYMBOL (e.g. © or →) in PowerPoint; you go to?
options: Insert → Text → Symbol or Special Character
explanation: Insert → Text → Symbol opens the Symbol dialog for inserting special characters and symbols not on the keyboard.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What are the three PANES visible in Normal View in PowerPoint?
options: Slides Pane (thumbnails); Slide Editing Area; Notes Pane
explanation: Normal View shows the Slides Pane (left; thumbnails); the main Slide Editing Area (centre); and the Notes Pane (bottom) — the three primary working areas.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To SELECT ALL OBJECTS on a slide in PowerPoint; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+A selects all objects on the current slide — useful when you want to move; resize; or format all elements together.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the READING VIEW in PowerPoint?
options: A view that plays the slide show inside the PowerPoint window (not full screen) — useful for reviewing the presentation on your own
explanation: Reading View plays the presentation in a window (rather than full screen); allowing you to review the slide show without other applications being hidden.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student wants to present a project on computers using PowerPoint. Which view should she use to PRESENT to the class?
explanation: Slide Show view (F5) plays the presentation in full screen on the screen or projector; displaying it exactly as the audience will see it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To ADD SLIDE NUMBERS to all slides; you go to?
options: Insert → Text → Slide Number (or Header & Footer → tick 'Slide number')
explanation: Insert → Text → Slide Number; or via Insert → Header and Footer → check 'Slide number'; then 'Apply to All' adds sequential slide numbers to every slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the STATUS BAR at the bottom of the PowerPoint window?
options: To show information such as current slide number; total slides; zoom level; and view buttons
explanation: The status bar displays contextual information — slide number (e.g. 'Slide 3 of 10'); language setting; zoom slider; and view shortcuts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the FONT of text in a PowerPoint text box; you first?
options: Select the text then use the Font dropdown in Home tab
explanation: Text must be selected first; then font changes (typeface; size; colour; bold; italic) are applied from the Font group in the Home tab.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does BOLD text formatting do in PowerPoint?
options: Makes text thicker and heavier for emphasis
explanation: Bold (Ctrl+B) makes the selected text thicker and darker — used to emphasise key words or headings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does ITALIC text formatting do in PowerPoint?
options: Slants the text to the right for stylistic emphasis
explanation: Italic (Ctrl+I) slants the text — used for titles; terms; or light emphasis in presentation text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does UNDERLINE text formatting do in PowerPoint?
options: Draws a line under the text — often used for links or emphasis
explanation: Underline (Ctrl+U) draws a horizontal line beneath the selected text — used for links or emphasis.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To ALIGN text to the CENTRE of a text box in PowerPoint; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+E centres the selected text within its text box — the other alignment shortcuts are Ctrl+L (left); Ctrl+R (right); Ctrl+J (justify).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a PRESENTATION HANDOUT in PowerPoint?
options: Printed pages showing multiple slide thumbnails per page for the audience to keep
explanation: Handouts are printed pages showing 2; 3; 4; 6; or 9 slide thumbnails per page — printed via File → Print → Handouts for audience takeaways.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To PRINT a PowerPoint presentation as HANDOUTS (multiple slides per page); you go to?
options: File → Print → Settings → Full Page Slides → change to Handouts
explanation: In File → Print; click 'Full Page Slides' to open the print layout dropdown; then select a Handouts layout (e.g. '2 Slides'; '3 Slides'; etc.).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does SLIDE SHOW → REHEARSE TIMINGS do?
options: Records how long you spend on each slide during a practice run; so the presentation can run automatically at those timings
explanation: Rehearse Timings plays the slide show and records the time spent on each slide — you can save these timings for a self-running presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In PowerPoint; what is 'PRESENTER VIEW'?
options: A special display mode showing the current slide on one screen and speaker notes; next slide; and timer on the presenter's screen
explanation: Presenter View (available when connected to a projector) shows the current slide on the projector; while the presenter's laptop shows notes; the next slide; and an elapsed timer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT a HYPERLINK to a website in PowerPoint; you select text or an object then?
options: Go to Insert → Links → Hyperlink (or press Ctrl+K)
explanation: Insert → Links → Hyperlink (Ctrl+K) opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog where you enter the destination URL or select a slide within the presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'APPLY TO ALL' button do in the Background Formatting pane?
options: Applies only to the selected slide
Applies the chosen background to every slide in the presentation
explanation: 'Apply to All' in the Format Background pane replaces the background of all slides simultaneously with the selected fill; gradient; picture; or pattern.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of ANIMATIONS in a presentation?
options: To make objects on a slide appear; disappear; or move to draw the audience's attention or reveal content step by step
explanation: Animations control when and how individual objects (text; images; shapes) appear or move on a slide — helping control the flow of information during a presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an ENTRANCE animation in PowerPoint?
options: How a slide transitions to the next
How an object APPEARS on a slide (e.g. Fly In; Fade; Bounce)
How an object leaves the slide
How an object moves across the slide
explanation: Entrance animations control how objects enter or appear on a slide — examples include Appear; Fade; Fly In; Zoom; Bounce.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an EXIT animation in PowerPoint?
options: How an object APPEARS on a slide
How an object DISAPPEARS from a slide (e.g. Fly Out; Fade Out)
explanation: Exit animations control how objects leave or disappear from a slide — examples include Disappear; Fade; Fly Out; Float Out.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an EMPHASIS animation in PowerPoint?
options: An animation that draws ATTENTION to an object already visible (e.g. Pulse; Spin; Grow/Shrink)
explanation: Emphasis animations apply to objects that are already visible — they highlight or draw attention without the object leaving the slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the ANIMATION PANE in PowerPoint show?
options: A list of all animations on the current slide with their order; timing; and type — allowing fine-grained control
explanation: The Animation Pane (Animations → Advanced Animation → Animation Pane) lists all animation effects on the slide; their order; duration; trigger; and allows reordering.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'TRIGGER: ON CLICK' mean for an animation?
options: The animation plays automatically after a delay
The animation plays when a specific object is clicked during the slide show
The animation plays when the slide appears
explanation: On Click trigger means the animation plays when the presenter clicks the mouse or presses a key during the slide show — giving manual control.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'TRIGGER: AFTER PREVIOUS' mean for an animation?
options: The animation plays automatically after the preceding animation finishes
The animation plays before the previous one
explanation: After Previous means the animation starts automatically when the preceding animation in the sequence finishes — creating a chain of sequential effects.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'TRIGGER: WITH PREVIOUS' mean for an animation?
options: The animation plays after the previous animation
The animation plays at the SAME TIME as the preceding animation
The animation plays before all others
explanation: With Previous makes the animation start simultaneously with the animation immediately above it in the pane — creating a simultaneous multi-effect.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a SOUND to a slide transition in PowerPoint; you?
options: In the Transitions tab; open the Sound dropdown and select a sound
explanation: The Transitions tab includes a Sound dropdown (next to Duration) where you can add a sound effect that plays when the transition occurs.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'ADVANCE SLIDE: AFTER 5 SECONDS' do in the Transitions tab?
options: Automatically advances the presentation to the next slide after 5 seconds without clicking
explanation: Setting 'After: 5 seconds' in the Transitions tab makes the slide automatically advance after 5 seconds — useful for self-running kiosk or timed presentations.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the NOTES PAGE view in PowerPoint?
options: Shows each slide as a printed page with the speaker notes below it; suitable for detailed note review
explanation: Notes Page view (View → Presentation Views → Notes Page) shows each slide reduced to half a page with the notes text below — useful for reviewing or printing detailed notes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a LOGO IMAGE to EVERY SLIDE (e.g. school logo in the corner); the best method is to?
options: Paste it on every slide individually
Add it to the SLIDE MASTER (View → Master Views → Slide Master)
explanation: The Slide Master (View → Master Views → Slide Master) is the template slide — objects placed on it appear on every slide; ideal for logos; watermarks; or consistent design elements.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the SLIDE MASTER in PowerPoint?
options: The first slide of the presentation
A master template slide whose layout and objects are inherited by all slides — used for consistent logos; backgrounds; and fonts
explanation: The Slide Master controls the overall design: fonts; background; layout; and objects placed on it appear consistently on all slides that use that master.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT an AUDIO file into a PowerPoint slide; you go to?
options: Insert → Media → Audio → Audio on My PC
explanation: Insert → Media → Audio → Audio on My PC (or 'Audio on This PC') inserts a sound file; which can be set to play automatically or on click during the slide show.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What type of view would you use to QUICKLY REORDER multiple slides in PowerPoint?
explanation: Slide Sorter view displays all slides as thumbnails; making it simple to drag and drop slides to reorder them or delete multiple slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To DUPLICATE a slide (create an identical copy) in PowerPoint; you?
options: Right-click the slide thumbnail and choose 'Duplicate Slide'
explanation: Right-click → Duplicate Slide creates an identical copy of the selected slide immediately after it — a quick way to create slides with similar layouts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In PowerPoint; the 'MORPH' transition creates?
options: A smooth animated transition that morphs common objects between two slides — available in PowerPoint 2016+
explanation: Morph transition (PowerPoint 2016+) creates a smooth animation between slides that have the same or similar objects — useful for cinematic position and size changes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the STATUS BAR at the bottom of the PowerPoint window?
options: To show information such as current slide number; total slides; zoom level; and view buttons
explanation: The status bar displays contextual information — slide number (e.g. 'Slide 3 of 10'); language setting; zoom slider; and view shortcuts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the FONT of text in a PowerPoint text box; you first?
options: Select the text then use the Font dropdown in Home tab
explanation: Text must be selected first; then font changes (typeface; size; colour; bold; italic) are applied from the Font group in the Home tab.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does BOLD text formatting do in PowerPoint?
options: Makes text thicker and heavier for emphasis
explanation: Bold (Ctrl+B) makes the selected text thicker and darker — used to emphasise key words or headings.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does ITALIC text formatting do in PowerPoint?
options: Slants the text to the right for stylistic emphasis
explanation: Italic (Ctrl+I) slants the text — used for titles; terms; or light emphasis in presentation text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does UNDERLINE text formatting do in PowerPoint?
options: Draws a line under the text — often used for links or emphasis
explanation: Underline (Ctrl+U) draws a horizontal line beneath the selected text — used for links or emphasis.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To ALIGN text to the CENTRE of a text box in PowerPoint; you press?
explanation: Ctrl+E centres the selected text within its text box — the other alignment shortcuts are Ctrl+L (left); Ctrl+R (right); Ctrl+J (justify).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a PRESENTATION HANDOUT in PowerPoint?
options: Printed pages showing multiple slide thumbnails per page for the audience to keep
explanation: Handouts are printed pages showing 2; 3; 4; 6; or 9 slide thumbnails per page — printed via File → Print → Handouts for audience takeaways.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To PRINT a PowerPoint presentation as HANDOUTS (multiple slides per page); you go to?
options: File → Print → Settings → Full Page Slides → change to Handouts
explanation: In File → Print; click 'Full Page Slides' to open the print layout dropdown; then select a Handouts layout (e.g. '2 Slides'; '3 Slides'; etc.).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does SLIDE SHOW → REHEARSE TIMINGS do?
options: Records how long you spend on each slide during a practice run; so the presentation can run automatically at those timings
explanation: Rehearse Timings plays the slide show and records the time spent on each slide — you can save these timings for a self-running presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In PowerPoint; what is 'PRESENTER VIEW'?
options: A special display mode showing the current slide on one screen and speaker notes; next slide; and timer on the presenter's screen
explanation: Presenter View (available when connected to a projector) shows the current slide on the projector; while the presenter's laptop shows notes; the next slide; and an elapsed timer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT a HYPERLINK to a website in PowerPoint; you select text or an object then?
options: Go to Insert → Links → Hyperlink (or press Ctrl+K)
explanation: Insert → Links → Hyperlink (Ctrl+K) opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog where you enter the destination URL or select a slide within the presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'APPLY TO ALL' button do in the Background Formatting pane?
options: Applies only to the selected slide
Applies the chosen background to every slide in the presentation
explanation: 'Apply to All' in the Format Background pane replaces the background of all slides simultaneously with the selected fill; gradient; picture; or pattern.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of ANIMATIONS in a presentation?
options: To make objects on a slide appear; disappear; or move to draw the audience's attention or reveal content step by step
explanation: Animations control when and how individual objects (text; images; shapes) appear or move on a slide — helping control the flow of information during a presentation.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an ENTRANCE animation in PowerPoint?
options: How a slide transitions to the next
How an object APPEARS on a slide (e.g. Fly In; Fade; Bounce)
How an object leaves the slide
How an object moves across the slide
explanation: Entrance animations control how objects enter or appear on a slide — examples include Appear; Fade; Fly In; Zoom; Bounce.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an EXIT animation in PowerPoint?
options: How an object APPEARS on a slide
How an object DISAPPEARS from a slide (e.g. Fly Out; Fade Out)
explanation: Exit animations control how objects leave or disappear from a slide — examples include Disappear; Fade; Fly Out; Float Out.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is an EMPHASIS animation in PowerPoint?
options: An animation that draws ATTENTION to an object already visible (e.g. Pulse; Spin; Grow/Shrink)
explanation: Emphasis animations apply to objects that are already visible — they highlight or draw attention without the object leaving the slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the ANIMATION PANE in PowerPoint show?

explanation: The Animation Pane (Animations → Advanced Animation → Animation Pane) lists all animation effects on the slide; their order; duration; trigger; and allows reordering.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the correct order for setting up a CUSTOM ANIMATION sequence?
options: Select the object; choose animation type; then set trigger and timing
Choose timing first; then select object
Select the slide then choose timing
Open the Design tab then pick a sound
explanation: Adding an animation: select the object on the slide; then in the Animations tab choose an animation; then set its duration; delay; and trigger order.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'DESIGN → Variants' section in PowerPoint allow?
options: Applying colour; font; effect; and background variations of the current theme without switching themes
explanation: The Variants gallery in the Design tab shows colour; font; effect; and background variations of the active theme — click one to update all slides to that variant.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To move an IMAGE to a specific position on a slide precisely; you can?
options: Right-click → Format Picture → Position; or use the X and Y position fields in Drawing Tools → Format → Size tab
explanation: For precise positioning; right-click → Format Picture → Position (or Drawing Tools → Format → Size group) lets you type exact horizontal and vertical coordinates.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the 'ALT TEXT' feature for images in PowerPoint?
options: To add a text description for screen-reader accessibility or when the image does not load
explanation: Alt text (Alternative Text) — set via right-click → Edit Alt Text — provides a text description of an image for screen readers (accessibility) or when images cannot display.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To CROP an image in PowerPoint (remove parts of the edges)?
options: Select the image → Picture Tools Format → Crop; then drag the crop handles
explanation: Crop (Picture Tools Format → Size → Crop) allows trimming the edges of an image by dragging the black crop handles that appear around the picture.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'PICTURE STYLES' in Picture Tools Format provide?
options: Pre-designed frame; shadow; and reflection effects that can be applied to a selected image in one click
explanation: Picture Styles (Picture Tools → Format → Picture Styles gallery) offer pre-set combinations of borders; shadows; and effects (e.g. rounded corners; drop shadow; reflection) for images.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the COLOR option in Picture Tools → Format → Adjust?
options: To adjust the image's colour saturation; colour tone; or recolour it with a solid tint
explanation: Picture Color adjustments allow changing colour saturation (vivid vs. washed); colour tone (cool vs. warm); or recolouring the image (e.g. grayscale; sepia; or a single tint colour).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT a TEXT BOX anywhere on a PowerPoint slide (outside a placeholder)?
options: Insert → Text → Text Box; then draw it on the slide
explanation: Insert → Text → Text Box lets you draw a free-floating text container anywhere on the slide — useful for labels; captions; or annotations outside the layout placeholders.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does CTRL+M do in PowerPoint?
explanation: Ctrl+M inserts a new slide after the currently selected slide in PowerPoint.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To UNDO multiple actions in PowerPoint; you?
options: Press Ctrl+Z repeatedly; or click the Undo dropdown arrow (next to the undo button on the Quick Access Toolbar) to undo several actions at once
explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes one action per press; the Undo dropdown lets you step back multiple actions at once — e.g. undoing the last 10 operations simultaneously.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does CTRL+Y do in PowerPoint?
options: REDO — re-applies the last undone action
explanation: Ctrl+Y redo redoes the most recently undone action — the opposite of Ctrl+Z.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What format should you save a PowerPoint presentation in to make it UNEDITABLE and viewable only as a slide show?
options: ppsx (PowerPoint Show) — opens directly in Slide Show mode and cannot be easily edited
explanation: Saving as .ppsx (PowerPoint Show) opens the file directly in full-screen slide show mode; preventing casual editing — useful for distributing finished presentations.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To export a PowerPoint presentation as a PDF; you go to?
explanation: File → Export → Create PDF/XPS Document converts the presentation to PDF; making it readable without PowerPoint and fixed in its layout.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In PowerPoint; what does the 'ANIMATION PAINTER' tool do?
options: Copies ALL animation effects from one object and applies them to another object
explanation: Animation Painter (Animations → Advanced Animation → Animation Painter) is similar to Format Painter for animations — click a source object; then click a target object to copy all its animations.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the SLIDE LAYOUT 'BLANK' mean?
options: A completely empty slide with no placeholders — the presenter adds all content freely
explanation: The Blank layout has no placeholders — all content must be added manually using text boxes; shapes; or images; giving complete design freedom.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the 'HIDE SLIDE' feature in PowerPoint do?
options: Keeps the slide in the file but skips it during the slide show — useful for backup slides
Moves the slide to the end
explanation: Right-click → Hide Slide marks the slide so it is not shown in the normal presentation flow — it can be revealed by pressing its slide number during the show.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'APPLY TO ALL SLIDES' do in the Header and Footer dialog?
options: Applies slide numbers; date; and footer text to every slide in the presentation
explanation: 'Apply to All' in the Header and Footer dialog adds the configured footer; date; and slide number to every slide — as opposed to 'Apply' which adds it only to the current slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 8; the main topic is?
options: An introduction to Microsoft PowerPoint — creating; editing; and formatting a basic presentation
explanation: Chapter 8 of Terabytes Book 4 introduces Microsoft PowerPoint — the PowerPoint window; creating slides; inserting text and images; and basic formatting and views.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student has 10 slides and wants slide 5 to come after slide 3. The EASIEST way in PowerPoint is?
options: Delete slide 5 and retype it after slide 3
In Slide Sorter View; drag slide 5 between slides 3 and 4
explanation: In Slide Sorter view; slides can be dragged and dropped to any position — the simplest way to reorder non-adjacent slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a GRADIENT background to a slide in PowerPoint; you?
options: Design → Format Background → Gradient Fill; set colours and direction; then Apply (or Apply to All)
explanation: Design → Format Background → Gradient Fill lets you choose a start colour; end colour; gradient type; and direction for the background.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To DUPLICATE a slide in PowerPoint (create an exact copy); you?
options: Right-click the slide thumbnail → Duplicate Slide
explanation: Right-click → Duplicate Slide (or Home → New Slide dropdown → Duplicate Selected Slides) creates a copy of the selected slide immediately after it.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the difference between 'New Slide' and 'Duplicate Slide' in PowerPoint?
options: New Slide inserts an empty slide with a chosen layout; Duplicate Slide creates an exact copy of the selected slide including its content
Duplicate Slide is found in the Insert tab
explanation: New Slide adds an empty slide; Duplicate Slide replicates the current slide's layout; text; images; and formatting — saving time when slides share the same design.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To INSERT SMARTART into a PowerPoint slide; you go to?
explanation: Insert → Illustrations → SmartArt opens the Choose a SmartArt Graphic dialog; where you select a category and layout.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category in PowerPoint shows STEPS IN A PROCESS in sequence?
explanation: Process diagrams show sequential steps — examples include 'Basic Process'; 'Chevron Process'; and 'Circular Bending Process' layouts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category shows a REPEATING LOOP or continuous cycle of events?
explanation: Cycle diagrams (e.g. Basic Cycle; Radial Cycle) show recurring or continuous processes — perfect for water cycle; seasons; or recurring business processes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category shows a TREE STRUCTURE or organisational chart?
explanation: Hierarchy layouts (e.g. Organisation Chart; Table Hierarchy) show parent-child relationships; reporting lines; or classification trees.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category is BEST for a simple BULLETED LIST of items with equal weight?
explanation: List layouts display items without implying sequence or hierarchy — examples include 'Vertical Box List'; 'Horizontal Bullet List'; and 'Stacked List'.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category shows PROPORTIONAL or FOUNDATIONAL relationships in a triangular shape?
explanation: Pyramid diagrams (e.g. Basic Pyramid) show items in proportion or in a foundational layered structure — like Maslow's hierarchy of needs.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category shows the RELATIONSHIP or OVERLAP between ideas (e.g. Venn diagram)?
explanation: Relationship layouts include Venn; counterbalance arrows; and convergent diagrams that show how ideas intersect; balance; or relate.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category displays items in a TWO-AXIS GRID (four quadrants)?
explanation: Matrix layouts display items in a 2×2 (or similar) grid showing the relationship of each item to two axes — useful for risk grids or classification frameworks.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which SmartArt category includes layouts that COMBINE IMAGES with explanatory text labels?
explanation: Picture layouts are SmartArt diagrams specifically designed to show images alongside captions or text — useful for photo galleries or illustrated steps.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: How many SmartArt categories are available in Microsoft PowerPoint (2016)?
explanation: There are 8 SmartArt categories: List; Process; Cycle; Hierarchy; Relationship; Matrix; Pyramid; and Picture.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What keyboard shortcut starts a PowerPoint slide show FROM THE BEGINNING?
explanation: F5 starts the Slide Show from slide 1; regardless of which slide is currently selected.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What keyboard shortcut starts the PowerPoint slide show FROM THE CURRENT SLIDE?
explanation: Shift+F5 starts the slide show from the currently selected slide — useful for testing a specific section without going through the whole presentation from the start.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: PowerPoint has FOUR main views. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
explanation: Print Preview is not a separate view in PowerPoint — it is accessed through File → Print. The four main views are Normal; Outline/Notes Page; Slide Sorter; and Reading/Slide Show.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which PowerPoint view is BEST for EDITING a single slide in detail?
explanation: Normal View provides the largest editing area with the slide at the centre; surrounded by the Slides pane and Notes pane — ideal for detailed editing.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which PowerPoint view is BEST for REORDERING many slides quickly?
explanation: Slide Sorter View shows all slides as thumbnails in a grid; making drag-and-drop reordering fast and visual.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which PowerPoint view shows the full slide show playing INSIDE the PowerPoint window (without hiding the taskbar)?
explanation: Reading View plays the presentation as a full-window slide show inside PowerPoint (not full screen) — good for personal review without covering the taskbar.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which PowerPoint view shows the printed version of a slide with speaker notes BELOW each slide image?
explanation: Notes Page View (View → Presentation Views → Notes Page) displays each slide reduced at the top and the full notes text below — like a printout of the speaker notes.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: During a presentation; to go to a specific slide by number; you press?
options: The slide's number followed by Enter
explanation: During a Slide Show; typing a slide number (e.g. '5') and pressing Enter jumps directly to that slide — useful for navigating without going through earlier slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does PRESSING 'B' during a PowerPoint slide show do?
options: Blanks the screen to BLACK to pause the audience's attention
explanation: Pressing 'B' during a slide show blacks out the screen — pressing 'B' again (or any key) restores the current slide; useful for pausing and focusing discussion.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does PRESSING 'W' during a PowerPoint slide show do?
explanation: Pressing 'W' during a slide show whitens the screen — a white blank; compared to 'B' for black; pressing 'W' again returns to the slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To print a PowerPoint presentation as NOTES PAGES (each slide with its notes below); you go to?
options: File → Print → change 'Full Page Slides' to 'Notes Pages'
explanation: In File → Print; clicking 'Full Page Slides' opens the print layout options; where selecting 'Notes Pages' prints each slide with its notes below.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To print only the TEXT OUTLINE of a presentation (no slide images); you choose?
explanation: File → Print → Print Layout → Outline prints only the text content of each slide's placeholders as a text outline — no images or backgrounds.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: When printing a PowerPoint presentation; what does 'FRAME SLIDES' option do?
options: Adds a thin rectangular border around each printed slide image
explanation: The 'Frame Slides' checkbox in File → Print → Settings adds a thin border/frame around each slide thumbnail on the printed page.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To SET UP a LOOPING (auto-repeating) presentation in PowerPoint; you go to?
options: Slide Show → Set Up Slide Show → check 'Loop continuously until Esc'
explanation: Slide Show → Set Up Slide Show → 'Loop continuously until Esc' makes the presentation automatically restart from slide 1 when the last slide is reached — used for kiosks.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In PowerPoint; what is the THEME COLOUR and THEME FONT?
options: A coordinated set of colours and fonts defined in the theme that apply consistently across all slides — changeable from Design → Variants
The default black and white colours
The font used in the Notes pane
explanation: Theme colours and fonts are part of the Design theme — they apply to all text; shapes; SmartArt; and charts on all slides; changed via Design → Variants → Colors or Fonts.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of SLIDE TRANSITIONS in a presentation?
options: To animate objects on a slide
To create a visual effect when moving from one slide to the next; making the show flow more smoothly
explanation: Slide transitions (e.g. Fade; Push; Wipe; Reveal; Morph) play between slides to smooth the flow — configured in the Transitions tab.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a KIOSK presentation in PowerPoint?
options: A self-running; looping presentation designed to run unattended (e.g. at an exhibition or reception desk)
explanation: A kiosk presentation is set up via Slide Show → Set Up Slide Show → 'Browsed at a kiosk (full screen)' with auto-advance timings — it loops without a presenter.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the MORPH TRANSITION require to work properly?
options: Two consecutive slides that contain MATCHING OBJECTS (same name or content) that PowerPoint can animate between positions/sizes
explanation: Morph analyses objects across two slides and smoothly animates changes in position; size; colour; or rotation of matching objects — requiring the same objects on both slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To CHANGE THE COLOUR of a SmartArt graphic in PowerPoint; you use?
explanation: SmartArt Tools Design → Change Colors (shown when SmartArt is selected) provides pre-set colour combinations that use the presentation's theme colours.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the OVERALL STYLE (flat vs 3D) of a SmartArt graphic; you use?
options: SmartArt Tools → Design → SmartArt Styles gallery
explanation: The SmartArt Styles gallery (SmartArt Tools Design) shows flat and three-dimensional style options for the selected SmartArt graphic.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To ADD MORE SHAPES to an existing SmartArt in PowerPoint; you?
options: Click an existing shape → SmartArt Tools Design → Add Shape; or press Enter in the Text pane
explanation: SmartArt Tools Design → Add Shape adds a shape at the same level (after; before; above; or below) the selected shape.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the TEXT PANE in SmartArt?
options: A text box on the slide
A panel (opened by clicking the small arrow on the left edge of the SmartArt) where you type content for each shape
explanation: The Text pane in SmartArt shows all content as a bulleted outline — type here to populate the shapes; and indent/outdent to set hierarchy levels.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To REORDER SLIDES quickly using the keyboard in Normal View; you?
options: Drag thumbnails in the Slides pane or cut (Ctrl+X) a slide and paste (Ctrl+V) it at the new location
explanation: In the Slides pane; you can drag thumbnail images to reorder; or cut a slide and paste it elsewhere — both work in Normal view.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 9; students learn to DESIGN a presentation using which advanced PowerPoint features?
options: SmartArt graphics; Duplicate Slide; slide views; and printing options
explanation: Chapter 9 covers advanced design skills: inserting SmartArt; using Duplicate Slide; understanding the four slide views; and printing options.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'APPLY TO ALL' mean in the Transitions tab?
options: Applies only to the last slide
Applies the selected transition to EVERY slide in the presentation
explanation: 'Apply to All' in the Transitions tab sets the same transition for every slide at once — saving the effort of applying it slide by slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which printing option in PowerPoint prints 3 slides per page WITH lines for notes on the right?
explanation: The '3 Slides' Handout layout is unique in that it prints three slide thumbnails on the left with three ruled lines on the right — commonly used for audience note-taking.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the SLIDE SHOW → HIDE SLIDE feature?
options: Marks the slide to be skipped during the slide show while keeping it in the file
Changes the slide's background to white
Moves the slide to the end
explanation: Hidden slides are visible in editing views (shown with a strikethrough slide number in Slide Sorter) but are skipped during a normal slide show — revealed on demand by pressing the slide number.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To EDIT the text inside a SmartArt shape directly; you?
options: Double-click the SmartArt shape to enter it; then click the specific shape and type
explanation: Double-clicking a SmartArt enters edit mode; single-click selects the whole SmartArt; another click selects an individual shape; then typing replaces or adds text.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student inserts a SmartArt 'Basic Cycle' with 5 shapes but needs 6. She should?
options: Click any shape in the cycle → SmartArt Tools Design → Add Shape → Add Shape After
explanation: Add Shape After (or Before) in SmartArt Tools Design adds a new shape at the selected position — for a Cycle; this inserts a new stage in the loop.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of 'PROMOTE' and 'DEMOTE' in the SmartArt Text Pane?
options: Move text left (higher level) or right (lower level indented) in the SmartArt hierarchy
Move a shape up or down
explanation: Promote (Shift+Tab) moves an item up one level (less indented; higher hierarchy); Demote (Tab) moves it down one level — adjusting its position in the SmartArt structure.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does PRINT → SCALE TO FIT PAPER do in PowerPoint?
options: Scales the printed slides to fill the paper size as large as possible
explanation: Scale to Fit Paper fits each slide to the full printable area of the page — useful when the slide's aspect ratio doesn't match the paper size.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To add a WATERMARK (e.g. 'DRAFT') to every slide; the best method is?
options: Add a text box on each slide separately
Insert a text box on the SLIDE MASTER so it appears on all slides automatically
explanation: Adding a semi-transparent text box (e.g. 'DRAFT') on the Slide Master means it appears on every slide based on that master — a change to one updates all.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student has created a 20-slide presentation and wants slides 5-10 to use a different background from the rest. She should?
options: Select slides 5-10 in the Slide Sorter; Design → Format Background → choose background → 'Apply' (not Apply to All)
explanation: Selecting specific slides first then using Design → Format Background → Apply applies the custom background ONLY to those selected slides; leaving all others unchanged.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the SELECTION PANE in PowerPoint?
options: A panel (Home → Editing → Select → Selection Pane) listing all objects on the current slide; allowing them to be selected; renamed; hidden; or reordered
explanation: The Selection Pane (Home → Editing → Select → Selection Pane) lists every object on the slide by name — useful for selecting hidden objects; renaming for animation; or reordering the stacking layer.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Terabytes Book 4 Chapter 9; students are taught to use DUPLICATE SLIDE. What is the main ADVANTAGE of duplicating a slide?
options: It copies the slide's layout; formatting; and content exactly — saving the time of recreating a similar slide from scratch
explanation: Duplicating a slide is a productivity technique — if multiple slides share a format or background; duplicate one and change only the specific content.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the ORDER of SmartArt items using the SmartArt Text pane; you?
options: Retype the items in the new order
Use SmartArt Tools Design → Move Up / Move Down to reorder items
explanation: Move Up and Move Down buttons in SmartArt Tools Design reorder the selected shape within the SmartArt without retyping content.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'SAVE AS' (Ctrl+Shift+S or File → Save As) do in PowerPoint compared to 'Save' (Ctrl+S)?
options: Save As saves a copy under a new name or location; Save overwrites the existing file — Save As is used to create a new version or change format
Save is for images; Save As is for text
explanation: Ctrl+S saves to the existing file; Ctrl+Shift+S (or File → Save As) opens a dialog to save a copy with a new name; location; or format — useful for versioning (e.g. Final_v2.pptx).
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To VIEW ALL SLIDES as thumbnails AND rearrange them in PowerPoint; which VIEW do you use?
explanation: Slide Sorter View is the dedicated view for managing all slides simultaneously — drag thumbnails to reorder; right-click to delete; or select multiple and apply transitions.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student's presentation auto-advances too quickly. To FIX THIS; she should go to?
options: Transitions tab → change the 'After' time (advance slide timing) or untick 'After' to return to manual click advance
explanation: The Transitions tab's Advance Slide section controls automatic timing — change the 'After' value (e.g. from 2 seconds to 5 seconds) or untick it to require a click.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To change the COLOUR THEME of a SmartArt to match your presentation's accent colour; you click the SmartArt then?
options: SmartArt Tools → Design → Change Colors; then pick a colour set
explanation: With the SmartArt selected; SmartArt Tools Design → Change Colors shows grouped colour sets (Colourful; Accent 1; Accent 2; etc.) — choosing one recolours all shapes using the theme palette.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is a SECTION in PowerPoint?
options: A named group of slides that helps organise a large presentation (e.g. 'Introduction'; 'Main Content'; 'Conclusion')
explanation: Sections group related slides with a label — visible in Normal and Slide Sorter views — helping navigate and manage large presentations with dozens of slides.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To ADD A SECTION in PowerPoint; you right-click between slides in the Slides pane and choose?
explanation: Right-click between two slides in the Slides pane → Add Section; then name the section — slides following the marker belong to that section.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'COLLAPSE ALL' for sections in PowerPoint do?
options: Hides all slides from view permanently
Collapses each section to show only the section header; hiding the slide thumbnails — making it easier to navigate a large presentation
explanation: Collapsing sections (right-click section bar → Collapse All) temporarily hides slides; showing only section names for high-level navigation — click the arrow to expand.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the TELL ME WHAT YOU WANT TO DO search box (the light bulb icon) in PowerPoint 2016?
options: To search for PowerPoint commands and features by typing a keyword — guiding you to the right tool quickly
explanation: The 'Tell me' box (Alt+Q) is a command search for PowerPoint — type 'insert table' or 'change animation' and it shows relevant commands; links to Help; or executes the command.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: Which KEYBOARD SHORTCUT opens the Format Shape (or Format Picture) pane in PowerPoint?
explanation: Double-clicking a shape opens the Format Shape pane directly; showing Fill; Line; Effects; and Size & Properties sections for detailed formatting.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'RESET GRAPHIC' in SmartArt Tools → Design do?
options: Reverts all manual formatting changes (moved shapes; colour overrides; effects) back to the original SmartArt layout style
explanation: Reset Graphic undoes all customisations made to a SmartArt graphic; reverting it to its initial style and layout — useful if formatting gets messy.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To CONVERT SmartArt to REGULAR SHAPES (editable individually) in PowerPoint?
options: Right-click the SmartArt → Convert → Convert to Shapes
explanation: Right-click SmartArt → Convert → Convert to Shapes breaks the SmartArt into a grouped set of regular drawing shapes that can each be moved; resized; and formatted independently.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'GROUP' do to multiple selected objects in PowerPoint?
options: Moves them all to the back
Combines them into a single unit so they can be moved; resized; and formatted together
explanation: Group (Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange → Group; or right-click → Group) combines multiple objects so they behave as one unit — maintain their relative positions when moved.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: To UNGROUP grouped objects in PowerPoint; you?
options: Right-click the group → Ungroup; or Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange → Ungroup
explanation: Ungroup separates previously grouped objects back into individual items; allowing each to be edited independently — access via right-click → Ungroup or the Arrange menu.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What is the ALIGN function under Drawing Tools → Format → Arrange used for?
options: Precisely aligning selected objects to each other or to the slide (e.g. Align Left; Align Top; Distribute Horizontally)
explanation: Align tools position multiple objects neatly — e.g. 'Align Left' snaps all selected objects to the leftmost object's edge; 'Distribute Horizontally' spaces them evenly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: A student adds 8 slides to her presentation and wants slides 1-3 as 'Introduction' and slides 4-8 as 'Main'. She should use?
options: Sections — right-click between slide 3 and 4 in the Slides pane → Add Section; name each section
explanation: Adding sections between slide 3 and 4 creates two labelled groups (Introduction; Main) making the presentation easier to navigate and manage.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does 'ZOOM' in PowerPoint allow? (Slide Show → Zoom)
options: Changes the zoom level of the editing view
Inserts an interactive zoom summary slide — clicking a section thumbnail zooms into those slides during the slide show
explanation: Zoom (Slide Show → Zoom; or Insert → Zoom) creates an interactive navigation slide that zooms into any section when clicked — a dynamic alternative to a static agenda slide.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: What does the EYEDROPPER tool in PowerPoint allow?
options: Sampling an exact colour from anywhere on the slide and applying it to a shape's fill or outline
explanation: The Eyedropper (in Shape Fill → More Fill Colors → Eyedropper; or font color picker) samples any pixel colour on screen and applies it — useful for matching colours exactly.
subject: Grade 4 Computing

text: In Book 4 Chapter 9; a student creates a 'Computer History' presentation. To show events in ORDER; the BEST SmartArt category is?
