subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the term for the process of retrieving (copying) data from storage into RAM for the CPU to process?
options: Loading (opening a file loads it from secondary storage into primary memory/RAM)
explanation: Loading a file or program means copying it from secondary storage (HDD; USB; SSD) into RAM (primary memory) where the CPU can directly access and process it.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Microsoft Word 2016; which TAB contains the command to insert a table?
explanation: Tables are inserted from the INSERT tab in Word 2016 — click Insert → Table to see the grid and dropdown options for creating a table.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a TABLE in Microsoft Word?
options: A grid of ROWS and COLUMNS used to organise and present data in a structured format
explanation: A table in Word is a grid made of rows (horizontal) and columns (vertical) — their intersections form CELLS where you type data. Tables help present structured information clearly.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a CELL in a Word table?
options: The intersection of one ROW and one COLUMN — the individual box where you enter data
explanation: A cell is the individual box formed where a row and column meet. You type text; numbers; or insert images into cells. Each cell can be individually formatted.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a ROW in a Word table?
options: A vertical division of the table
A HORIZONTAL division of the table — runs left to right across the page
explanation: A row runs horizontally (left to right) across the table. You add new rows when you need more entries. Word tables typically have one header row and multiple data rows.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a COLUMN in a Word table?
options: A horizontal division of the table
A VERTICAL division of the table — runs top to bottom
explanation: A column runs vertically (top to bottom). Columns typically hold one category of information (e.g. a 'Name' column or a 'Price' column).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: Book 5 teaches THREE methods to insert a table in Word. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
options: Using the Insert Table grid (drag to select rows and columns)
Insert → Table → Insert Table (dialog box method)
Drawing a table freehand (Insert → Table → Draw Table)
Copy-pasting a table from a website
explanation: The three methods taught in Book 5 are: (1) grid drag method; (2) Insert Table dialog box; (3) Draw Table. Copy-pasting from a website is not a structured Word insertion method.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To insert a table using the GRID METHOD in Word 2016; you?
options: Click Insert → Table; then hover over the grid to highlight the number of rows and columns you want; then click
explanation: The grid method: Insert tab → Table → hover over the grid squares until the desired rows×columns are highlighted (e.g. 3×4) → click to insert the table instantly.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the INSERT TABLE DIALOG BOX method; you specify?
options: The exact number of columns and rows; plus AutoFit behaviour (Fixed column width; AutoFit to contents; AutoFit to window)
explanation: The Insert Table dialog box lets you set precise numbers of columns and rows; plus AutoFit options: Fixed width (exact pixel width); AutoFit to contents (columns auto-size to text); AutoFit to window (stretches to page margins).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the DRAW TABLE method allow you to do?
options: Draw an irregular table with non-uniform rows and columns by dragging a pencil cursor
explanation: Draw Table (Insert → Table → Draw Table) turns the cursor into a pencil — you draw the outer border; then draw lines inside to create rows and columns. Useful for complex; non-uniform layouts.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To NAVIGATE between cells in a Word table; you press?
options: Tab (to move to the next cell; Shift+Tab to move to the previous cell)
explanation: Tab key moves the cursor to the NEXT cell (right; or down to the first cell of the next row). Shift+Tab moves to the PREVIOUS cell. Tab in the last cell of a row moves to the first cell of the next row.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: If you press TAB when the cursor is in the LAST CELL of the last row; what happens?
options: The cursor jumps to the first cell of the table
A NEW ROW is automatically added at the bottom of the table
explanation: Pressing Tab in the very last cell of the last row adds a new empty row at the bottom — allowing you to keep adding rows without using the menu.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To MERGE two or more cells in a Word table; you?
options: Select the cells; then right-click → Merge Cells (or Table Tools Layout → Merge Cells)
explanation: Select the cells to merge → right-click → Merge Cells OR go to Table Tools → Layout tab → Merge group → Merge Cells. This combines the selected cells into one larger cell.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of MERGING cells in a Word table?
options: To combine multiple cells into one — useful for creating header cells that span multiple columns (e.g. a title row spanning all columns)
explanation: Merging creates a single larger cell from multiple cells — commonly used for header rows that span the full table width; or for cells that group related data under one label.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of SPLITTING a cell in a Word table?
options: To divide ONE cell into MULTIPLE smaller cells (specify the number of rows and columns to split into)
explanation: Splitting (Table Tools → Layout → Split Cells) divides a single cell into multiple rows and/or columns — the reverse of merging.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To SPLIT A TABLE into two separate tables in Word?
options: Click in the row that should become the first row of the second table; then Table Tools → Layout → Split Table
explanation: Split Table (Table Tools → Layout → Split Table) divides the table at the selected row — the row where your cursor is becomes the first row of the new second table.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What are TABLE TOOLS in Word 2016?
options: Menu items that appear at all times
Two contextual tabs (DESIGN and LAYOUT) that appear in the ribbon only when the cursor is inside a table
explanation: When you click inside a table; Table Tools appear in the ribbon — two extra tabs: DESIGN (for styles; borders; shading) and LAYOUT (for rows/columns; merge/split; alignment; cell size).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: The TABLE TOOLS DESIGN tab contains options for?
options: TABLE STYLES (pre-designed colour/border combinations); borders; and cell shading
explanation: Table Tools Design tab contains: Table Styles gallery (pre-designed formatted table looks); Table Style Options (header row; banded rows; etc.); and Borders & Shading controls.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: The TABLE TOOLS LAYOUT tab contains options for?
options: Rows & Columns management (insert/delete); Merge & Split; Cell Size; Alignment; and Data (sort; formula)
explanation: Table Tools Layout tab handles structural changes: inserting/deleting rows and columns; merging/splitting cells; setting cell height and width; aligning cell content; and data operations like sorting.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a TABLE STYLE in Word?
options: A pre-designed combination of colours; borders; and shading that can be applied to a table with one click
A type of table (e.g. data table vs. calendar)
A way to sort table data
explanation: Table styles (in Table Tools Design) are pre-built formatting packages — colour schemes for header rows; banded rows; borders — applied in one click to give the table a professional look.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT A ROW ABOVE the current row; you go to?
options: Table Tools Layout → Rows & Columns → Insert Above
Press Enter in the cell above
explanation: Table Tools → Layout tab → Rows & Columns group → 'Insert Above' inserts a new empty row above the row where your cursor is.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT A COLUMN TO THE LEFT of the current column in Word?
options: Table Tools Layout → Rows & Columns → Insert Left
explanation: Table Tools → Layout tab → Rows & Columns → 'Insert Left' inserts a new empty column to the left of the column where your cursor is positioned.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To DELETE an entire ROW from a Word table?
options: Select the row; then Table Tools Layout → Rows & Columns → Delete → Delete Rows
explanation: Select any cell in the row (or the whole row) → Table Tools Layout → Delete → Delete Rows. Or right-click the row → Delete Rows.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'HEADER ROW' checkbox do in Table Tools Design → Table Style Options?
options: Applies special formatting (bold; contrasting colour) to the first row to indicate it is the header — containing column labels
Adds a border above the table
explanation: The Header Row checkbox applies a distinct style to the first row (usually bold text with a contrasting background colour) to show it contains column headings rather than data.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'BANDED ROWS' mean in a Word table style?
options: Alternating shading on odd and even rows — making it easier to read across long rows without losing your place
explanation: Banded rows alternate between two background colours (e.g. white and light grey) for odd and even rows — a classic design feature for readability in data tables.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To ALIGN TEXT in the centre of a table cell BOTH horizontally and vertically in Word?
options: Table Tools Layout → Alignment group → Align Center (Centre text both horizontally and vertically)
explanation: Table Tools Layout → Alignment group has 9 alignment buttons for all combinations of horizontal (Left; Centre; Right) and vertical (Top; Middle; Bottom) alignment. 'Align Center' centres both ways.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the CELL MARGIN in a Word table?
options: The width of the table border
The space between the cell border and the text inside the cell — affects readability
explanation: Cell margins are the gaps between the cell's border and its content. Larger margins make text less cramped. Set via Table Tools → Layout → Table group → Cell Margins (or Table Properties).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To make all COLUMNS IN A TABLE the same width automatically in Word?
options: Table Tools Layout → Cell Size group → Distribute Columns (evenly distributes available width across all columns)
explanation: Distribute Columns (Table Tools Layout → Cell Size → Distribute Columns) makes all selected columns equal width — a quick way to normalise column widths after manual adjustments.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To SORT DATA in a Word table alphabetically by the first column?
options: Table Tools Layout → Data group → Sort (choose the column and order — ascending or descending)
explanation: Sort (Table Tools Layout → Data → Sort) opens a dialog to sort table rows by one or more columns; in ascending (A→Z; 1→10) or descending order. Useful for alphabetical lists or ranked data.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the CONVERT TEXT TO TABLE function do?
options: Converts a table to plain text
Converts separated text (e.g. comma-separated or tab-separated) into a formatted Word table automatically
explanation: Insert → Table → Convert Text to Table reads delimited text (commas; tabs; or custom separator) and converts each delimited section into a table cell — useful for turning CSV or tabbed lists into tables.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What tab and section in Book 5 teaches students to add BORDERS and SHADING to a table?
options: Table Tools Design tab — Borders dropdown and Shading dropdown in the Table Styles section
explanation: Table Tools → Design tab has Borders (choose border type; thickness; colour) and Shading (fill cell backgrounds with a colour) — letting students customise how the table looks.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student creates a 3×4 table. How many CELLS does it have total?
explanation: A 3-column × 4-row table has 3 × 4 = 12 cells. Each row has 3 cells; 4 rows × 3 = 12 cells total.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To change the BORDER COLOUR of a table in Word?
options: Table Tools Design → Borders → Border Color; then draw or apply to selected borders
explanation: Table Tools Design → Borders dropdown → Border Color opens a colour picker; then the Pen Color button turns the cursor into a pen to redraw borders in the chosen colour.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the ERASER tool in Draw Table mode?
options: To erase (remove) individual border lines inside the table; effectively merging the cells separated by that line
explanation: The Eraser (in Draw Table mode) removes individual border lines — clicking a line removes it and merges the cells on either side; a quick alternative to using Merge Cells.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: How do you SELECT AN ENTIRE TABLE in Word?
options: Click the table MOVE handle (a four-headed arrow icon that appears at the top-left corner of the table when you hover over it)
explanation: The table move handle (⊹) appears at the table's top-left corner when you hover — clicking it selects the entire table. You can then format; move; or delete the whole table at once.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of HEADER ROW in a large table that spans multiple pages?
options: To REPEAT the header row at the top of each page if the table runs onto multiple pages (Table Tools Layout → Data → Repeat Header Rows)
explanation: In a long table that spans pages; Repeat Header Rows (Table Tools Layout → Data → Repeat Header Rows) makes the header row print/display at the top of each page — maintaining readability.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: When you move the cursor OVER A TABLE in Word 2016; which icon appears at the top-LEFT corner?
options: A move handle (four-headed arrow ✥) — clicking it selects the whole table; dragging it moves the table
explanation: The move handle (✥) at the top-left corner appears when hovering — click to select the whole table; drag to move it anywhere on the page.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the FORMULA function in Word tables (Table Tools → Layout → Data → Formula)?
options: To perform simple calculations (SUM; AVERAGE; etc.) on values in table cells — similar to basic spreadsheet functions
explanation: Word tables support basic formulas using cell references (like =SUM(ABOVE)) — though this is simpler than Excel; it lets you calculate totals directly in Word tables.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: Which TABLE STYLE OPTION adds special formatting to the LAST ROW of a table?
options: Total Row (often bold; with a top border; to highlight a summary/total row at the bottom)
explanation: The Total Row option applies distinct formatting to the last row — typically bold text and a contrasting colour — to highlight it as a summary or total row.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the DEFAULT TABLE BORDER STYLE when you first insert a table in Word?
options: Thin single-line black borders on all cells
explanation: By default; Word inserts a table with thin single-line black borders on all sides and between all cells — visible in both the Normal and Print Layout views.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To CONVERT an existing Word table into PLAIN TEXT?
options: Table Tools Layout → Data → Convert to Text (choose a separator — tabs; commas; etc.)
explanation: Convert to Text (Table Tools Layout → Data → Convert to Text) turns the table back into plain text; with cell content separated by tabs; commas; or paragraph marks as chosen.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student wants to create a school TIMETABLE in Word. Which of the following would be MOST appropriate?
options: A table — with days of the week as column headers and periods/times as row headers
explanation: A table is ideal for a timetable — columns for days (Mon-Fri); rows for periods (Period 1; Period 2; etc.); cells for subjects. This presents the structured data clearly and is easy to read.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What KEYBOARD SHORTCUT inserts a TAB CHARACTER inside a table cell (rather than moving to the next cell)?
options: Ctrl+Tab (inserts a tab inside the cell without moving to the next cell)
explanation: In a table cell; pressing Tab moves to the NEXT cell. To insert an actual tab character WITHIN a cell; press Ctrl+Tab.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To add SHADING (background colour) to selected cells in a Word table?
options: Table Tools Design → Table Styles → Shading dropdown — choose a colour to fill the cell background
explanation: Shading (Table Tools Design → Shading dropdown or right-click → Table Properties → Shading) fills selected cells with a background colour — useful for highlighting header rows or colour-coding data.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'FIRST COLUMN' checkbox do in Table Style Options?
options: Applies special bold or contrasting formatting to the first column — useful when the first column acts as row labels
Merges all cells in the first column
explanation: The First Column option formats the first column with bold text or a contrasting style — ideal when the first column contains row labels or categories (e.g. time slots in a timetable).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student has a table with 5 rows and 3 columns. She merges the 3 cells in the top row to make a title. How many cells does the table now have?
explanation: Originally 5 × 3 = 15 cells. Merging 3 cells in the top row into 1 reduces the count by 2 (3 cells → 1 cell; a reduction of 2). 15 - 2 = 13 cells.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: The TABLE PROPERTIES dialog box (right-click → Table Properties) allows you to set?
options: Table alignment on the page; cell width/height; text wrapping around the table; and cell margins
explanation: Table Properties (right-click → Table Properties) has four tabs: Table (alignment; wrapping); Row (height; allow row to break across pages); Column (width); Cell (width; vertical alignment).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; what kind of TABLE is created in the chapter activity?
options: A school timetable or student data table (the practical activity in Chapter 3)
explanation: Book 5 Chapter 3's activity has students create a structured table — typically a timetable or class schedule — to practice inserting; formatting; merging cells; and applying table styles.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'AUTOFIT TO WINDOW' do when inserting a table?
options: Adjusts the table to the window size on screen
Stretches the table width to fill the full margin-to-margin width of the Word page automatically
Reduces the table to fit one column
explanation: AutoFit to Window makes the table span the full text width of the page (between the left and right margins) — the total table width automatically adjusts when margins change.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To RESIZE A COLUMN WIDTH manually in a Word table; you?
options: Drag the column BORDER (the vertical gridline) left or right
explanation: Dragging a column border (the vertical gridline between columns) left or right changes that column's width manually. You can also double-click a border to AutoFit to the widest content.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What happens when you PRESS ENTER inside a table cell in Word?
options: Starts a NEW PARAGRAPH within the SAME CELL — the cell height grows to fit
explanation: Pressing Enter in a cell creates a new paragraph within that cell — the cell expands vertically. This is different from Tab (which moves to the next cell).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To DELETE A COLUMN from a Word table?
options: Select the column; press Delete key
Select the column; Table Tools Layout → Rows & Columns → Delete → Delete Columns
explanation: Selecting a column and pressing Delete only clears the cell contents. To remove the column itself; use Table Tools Layout → Delete → Delete Columns (or right-click → Delete Columns).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the TABLE MOVE HANDLE at the top-left of a table?
options: Clicking it selects the entire table; dragging it moves the table to a new position on the page
explanation: The move handle (✥ icon) at the top-left corner: click → selects whole table; drag → moves the entire table to a new location on the page. Appears when hovering over the table.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What appears at the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner of a Word table?
options: A resize handle (small square) — dragging it resizes the entire table proportionally
explanation: The resize handle (small square ◻) at the bottom-right corner: drag it to resize the whole table proportionally; enlarging or shrinking all rows and columns together.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Book 5 Chapter 3 activity; students insert a HEADER ROW and then MERGE the cells in that row to create a table title. What is this merged cell used for?
options: A TABLE CAPTION or TITLE that spans the full width — identifying what the table contains (e.g. 'Class Timetable - Grade 5B')
explanation: A merged header cell spanning all columns creates a wide title area for the table — containing the table's name or description; clearly labelling what the data below represents.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: How many ways of inserting a table does Book 5 Chapter 3 teach?
explanation: Book 5 teaches three methods: (1) grid drag; (2) Insert Table dialog box; (3) Draw Table freehand. Each has different use cases — the grid is quickest; the dialog gives precision; Draw allows custom shapes.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the GRIDLINES feature in Word tables?
options: Non-printing dotted lines that show table structure when borders are turned off — visible on screen but not in print (View → Show → Gridlines)
explanation: Table gridlines are non-printing structural guides — they show the table's cell boundaries on screen even when borders are removed; helping you navigate the table without printed borders appearing.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT A TABLE using the DRAW TABLE method; the cursor changes to?
options: A PENCIL ICON — you draw the table outline and then draw lines inside to create rows and columns
explanation: When Draw Table mode is activated (Insert → Table → Draw Table); the cursor changes to a pencil. You first draw the outer rectangle; then draw horizontal/vertical lines inside to create cells.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What Word feature allows you to fit TABLE CONTENT to the column width automatically?
options: AutoFit to Contents — adjusts each column width to fit its widest cell content automatically
explanation: AutoFit to Contents (right-click → AutoFit → AutoFit to Contents; or in the Insert Table dialog) automatically sizes each column to fit its content — prevents wasted space or cut-off text.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: Which TABLE STYLE OPTION highlights every OTHER ROW with a different background colour?
explanation: Banded Rows alternates the background colour of odd and even rows — making data in long tables easier to read across the page; a common design pattern in professional reports.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: When splitting a cell into 2 columns and 3 rows; how many cells result?
explanation: Splitting 1 cell into 2 columns × 3 rows = 2 × 3 = 6 cells. The original cell is divided into a mini-table of 6 cells.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is one reason to use TABLES in Word instead of TABS for aligning data?
options: Tables automatically maintain alignment even when text length varies; text in columns stays perfectly aligned without manual spacing adjustments
explanation: Tabs break if text is too long — the alignment shifts. Tables are far more reliable: each cell holds its content at a fixed position regardless of text length; keeping columns perfectly aligned.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the DIFFERENCE between a table's OUTER BORDER and its INNER BORDERS?
options: The outer border is the rectangle around the entire table; inner borders are the lines between individual cells (gridlines between rows and columns)
explanation: Outer borders surround the whole table; inner borders divide the cells inside. In Word's Borders dropdown; you can apply different styles to outer and inner borders independently.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To make the TABLE align in the CENTRE of the page (not cell content; but the table itself)?
options: Table Properties (right-click → Table Properties → Table tab → Alignment → Center)
explanation: Table Properties → Table tab → Alignment has options for Left; Center; and Right table alignment on the page — this positions the table itself; not the text inside cells.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: Book 5 Chapter 3 notes that tables can be IMPORTED from Excel. How does this work in Word?
options: Copy cells in Excel → Paste in Word → choose Paste Options (Paste as Table; Link to Excel; etc.)
explanation: Copying Excel cells and pasting into Word shows Paste Options: paste as a Word Table (editable in Word); paste as a picture; or paste with a link to the Excel source (updates when Excel changes).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does RIGHT-CLICKING inside a table cell give you access to?
options: A context menu with table-specific options including Insert; Delete; Merge Cells; Split Cells; Table Properties; and text formatting
explanation: Right-clicking inside a table cell shows a context menu with all common table operations: Insert rows/columns; Delete; Merge; Split; Table Properties; plus standard text formatting options.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student accidentally DELETES the content of a row but keeps the row. To REMOVE THE ROW ENTIRELY she should?
options: Select the row then right-click → Delete Rows (or Table Tools Layout → Delete → Delete Rows)
explanation: Pressing Delete or Backspace in a table only clears cell content — it does not remove the row structure. To delete the entire row; use right-click → Delete Rows or Table Tools Layout → Delete.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the shortcut to INSERT A NEW ROW at the very BOTTOM of a table (without using a menu)?
options: Press Tab while in the last cell of the last row — automatically adds a new row
explanation: Tab in the last cell of the last row adds a new row at the bottom — the fastest way to extend a table as you type data; without interrupting your workflow with menu commands.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'TABLE ALIGNMENT' refer to in Word?
options: How the TABLE ITSELF is positioned relative to the page margins (Left; Centered; Right) — set in Table Properties → Table → Alignment
explanation: Table alignment (Table Properties → Table tab) positions the entire table left; center; or right on the page — separate from text alignment within cells; which is controlled by the Layout tab.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is an ADVANTAGE of using a table for a SCHOOL CLASS LIST in Word?
options: Each student's name; mark; and comment stays in its own cell in the correct column — data never misaligns; and rows can be sorted alphabetically
explanation: A table keeps student data (name; mark; grade; comment) perfectly aligned in columns — unlike tabbed text which breaks when names are different lengths. Rows can also be sorted alphabetically with one click.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; students learn to apply a TABLE STYLE. What is the effect of selecting 'Light List — Accent 1'?
options: It applies a specific pre-designed colour theme with banded rows and an accent colour (Accent 1; typically blue) to the table
It converts the table to text
explanation: 'Light List — Accent 1' is a built-in table style applying a light background with banded rows in the first accent colour (usually blue in default themes) — giving the table a clean professional look.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student presses CTRL+Z after accidentally deleting a row in a Word table. What happens?
options: The deleted row is RESTORED — Undo (Ctrl+Z) reverses the last action
explanation: Ctrl+Z is the Undo shortcut in Word — it reverses the last action; including deleted rows; merged cells; or applied table styles. Multiple Ctrl+Z presses step back through multiple actions.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the 'NO BORDER' option in Word table borders?
options: Removes ALL visible borders from the table (cells are separated by non-printing gridlines only) — giving a borderless table appearance
explanation: Setting borders to 'No Border' removes all visible black lines from the table — the structure remains (shown by faint gridlines) but the printed table has no lines; useful for invisible-grid layouts.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To CHANGE THE HEIGHT of a specific row in a Word table to exactly 1 cm?
options: Right-click → Table Properties → Row tab → Specify height → enter 1 cm
explanation: Table Properties → Row tab → check 'Specify height' and enter the exact value (e.g. 1 cm). This sets the row to a precise height — useful for forms or timetables needing uniform rows.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the minimum number of ROWS a Word table can have?
explanation: A Word table must have at least 1 row and 1 column — a 1×1 table is the smallest possible; though it is rarely useful. Tables are defined by having at least 1 row.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: WHICH FEATURE in Book 5 teaches students to use a table for a PRICE LIST or CATALOGUE?
options: Chapter 3 practical activity — create a table with product; price; and description columns
explanation: Book 5 Chapter 3 uses a practical activity where students create a structured table — which typically includes items; their prices; and descriptions — demonstrating real-world table use for price lists or catalogues.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What happens when you press TAB at the END OF A ROW (but not the last row) in a Word table?
options: The cursor moves to the FIRST CELL of the NEXT ROW
explanation: Tab at the end of any row (except the last) moves the cursor to the first cell of the next row — allowing continuous data entry from left to right; row by row.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student has a table for a timetable. She wants the DAYS OF THE WEEK in the first row to be centred and bold. Which steps should she take?
options: Select days; Home → Bold; Table Tools Layout → Align Center
Directly type each day in bold
explanation: Select the cells with days → Home → Bold (or Ctrl+B) for bold → Table Tools Layout → Alignment → Align Center (horizontally and vertically centered). Both steps can be done together.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Word; can you INSERT AN IMAGE inside a table cell?
options: No; only text is allowed in cells
Yes — place the cursor in the cell; then Insert → Pictures to add an image that stays within that cell
No; you need a text box
explanation: Word allows images; icons; and other objects to be inserted directly into table cells — they stay within the cell boundary and move with the cell when the table is resized or moved.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the QUICKEST way to insert a simple 3x3 table in Word?
options: Insert → Table → Insert Table dialog → type 3 rows and 3 columns
Insert → Table → hover over the grid to highlight 3 columns × 3 rows → click
Draw Table and draw 9 cells manually
explanation: The grid method is the fastest for simple tables: Insert → Table → hover to highlight the desired number of rows and columns in the grid preview → click to insert instantly.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Word 2016; when you hover over the INSERT TABLE GRID; what feedback do you see?
options: The table dimensions are shown (e.g. '3×4 Table') and a live preview highlights in the document showing exactly how the table will look
explanation: As you hover over the grid; Word shows a dynamic preview — the highlighted squares show the table dimensions (e.g. '3×4 Table') and a live preview appears in the document so you can see the exact size before clicking.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the PENCIL TOOL do in Draw Table mode?
options: Draws new table borders — drag to create the outer boundary; then drag inside to add rows and columns
explanation: The pencil tool in Draw Table mode lets you draw custom table borders. First draw the outer rectangle; then draw horizontal lines for rows and vertical lines for columns — perfect for irregular layouts.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: When is the DRAW TABLE method most useful?
options: For tables with non-uniform rows and columns — like a complex schedule where some rows are taller or some cells span multiple columns
explanation: Draw Table is most useful when you need an irregular table — cells of different sizes; columns of varying width; or a layout that cannot be achieved with the uniform grid from the standard Insert Table.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'AUTOFIT TO CONTENTS' option do in the Insert Table dialog?
options: Automatically adjusts each column's width to match the widest content typed into any cell in that column
Stretches the table to the full page width
explanation: AutoFit to Contents makes columns shrink or expand automatically to fit their widest entry — the table stays compact and well-fitted to the content without manual resizing.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To SELECT A SINGLE CELL in a Word table; you click?
options: The LEFT EDGE of the cell (when the cursor becomes a black right-pointing arrow → click to select just that cell)
The top border of the cell
explanation: To select one cell: move the mouse to the cell's left edge until the cursor turns into a solid black right-pointing arrow → click to select just that cell (it highlights). This lets you apply formatting to one cell only.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To SELECT AN ENTIRE COLUMN in a Word table?
options: Click any cell in the column
Move the mouse ABOVE the column until the cursor becomes a black downward-pointing arrow → click to select the whole column
explanation: Hover above a column until the cursor becomes a solid black downward arrow → click to select that entire column. You can then delete; resize; or format that column in one step.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To SELECT AN ENTIRE ROW in a Word table?
options: Click any cell in the row
Click in the row; then Shift+End
Move the mouse to the LEFT of the row (outside the table) until the cursor becomes a white arrow → click to select the whole row
explanation: Click outside the table to the left of the row when the cursor turns into a white arrow pointing up-right → click to select that row. You can then format or delete the entire row at once.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does it mean when a table STYLE uses a 'LAST COLUMN' option?
options: The last column receives special formatting — bold or contrasting colour — to highlight it as a totals or summary column
explanation: The Last Column option applies distinctive formatting to the rightmost column — useful when it contains totals; maximums; or other summary data that should stand out from the data columns.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student wants the ROW HEIGHT of every row in a table to be EXACTLY 0.8 cm. What is the MOST EFFICIENT way to do this?
options: Select ALL rows → Table Tools Layout → Cell Size → set row height to 0.8 cm for all at once
Change font size in each cell
explanation: Select all rows (click the move handle or Ctrl+A) → Table Tools Layout → Cell Size → set the row height value. This applies to all selected rows simultaneously — faster than setting each row individually.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of TABLE PROPERTIES → ROW → 'Allow row to break across pages'?
options: Prevents the row from being deleted
Controls whether a tall row can be split across a page break — unchecking it forces the entire row to stay on one page
Adds a page break before the row
Repeats the row on each page
explanation: 'Allow row to break across pages' determines what happens when a row is too tall to fit at the bottom of a page: checked → the row splits across the page break; unchecked → the whole row moves to the next page intact.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a NESTED TABLE in Word?
options: A table inside another table — a table inserted within a cell of an outer table
A table that is linked to Excel
explanation: A nested table is a complete table inserted inside a cell of another table — used for complex layouts where a section of a table needs its own sub-rows and sub-columns. Word supports multiple levels of nesting.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; students are taught to PRINT a Word document containing a table. Which view best shows how the table will look when printed?
options: Print Layout (File → Print → Print Preview also shows the exact printed output)
explanation: Print Layout view (the normal working view) shows the document as it will print — with the table; borders; and formatting exactly as they will appear on paper. File → Print shows the Print Preview for final confirmation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the difference between pressing DELETE and pressing BACKSPACE inside a table cell?
options: Delete removes text to the RIGHT of the cursor; Backspace removes text to the LEFT of the cursor — both work within a cell without deleting the cell structure
Delete removes the cell; Backspace removes the row
Delete and Backspace remove entire rows
explanation: Inside a cell; Delete removes the character to the right of the cursor and Backspace removes the character to the left — standard text-editing behaviour. Neither deletes the cell or row structure itself.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'SORT ASCENDING' mean when sorting a Word table?
options: A to Z for text; smallest to largest for numbers; earliest to latest for dates
explanation: Ascending sort = A→Z for text; 1→10 for numbers; oldest→newest for dates. Descending is the reverse. Sort is in Table Tools → Layout → Data → Sort.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: When a Word table CONTAINS A HEADER ROW and you use Sort; how should you set the dialog to avoid sorting the header?
options: In the Sort dialog; select 'My list has a Header row' — this excludes the first row from sorting so column labels stay at the top
Delete the header row before sorting
explanation: The Sort dialog has a 'My list has a Header row' option. When checked; the first row is treated as labels (not data) and is excluded from sorting — keeping column headers in place.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is TABLE WRAPPING in Word?
options: How text inside cells wraps to the next line
How BODY TEXT OUTSIDE the table wraps AROUND the table — set in Table Properties → Table → Text Wrapping (None or Around)
How the table wraps to a new page
explanation: Text Wrapping (Table Properties → Table tab): 'None' means the table sits on its own lines; body text above and below. 'Around' lets body text flow around the left and right sides of the table — like how images can be wrapped.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does CTRL+Z do after you accidentally APPLY A TABLE STYLE?
options: Undo — reverses the last action; removing the applied style and restoring the previous table formatting
explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action in Word — including table style changes; cell merges; row deletions; and formatting changes. Multiple Ctrl+Z presses step back through the action history.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student creates a PRICE LIST TABLE with columns: Item; Description; Price. She wants the Price column to be RIGHT-ALIGNED. To align numbers right in those cells she?
options: Selects the Price column → Home → Align Right (Ctrl+R) to right-align the text in those cells
Presses Tab until the numbers shift right
explanation: Select the Price column cells → Home → Align Right (or Ctrl+R). Right-aligning numbers in a price column makes decimal points line up — standard formatting for numerical data.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the MAXIMUM number of columns a Word 2016 table can have?
explanation: Word 2016 supports up to 63 columns in a table. This is a technical limit — in practice; tables rarely need more than about 10–15 columns before becoming too narrow to read on a standard page.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To QUICKLY ADD A CAPTION below a table in Word (e.g. 'Table 1: Class Timetable')?
options: Right-click the table → Insert Caption (or References → Insert Caption) — Word numbers the caption automatically
explanation: Right-click the table → Insert Caption (or References → Insert Caption) opens a dialog where you type the caption text. Word automatically numbers captions (Table 1; Table 2; etc.) and updates numbering if tables are reordered.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In BOOK 5 Chapter 3; after creating the table; what is the FINAL STEP students are taught to do before printing?
options: Apply a table style and adjust column widths to ensure all data fits properly within the page margins — then Save (Ctrl+S)
explanation: The final steps in Book 5 Chapter 3 are: apply a table style for professional appearance; check that all columns fit within the page margins (no text cut off); and save the document before printing.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In PowerPoint 2016; where do you find the THEMES gallery?
options: DESIGN tab — the Themes group contains built-in theme thumbnails that change the look of the entire presentation
explanation: Themes are on the DESIGN tab in PowerPoint 2016. The Themes gallery shows thumbnail previews of all built-in themes (colour schemes; fonts; background graphics). Click one to apply it to all slides.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a THEME in PowerPoint?
options: A coordinated set of COLOURS; FONTS; and EFFECTS (background styles; graphic effects) that gives the entire presentation a consistent professional look
explanation: A PowerPoint theme packages three design elements: a colour set (6 accent colours + background + text colours); a font pair (heading + body fonts); and an effects set (shadow; glow; bevel styles for shapes). Applying one theme changes all three at once.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What THREE components make up a PowerPoint THEME?
options: COLOURS; FONTS; and EFFECTS — all three coordinate together when a theme is applied
explanation: A theme consists of: (1) a Theme Colors set (defines accent; text; and background colours); (2) a Theme Fonts set (heading font + body font pair); and (3) a Theme Effects set (determines shadow; glow; bevel styles for shapes/pictures).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the VARIANTS section on the Design tab used for?
options: Applying colour VARIATIONS of the current theme — alternative colour palettes while keeping the same fonts and layout
explanation: Variants (Design tab; to the right of Themes) shows 4 colour variations of the current theme. Click one to switch colour palette without changing the theme's fonts or layout structure.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To CUSTOMISE THE COLOURS of a theme in PowerPoint?
options: Design tab → Variants group → click the dropdown arrow → Colors → Customise Colors (opens a dialog to change each of the 12 colour slots)
explanation: Design → Variants → dropdown arrow → Colors → Customise Colors opens a dialog showing all 12 theme colour slots (Dark 1&2; Light 1&2; Accent 1–6; Hyperlink; Followed Hyperlink). Change any slot and save as a custom theme colour set.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the BACKGROUND STYLES option on the Design tab allow you to do?
options: Change the BACKGROUND of slides (solid colours; gradient fills; textures; pictures) independently of the theme colours
explanation: Design → Background Styles (or Format Background) lets you set each slide's background independently: solid fill; gradient; texture; pattern; or a picture. Click 'Apply to All' to set the same background on every slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In PowerPoint 2016; a TRANSITION is applied to?
options: The SLIDE ITSELF — it is the visual effect seen when moving from one slide to the NEXT during a slideshow
The entire presentation at once (cannot be changed per slide)
explanation: Transitions are slide-level effects: the animation that plays as you move FROM slide to slide. Each slide can have a different transition; set individually. A transition starts when you advance to that slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What TAB in PowerPoint contains all the TRANSITION effects?
options: TRANSITIONS tab — contains the Transition to This Slide gallery; Effect Options; Timing; and Advance Slide settings
explanation: The TRANSITIONS tab in the ribbon has: the Transitions gallery (Subtle; Exciting; Dynamic Content categories); Effect Options (direction/style of the transition); Duration; Sound; and Advance Slide (on click or after X seconds).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the EFFECT OPTIONS button do for a transition?
options: Changes the DIRECTION or STYLE of the selected transition (e.g. Wipe can go From Left; From Right; From Top; From Bottom)
explanation: Effect Options appears after selecting a transition — it customises that transition's specific direction; shape; or variant. For example; a Wipe transition can be From Left; From Right; From Top; From Bottom; or From Top-Left; etc.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the DURATION setting in the Transitions tab control?
options: How long a slide is displayed
How many seconds the transition ANIMATION takes to complete (e.g. 0.5 seconds for a fast transition; 3 seconds for a slow fade)
The delay before the next slide starts
explanation: Duration (Transitions tab → Timing group) sets the length of the transition animation in seconds. A short duration (0.50s) produces a snappy transition; a long one (3.00s) is slow and dramatic. Default is usually 0.70s.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'APPLY TO ALL' button do in the Transitions tab?
options: Applies the currently selected transition (with all its settings — effect; duration; sound; advance) to EVERY slide in the presentation
Applies the transition only to selected slides
Applies the transition to the current slide only
explanation: Apply to All saves time by copying the current transition setting to every slide at once. Without it; each slide must be selected individually to set its transition.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Advance Slide section (Transitions tab); what does 'After: 00:03.00' mean?
options: The slide appears 3 seconds before being clicked
The slide automatically advances to the NEXT slide after 3 seconds; without needing a mouse click or key press
The slide is shown for 30 seconds
explanation: 'After: X seconds' in Advance Slide sets automatic advancement — the presentation moves to the next slide after the specified time even with no user input. Useful for self-running kiosk presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the SOUND option in the Transitions tab?
options: Adds background music to the whole presentation
Adds a SOUND EFFECT that plays during the transition animation (e.g. a whoosh; a click; a drum roll)
explanation: The Sound dropdown (Transitions → Timing → Sound) adds an audio cue to the transition — a brief sound (e.g. Camera; Chime; Whoosh; Laser) that plays as the transition animation plays. Can be set differently per slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: The TRANSITIONS gallery in PowerPoint 2016 is divided into three categories. What are they?
explanation: The Transitions gallery has three groups: SUBTLE (simple clean transitions like Fade; Push; Wipe); EXCITING (more dramatic effects like Curtains; Flip; Fracture); and DYNAMIC CONTENT (moves only the content; not the slide background — like Pan; Orbit; Rotate).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the MORPH transition do in PowerPoint 2016?
options: SMOOTHLY ANIMATES objects that appear on two consecutive slides — moving; scaling; and transforming shared objects to create a seamless animated effect
explanation: Morph creates a fluid transition by finding matching objects on consecutive slides and smoothly animating changes in their position; size; rotation; colour; and shape. This produces a seamless motion graphic effect between slides.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is an ANIMATION in PowerPoint?
options: A visual effect applied to an INDIVIDUAL OBJECT (text; image; shape; SmartArt) ON A SINGLE SLIDE — it appears; disappears; or moves without leaving the slide
A video inserted on a slide
explanation: Animations are object-level effects on a single slide: text flies in; an image fades; a shape spins. Unlike transitions (slide-level); animations control when and how each object on the slide appears; moves; or exits.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What TAB in PowerPoint 2016 contains all ANIMATION effects?
options: ANIMATIONS tab — the Animation gallery; Effect Options; Advanced Animation (Add Animation; Animation Pane; Trigger); and Timing
explanation: The ANIMATIONS tab has: the Animation gallery (Entrance; Emphasis; Exit; Motion Paths); Effect Options; the Animation Pane (to manage all animations on the slide); Trigger; and Timing settings (Start; Duration; Delay).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: The Animation gallery is grouped into four categories. What are they?
options: ENTRANCE; EMPHASIS; EXIT; and MOTION PATHS
explanation: The four animation categories: ENTRANCE (object appears — Appear; Fly In; Bounce); EMPHASIS (object is highlighted while on the slide — Pulse; Spin; Grow/Shrink); EXIT (object disappears — Fade; Fly Out); MOTION PATHS (object moves along a drawn path — Arc; Line; Custom).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is an ENTRANCE animation?
options: An animation that makes an object disappear
An animation that makes an object EXIT the slide
An animation that makes an object APPEAR on the slide during the presentation (the object is hidden until the animation plays)
An animation that highlights an object
explanation: Entrance animations (shown in green in the Animation pane) make an object appear on the slide when triggered. Before the animation plays; the object is invisible. Examples: Appear; Fly In; Bounce; Zoom; Fade.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is an EMPHASIS animation?
options: An animation applied to video clips
An animation that makes an object APPEAR
An animation that makes an object DISAPPEAR
An animation applied to an object ALREADY VISIBLE on the slide — it draws attention to it (e.g. Pulse; Spin; Grow; Change Colour) without making it appear or disappear
explanation: Emphasis animations (shown in yellow) are applied to objects already on the slide to draw the audience's attention — Pulse; Spin; Grow/Shrink; Teeter; Change Font Color. The object stays on the slide throughout.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is an EXIT animation?
options: An animation that makes an object appear
An animation that makes an object LEAVE THE SLIDE during the presentation (the object disappears when the animation plays)
An animation that moves the object
explanation: Exit animations (shown in red) make an object disappear from the slide when triggered. The object is visible; then plays the exit animation and is gone. Examples: Fade; Fly Out; Shrink and Turn; Bounce.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a MOTION PATH animation?
options: An animation that makes an object fade
An animation that makes an object move ALONG A DEFINED PATH on the slide (e.g. Line; Arc; Circle; Custom freehand path)
An animation that changes the object's colour
An animation that makes the object spin
explanation: Motion Path animations move an object from one place to another along a path drawn on the slide. Built-in paths include Line; Arc; Turn; Circle; and S-Curve. Custom draws any freehand path. The object ends at the path's end point.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the ANIMATION PANE in PowerPoint?
options: The slide panel on the left
A panel that lists ALL animations on the current slide in order; with controls for reordering; timing; and editing each animation
explanation: The Animation Pane (Animations → Advanced Animation → Animation Pane) shows a timeline-style list of all animations on the slide — their order; start trigger; duration; delay; and type. Essential for managing multiple animations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'START: ON CLICK' setting mean for an animation?
options: The animation plays automatically when the slide appears
The animation plays when the PRESENTER CLICKS THE MOUSE (or presses a key) — it waits for user input
The animation plays on a timer
The animation plays when the object is hovered over
explanation: Start: On Click (the default) means the animation is triggered by a mouse click or spacebar press during the presentation. Each click advances to the next animation in sequence; giving the presenter control over pacing.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'START: WITH PREVIOUS' mean for an animation?
options: The animation starts after a click
The animation starts automatically AT THE SAME TIME as the previous animation (they play simultaneously; no additional click needed)
The animation starts before the slide appears
The animation starts at a random time
explanation: Start: With Previous makes the animation begin at the same moment as the previous animation — they play together. No additional click is needed. Useful for making multiple objects animate simultaneously.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'START: AFTER PREVIOUS' mean for an animation?
options: The animation plays before the previous animation ends
The animation starts automatically AFTER THE PREVIOUS ANIMATION FINISHES playing (a short delay can be added)
The animation plays on click only
The animation reverses the previous animation
explanation: Start: After Previous automatically begins the animation once the previous animation completes — like a chain reaction; without any user click. The Delay setting adds extra wait time before this animation starts.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the DELAY setting do for an animation?
options: Adds a PAUSE (in seconds) BEFORE the animation starts playing — giving the audience time to read existing content first
explanation: Delay (Animations → Timing → Delay) adds a wait time between when the animation is triggered (or when the previous one ends) and when this animation actually begins. Useful for staggered effects.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does DURATION control in the Animation Timing settings?
options: How long the animation's visual effect takes to complete — e.g. 0.5s for a quick Fly In; 2s for a slow Fade In
The delay before the animation starts
The number of times the animation repeats
explanation: Duration (Animations → Timing → Duration) sets the length of the animation effect in seconds. A short duration (0.25–0.50s) produces quick snappy animations; longer (2–3s) creates slow graceful effects.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does REPEAT do in an animation's timing settings?
options: Makes the animation play MULTIPLE TIMES (e.g. 2; 3; Until Next Click; Until End of Slide)
Adds a delay before the animation
explanation: Repeat (Effect Options or Timing pane) makes the animation loop: you can set a specific number of repeats; or Until Next Click/Until End of Slide to keep it looping until manually stopped.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a TRIGGER animation in PowerPoint?
options: An animation that plays on slide entry
An animation that plays when a specific OBJECT ON THE SLIDE IS CLICKED — click that object to start its animation
An animation with a custom path
explanation: Trigger (Animations → Advanced Animation → Trigger → On Click Of) assigns an animation to fire when a specific object (a button; shape; or image on the slide) is clicked — making interactive presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'ADD ANIMATION' (Animations → Advanced Animation → Add Animation) allow you to do?
options: Add a SECOND (or more) animation to the same object — so one object can have multiple sequential animations (e.g. Fly In → Pulse → Fly Out)
Add an animation to all slides
explanation: Add Animation lets you assign multiple animations to one object — it does NOT replace the current one (unlike the Animation gallery which replaces). This way an object can enter; emphasise; then exit within the same slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of using the ANIMATION PAINTER (eyedropper icon near the Animation Pane)?
options: COPIES animation settings from one object and pastes them onto another object — one click to copy to one object; double-click to copy to multiple objects
explanation: Animation Painter (Animations → Advanced Animation → Animation Painter) copies all animation settings (type; start; duration; delay) from one object. Single-click to paste to one object; double-click to enter 'stamp mode' and paste to multiple objects.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To PREVIEW all animations on a slide without starting the full slideshow?
options: Click PREVIEW (Animations tab → Preview) or click PLAY ALL in the Animation Pane to see all animations play on the slide in Normal view
explanation: Preview (Animations tab) plays all animations on the current slide in Normal view — letting you check timings; order; and effects without entering Slide Show mode. The Animation Pane's Play From button previews from the selected animation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does clicking the PLAY ALL button in the Animation Pane do?
options: Plays ALL animations on the current slide in sequence in Normal view — useful for checking the full animation sequence without entering Slide Show mode
explanation: Play All in the Animation Pane runs the complete animation sequence for the current slide in Normal view — each animation plays in order so you can review timings; start settings; and effects before presenting.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5 Chapter 4; students apply a THEME to a presentation then customise it. What customisation is taught?
options: Changing only the theme's fonts by Design → Variants → Fonts → Customise Fonts (to set a specific heading and body font pair)
explanation: Book 5 Chapter 4 teaches students to customise a theme's fonts — Design → Variants → Fonts → Customise Fonts — where they set the heading font (for titles) and body font (for body text) to specific choices; creating a personalised look.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'TRIGGER' feature in PowerPoint animations most useful for?
options: Creating INTERACTIVE presentations where clicking a specific shape; button; or image on the slide starts a specific animation — turning the slide into an interactive element
explanation: Triggers are used in interactive presentations — quizzes; e-learning modules; games — where clicking a hotspot (shape; button; picture) triggers a specific response animation; making the presentation respond to viewer choices.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student wants FIVE bullets to FLY IN one at a time; each triggered by a separate click. How should she set the animation for the text box?
options: One Fly In animation with Start: After Previous
Select the text box → Animation Fly In → Effect Options → By 1st Level Paragraphs; set Start to 'On Click' — each bullet will fly in on a separate click
Animate each bullet separately using 5 text boxes
Use a transition for each bullet
explanation: Animating text with 'By 1st Level Paragraphs' breaks the text box into one animation per paragraph (bullet) — each one starts On Click. This lets the presenter reveal bullets one at a time; controlling the pace of the explanation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the MORPH transition REQUIRE to work correctly?
options: Two CONSECUTIVE slides that contain matching objects — the Morph algorithm identifies objects with the same name or content and smoothly animates the differences
explanation: Morph works by matching objects across two consecutive slides. Objects are matched by: (1) same name in the Selection Pane; or (2) same content (text; shape type). The transition then animates the changes between matched objects.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the difference between a TRANSITION and an ANIMATION in PowerPoint?
options: There is no difference — they are the same
A transition is a SLIDE-LEVEL effect (plays when moving between slides); an animation is an OBJECT-LEVEL effect (plays on individual objects within a single slide)
Animations are for images; transitions are for text
explanation: Key distinction: TRANSITION = the effect between slides (applies to the whole slide; plays during advancement); ANIMATION = effect on an individual object on a slide (text; shape; image). Both can have timing and sound settings.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5's animation chapter; students learn to create a 'BOUNCING BALL' effect. Which animation category is used?
options: Motion Paths — the ball is animated to follow a drawn path (e.g. an arc or bounce path) around the slide
explanation: Book 5 Chapter 4 uses a Motion Path animation to move a ball-shaped object along a path — demonstrating how Motion Paths create realistic movement. Students draw or choose a path and the object follows it during the presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does clicking 'EFFECT OPTIONS' after selecting an animation allow you to do?
options: Customise DIRECTION; SEQUENCE; SOUND; and AFTER-ANIMATION behaviour of the selected animation
Change the animation type to a different category
explanation: Effect Options opens a detailed dialog for the selected animation — covering Direction or Shape of the effect; a Sound to play with it; After-animation behaviour (dim; hide; change colour); and Text Animation (animate all at once; by paragraph; by word; etc.).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'AFTER ANIMATION' setting (in Effect Options → Effect tab) do?
options: Controls what happens to the object AFTER the animation completes — options include: Don't Dim; Hide After Animation; Hide on Next Mouse Click; or change to a different colour
Adds a sound after the animation
explanation: After Animation (Effect Options → Effect tab) determines the object's fate after its animation: it can stay visible (Don't Dim); fade out (use a dim colour); hide immediately; or hide on the next click. Useful for click-to-reveal quiz answers.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In PowerPoint; what does the SLIDE MASTER (View → Slide Master) have to do with THEMES?
options: The Slide Master is where the THEME is STORED AND EDITED — changes to theme colours; fonts; and layouts on the Slide Master apply to all slides using that layout
It is the first slide in the presentation
explanation: The Slide Master holds the theme's master formatting — title/content placeholder positions; fonts; colours; background graphics. Editing the Slide Master changes all slides at once; ensuring consistency across the presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the SLIDE SIZE option (Design → Customise → Slide Size)?
options: Changes the DIMENSIONS of all slides (e.g. Standard 4:3; Widescreen 16:9; or custom size in cm/inches) to match the display or print format
explanation: Slide Size (Design → Customise → Slide Size) sets the slide dimensions: Widescreen (16:9) for modern projectors and screens; Standard (4:3) for older projectors; or a custom size for posters; banners; or printed materials.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5 Chapter 4; the PRACTICAL ACTIVITY asks students to add animations to a presentation about their school. Which sequence is recommended?
options: Add all animations before adding content
First create all slides and add content; THEN apply a theme; THEN add transitions; THEN add animations to objects — in that logical build order
Start with animations; then add text
explanation: The standard workflow for building a presentation: (1) Create slides and add content; (2) Apply theme for consistent design; (3) Add slide transitions; (4) Add object animations. This prevents design changes from disrupting already-set animations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the PRESENTER VIEW in PowerPoint (used during a slideshow)?
options: A view that shows all slides at once
A special view that shows the CURRENT SLIDE on the audience screen while the presenter sees the current slide; NEXT SLIDE PREVIEW; speaker notes; and a timer on their own screen
A view that hides the animations
explanation: Presenter View (Slide Show → Presenter View; or press Alt+F5) displays: audience screen = full-screen slide; presenter's screen = current slide + next slide thumbnail + speaker notes + elapsed timer. Great for professional presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To REMOVE ALL ANIMATIONS from a slide quickly?
options: Delete each animation one by one
Select all objects on the slide (Ctrl+A) → in the Animations tab; select 'None' from the Animation gallery → this removes all animations from all selected objects
explanation: Select all objects (Ctrl+A in the slide area) → Animations tab → click 'None' in the Animation gallery. This removes all animations from every selected object at once — faster than deleting animations individually.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What type of ENTRANCE animation is 'APPEAR' in PowerPoint?
options: The object flies in from the side
The object INSTANTLY becomes visible on the slide with NO animation motion — the simplest entrance animation
The object bounces onto the slide
explanation: Appear is the simplest entrance animation — the object is invisible; then instantly appears (no motion; no fade; no fly-in). It is the default 'No animation' animation — useful when you want the object to simply pop into existence on click.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What category is the 'SPIN' animation in PowerPoint?
options: Entrance (makes the object appear by spinning)
Exit (makes the object disappear by spinning)
EMPHASIS — the object is already on the slide; it spins to draw attention; then stays on the slide
explanation: Spin is an Emphasis animation — the object is visible on the slide; the Spin animation makes it rotate to draw the audience's eye; then it stops spinning and remains on the slide. Great for highlighting a key image or diagram.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'FADE' transition do in PowerPoint?
options: Wipes across from left to right
The current slide GRADUALLY BECOMES TRANSPARENT while the next slide GRADUALLY BECOMES OPAQUE — a smooth dissolve between slides
Flips the slide like a page turn
Pushes the slide off the screen
explanation: Fade (in the Subtle category) cross-dissolves between slides: the current slide fades to nothing while the next slide fades in. It is professional; subtle; and works well for serious presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'PUSH' transition do?
options: The next slide PUSHES the current slide off the screen from one direction (left; right; up; or down)
explanation: Push (Subtle category) makes the next slide push the current one out of view — the direction is set via Effect Options (From Right; From Left; From Bottom; From Top). It suggests movement and flow.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'CHECKERBOARD' transition effect in PowerPoint?
options: An exciting transition where the slide breaks into a CHECKERBOARD PATTERN of squares that alternate between old and new slides
A wipe from left to right
explanation: Checkerboard (Exciting category) creates a pattern of alternating squares that reveal the new slide — an energetic effect that works well for quiz reveals or game-style presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What type of presentations are DYNAMIC CONTENT transitions most suitable for?
options: Presentations where the slide BACKGROUND STAYS FIXED while only the CONTENT (text; images) animates in — giving the impression of continuous flowing content
explanation: Dynamic Content transitions (Orbit; Pan; Rotate; Conveyor) move only the content placeholders while the background appears fixed — creating a magazine-scroll feeling ideal for story-driven or visual presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the CUBE transition?
options: The slide breaks into a checkerboard
The slide appears to ROTATE ON A 3D CUBE — the current slide rotates away and the next slide rotates into view on an adjacent face
The slide flips like a book page
explanation: Cube (Exciting category) rotates the slide in 3D around a vertical or horizontal axis — as if the slide is one face of a cube rotating to reveal the next face. Direction set with Effect Options.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'REVEAL' transition do in PowerPoint?
options: The current slide is WIPED AWAY like a curtain to REVEAL the next slide underneath
The slide rotates on a vertical axis
explanation: Reveal wipes the current slide away from one edge — as if pulling a cloth to reveal what's underneath. Effect Options control the direction. It suggests uncovering or unveiling content.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the GALLERY transition in PowerPoint?
options: A transition that makes slides appear to flip like PAGES IN A GALLERY or magazine — with a 3D side-panel sliding effect
A transition that shows all slides at once
explanation: Gallery (Exciting category) creates a 3D effect where slides appear to flip like pages in a book or panels on a gallery wall — using a horizontal or vertical flip direction.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Animation Pane; what does a GREEN bar represent?
options: An ENTRANCE animation — the object appears on the slide when this animation plays
explanation: In the Animation Pane; colour coding shows: GREEN = Entrance; YELLOW = Emphasis; RED = Exit; GREY or TEAL = Motion Path. This colour coding makes it easy to identify animation types at a glance.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Animation Pane; what does a RED bar represent?
options: EXIT animation — the object leaves the slide when this animation plays
explanation: RED bars in the Animation Pane represent Exit animations — the object disappears from the slide when this animation runs. Green = Entrance; Yellow = Emphasis; Grey/teal = Motion Path.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'BY 1ST LEVEL PARAGRAPHS' mean in Text Animation (Effect Options)?
options: The entire text box appears at once
Each FIRST-LEVEL BULLET POINT (paragraph) is animated separately — so the presenter can reveal the text one bullet at a time
Only the first bullet is animated
The title and subtitle animate together
explanation: By 1st Level Paragraphs breaks a text placeholder's animation into one per first-level bullet. Each click triggers the next bullet's animation — letting presenters reveal information progressively rather than all at once.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'AS ONE OBJECT' mean in Text Animation (Effect Options)?
options: All text animates word by word
The ENTIRE text box (all paragraphs/bullets) is treated as ONE unit and animates together in a single animation event
explanation: As One Object: the whole text box — including all bullets — animates together as a single unit. One click shows all text at once. Contrast with 'By 1st Level Paragraphs' which splits bullets into individual animations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'BY LETTER' animation sequence mean?
options: Each individual CHARACTER (letter) in the text flies in or fades in separately — creating a typewriter or showering effect
The text box is split into rows
explanation: By Letter animates each character one after another — very dramatic and slow for long text; best used for short words or titles. The Delay between letters is controlled by the percentage setting (% delay between letters).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To CHANGE THE ORDER of animations in the Animation Pane; you?
options: Right-click and choose Move to Top
Select the animation in the pane then click the UP or DOWN ARROW buttons at the top of the Animation Pane to reorder it
Drag and drop within the Animation Pane (also works)
Delete and recreate in the correct order
explanation: Both methods work: (a) select the animation → click the up/down arrows in the Animation Pane toolbar; (b) drag the animation bar up or down within the pane. Order determines which animation plays first when Click triggers are used.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is 'WIPE' as a PowerPoint transition?
options: The new slide is REVEALED gradually by a line sweeping across from one direction (e.g. left to right) — the old slide is wiped away as the new one appears
explanation: Wipe (Subtle category) reveals the next slide by sweeping a line across the screen — like a windshield wiper. Direction (From Left; From Right; From Top; From Bottom; From Top-Left; etc.) is set via Effect Options.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is 'SPLIT' as a transition in PowerPoint?
options: The slide is divided into random shapes
The slide opens from the centre outward (or closes to centre) either HORIZONTALLY or VERTICALLY — revealing the next slide
explanation: Split (Subtle category) makes the current slide appear to split open — either horizontal (top and bottom halves moving apart) or vertical (left and right halves) — to reveal the next slide. Effect Options choose direction.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'DRAPE' transition do in PowerPoint?
options: The slide appears to FOLD AND DRAPE like a curtain or fabric falling — a dramatic textured transition in the Exciting category
The slide tiles into smaller pieces
explanation: Drape is an Exciting category transition that creates a fabric-draping visual — the current slide appears to fold and drop like a cloth curtain; revealing the next slide underneath. Very theatrical for creative presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To add a SOUND to a specific ANIMATION (not a transition); you?
options: Animation → Effect Options → Effect tab → SOUND dropdown — choose a built-in sound or browse for a sound file
explanation: Animation sound is in Effect Options → Effect tab → Sound dropdown. You can choose built-in sounds (Camera; Chime; Coin; etc.) or '[Other Sound…]' to browse for a .wav file. Sound plays when the animation runs.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'GROW/SHRINK' emphasis animation do?
options: Moves the object to a new position
SCALES the object UP (grows) or DOWN (shrinks) by a percentage — drawing attention by temporarily enlarging or reducing it
Spins the object around its centre
explanation: Grow/Shrink is an Emphasis animation that changes the object's size — you set the percentage (e.g. 150% to grow to 1.5× size; 50% to shrink). The object returns to original size after the animation unless set otherwise.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'PULSE' emphasis animation do?
options: The object fades out then back
The object RAPIDLY SCALES UP then back to original size — a quick pulsing beat that draws the eye
The object slides to a new position
explanation: Pulse (Emphasis) makes the object quickly enlarge then snap back to its original size — like a heartbeat — drawing attention. Repeating it creates a continuous pulsing effect. Great for highlighting a button or call-to-action.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'TEETER' emphasis animation do?
options: Makes the object rotate back and forth LIKE A ROCKING OR TEETERING MOTION — a slight side-to-side rotation that draws attention
explanation: Teeter (Emphasis) rotates the object slightly clockwise then slightly anticlockwise — like a rocking chair — drawing attention with a gentle wobble. Often used on icons or characters to make them appear animated/alive.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'BOUNCE' entrance animation?
options: The object fades in from top
The object FLIES IN from outside the slide and BOUNCES a few times before settling in its final position — as if it dropped and bounced like a ball
explanation: Bounce (Entrance) makes the object fly in (usually from above) and bounce two or three times before stopping at its position — like a dropped ball. Energetic and playful; suits younger audiences or light-hearted content.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'ZOOM' entrance animation?
options: The object slides in from the left
The object GROWS from a tiny point to full size AT ITS POSITION on the slide — appearing to zoom toward the viewer
explanation: Zoom (Entrance) starts the object very small (or invisible at a point) and scales it up to full size at its position — like a camera zoom into the object. It draws focus to that element's position on the slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'FLY IN' entrance animation in PowerPoint?
options: The object FLIES IN FROM OUTSIDE THE SLIDE (default: from the bottom) and moves to its position on the slide
The object fades from 0% to 100% opacity
explanation: Fly In (Entrance) moves the object from outside the slide edge to its final position — direction set in Effect Options (From Bottom; From Left; From Right; From Top; From Top-Left; etc.). A classic; widely used animation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'FLOAT IN' entrance animation do?
options: Exactly the same as Fly In
The object APPEARS ABOVE ITS FINAL POSITION and FLOATS DOWN (or up) gently to settle in place — a softer; more graceful version of Fly In
The object appears with a bounce
explanation: Float In (Entrance) is similar to Fly In but with a smoother; more gradual deceleration — the object glides gently into position rather than flying at constant speed. More elegant for professional presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'SWIVEL' entrance animation?
options: The object appears to SPIN ON A VERTICAL OR HORIZONTAL AXIS — rotating into view from an edge as if mounted on a hinge
The object grows from a point
explanation: Swivel (Entrance) rotates the object around a vertical axis (like a revolving door) to bring it into view. Effect Options allow Horizontal or Vertical swivel direction.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; students learn to use SOUND EFFECTS with transitions. What format does PowerPoint prefer for transition sounds?
options: WAV — the standard uncompressed audio format compatible with PowerPoint transition sound effects
explanation: PowerPoint's transition sound picker uses WAV files for custom sounds (browse option). WAV is uncompressed audio that plays reliably across all PowerPoint versions. MP3 can be used via Insert → Audio for background music; but transition sounds use WAV.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student has applied a 'FLY IN' animation to a title text and the text appears all at once. She wants each WORD to fly in separately. She should?
options: Change Effect Options → Sequence → 'BY WORD' — this makes each word in the text animate separately in sequence
explanation: Effect Options → Sequence → By Word splits the text animation word by word — each word flies in one after another (with a short delay between words set by the % delay option) rather than all words appearing simultaneously.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'PATH POINTS' edit mode allow you to do for a Custom Motion Path?
