options: RESHAPE the motion path by dragging its anchor points — add; delete; or move points to create curves and corners in the path
explanation: Right-clicking a Motion Path → Edit Points shows the path's control points (like a vector curve). Drag these points to reshape the path; add new points; or delete existing ones to create any custom movement shape.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: Which of the following animations would be BEST for making a company LOGO gradually appear on a title slide?
options: Appear Entrance (no movement; just instant reveal)
Fade Entrance — a professional; subtle appearance that draws attention without distraction
explanation: Fade is the most professional entrance for logos and headlines on formal presentations — it avoids distracting movement and lets the audience focus on the content; suitable for corporate; medical; or academic presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'HIDE AFTER ANIMATION' (Effect Options → After animation) do?
options: The object BECOMES INVISIBLE immediately after its animation completes — useful for making content disappear after being revealed
The object moves off the slide
explanation: Hide After Animation makes the object invisible right after its animation finishes — useful for step-by-step builds where earlier content should disappear as newer content appears; or for quiz questions where the correct answer should hide after shown.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of NAMED OBJECTS in the Selection Pane for the Morph transition?
options: To give objects CONSISTENT NAMES across two consecutive slides so PowerPoint can match them and animate the differences smoothly using Morph
explanation: Morph matches objects across slides by name. Renaming an object '!!circle' on slide 1 and '!!circle' on slide 2 (using !! prefix) ensures Morph links them even if their content is different — enabling smooth transformation animations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student applies a theme and realises the BACKGROUND COLOUR is not ideal. Without changing the entire theme; she can?
options: Go to Design → Customise → Format Background → change only the background fill (solid; gradient; picture) while keeping all other theme settings
Change the text colours in Home
explanation: Format Background (Design → Customise → Format Background) changes only the slide background — fill type; colour; transparency — without affecting theme colours; fonts; or layout. Apply to All spreads it across the presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'REVERSE PATH DIRECTION' do for a Motion Path animation?
options: Makes the object travel the path in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION — start point becomes end point; end becomes start
explanation: Right-click a Motion Path → Reverse Path Direction flips the direction of travel — the object now travels from the original end point back to the start point. Useful for making objects retrace their path.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What happens to an object set to 'HIDE ON NEXT MOUSE CLICK' after animation?
options: The object STAYS VISIBLE after its animation but DISAPPEARS when the presenter makes the next mouse click (or keypress)
explanation: Hide on Next Mouse Click (Effect Options → After animation) lets the object stay visible temporarily after its animation; then hides it on the next click. Useful for revealing an answer that then disappears when you advance.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; students create a QUIZ slide using animations. What technique is taught for REVEALING ANSWERS one at a time?
options: Animate each answer text with Start: On Click so each presenter click reveals the next answer option progressively
Put all answers in a table
explanation: The quiz technique in Book 5: place each answer as a separate text box or bullet → apply Fly In or Appear animation to each → set Start: On Click → each click during the presentation reveals the next answer option.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student applies FIVE different transitions to FIVE slides. She later decides all slides should have the SAME FADE transition. What is the fastest method?
options: Delete all transitions and redo them
Apply Fade to slide 1; select all slides in Slide Sorter view (Ctrl+A); then click Apply to All in the Transitions tab
explanation: With all slides selected (Ctrl+A in Slide Sorter) → Transitions tab → choose Fade → Apply to All. This simultaneously sets the Fade transition with the same duration and settings on every slide — overwriting all five individual transitions.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What view in PowerPoint is BEST for managing and reordering slides while checking which transitions are applied?
options: SLIDE SORTER VIEW (View → Slide Sorter) — shows all slide thumbnails with transition icons below each; and allows drag-and-drop reordering
explanation: Slide Sorter (View → Slide Sorter) shows all slides as thumbnails in a grid — a star icon under each slide indicates a transition or animation is set. Slides can be dragged to reorder; and transitions can be applied to multiple selected slides.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In PowerPoint 2016; what does pressing F5 do during a presentation?
options: Starts the SLIDESHOW FROM THE FIRST SLIDE — the presentation goes full-screen from slide 1
Starts the slideshow from the current slide
explanation: F5 starts the slideshow from the beginning (slide 1). Shift+F5 starts from the current slide. Esc exits the slideshow. These keyboard shortcuts work during editing to quickly preview the presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does pressing SHIFT+F5 do in PowerPoint?
options: Starts the slideshow FROM THE CURRENT SLIDE (not from slide 1) — useful for testing the current slide without going back to the beginning
explanation: Shift+F5 launches the slideshow from the currently selected slide — not from slide 1. This saves time when testing a specific slide's animations and transitions without sitting through the whole presentation from the start.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does ESCAPE (Esc) do when pressed during a PowerPoint slideshow?
options: Ends the slideshow and RETURNS TO NORMAL EDITING VIEW — the current slide stays selected
explanation: Pressing Esc during a slideshow exits full-screen presentation mode and returns to PowerPoint's Normal view — with the slide that was being shown selected. You can then edit and restart.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'HIDE SLIDE' feature do in PowerPoint?
options: MARKS A SLIDE so it is SKIPPED during the normal slideshow — the slide stays in the file but does not appear when pressing Next. It can be shown by typing its slide number during the show
explanation: Hide Slide (Slide Show tab → Hide Slide; or right-click in Slide panel → Hide Slide) keeps the slide in the file but skips it during the presentation. Hidden slides are shown with a diagonal line through their number in the Slide panel.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'SCREEN RECORDING' feature in PowerPoint 2016 used for?
options: Recording the COMPUTER SCREEN and inserting the recording directly onto a slide as a video object
explanation: Insert → Screen Recording (or using the recording tools in newer versions) records the Windows screen — a region you define — and embeds the recording as a video on the slide. Useful for creating tutorial content directly in PowerPoint.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the difference between 'LOOP CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL ESC' and a fixed repeat count for an animation?
options: Loop Continuously keeps repeating the animation INDEFINITELY until Esc is pressed or until another trigger fires; a fixed count repeats it exactly N times then stops
explanation: In Effect Options → Timing → Repeat: a number (1; 2; 3…) repeats the animation that many times then stops. 'Until Next Click' repeats until clicked. 'Until End of Slide' repeats for the duration of the slide. 'Continuously' never stops until Esc.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'SMOOTH START' and 'SMOOTH END' do in animation Effect Options Timing?
options: Causes the animation to START SLOWLY then speed up (Smooth Start) or SLOW DOWN before stopping (Smooth End) — creating a more natural; eased movement
explanation: Smooth Start/End adds easing to animations — instead of starting or ending at constant speed; the object accelerates from rest (Smooth Start) or decelerates to rest (Smooth End). This produces more natural physics-like motion.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; students apply a theme to a presentation. After applying the theme; the teacher tells them to check that ALL TEXT IS STILL READABLE. Why might text become HARD TO READ after applying a theme?
options: A theme changes the slide BACKGROUND COLOUR — if existing text is dark on a white background; a theme with a dark background makes dark text invisible against dark
The theme changes font to white on white
explanation: Theme colour changes include the background. If a slide had black text on white; and the new theme uses a dark background; the black text may be almost invisible. Students must check contrast after applying any theme; adjusting text colour if needed.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the ANIMATION PAINTER keyboard shortcut in PowerPoint?
options: There is no keyboard shortcut — only the toolbar button (double-click for multiple applications)
explanation: Animation Painter has no keyboard shortcut — you access it via the toolbar button in Animations → Advanced Animation → Animation Painter. Single-click to apply to one object; double-click to apply to multiple objects (click Esc to exit).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: A student wants a PHOTO to stay HIDDEN; then APPEAR only when she clicks during her presentation. Which animation should she apply to the photo?
options: ENTRANCE → APPEAR (or Fade) with Start: On Click — the photo is invisible initially and appears when clicked
explanation: An Entrance animation (e.g. Appear; Fade; Fly In) with Start: On Click keeps the object hidden until the presenter clicks. The photo is invisible while on the slide; then appears when triggered by a click — ideal for revealing supporting images progressively.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'REWIND WHEN DONE PLAYING' do for an animation?
options: After the animation completes; the OBJECT RETURNS TO ITS ORIGINAL STARTING STATE — useful for Motion Paths where you want the object to 'snap back' to its starting position after moving
explanation: Rewind When Done Playing (Effect Options → Timing) returns the object to where it started after the animation — e.g. a ball that rolls along a path returns to the start position. Without this; the object stays at the animation's end position.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5 Chapter 4; what is the RECOMMENDATION about how many animations to use per slide for a professional presentation?
options: As many as possible — more is better
Use at MOST 2–3 animations per slide; focusing on animations that serve a purpose (revealing content gradually; emphasising key points) rather than decorating with effects for their own sake
explanation: Book 5 recommends restraint: 2–3 purposeful animations per slide prevent the audience from being distracted by constant motion. Good animation supports the message; poor animation overwhelms it.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'ORIGAMI' transition in PowerPoint 2016?
options: An Exciting category transition that makes the slide appear to FOLD like origami paper into a new shape revealing the next slide
explanation: Origami (Exciting) creates a 3D paper-folding effect — the current slide appears to fold along diagonal crease lines; revealing the next slide on the folded sections. A visually complex and distinctive effect.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a CUSTOM SLIDE SHOW in PowerPoint (Slide Show → Custom Slide Show)?
options: A SAVED SUBSET of slides from the full presentation that can be run independently — useful for presenting different versions to different audiences without maintaining separate files
A slideshow with custom animations only
explanation: Custom Slide Show (Slide Show → Custom Slide Shows → New) lets you choose a subset of slides; name the subset; and run it independently. One file can have multiple custom shows for different audiences (e.g. a 10-min version and a 30-min version).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the PHOTO ALBUM feature in PowerPoint 2016?
options: A feature to create slideshows of internet images
A built-in tool (Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album) that automatically creates a new presentation with one or more photos per slide — imported from folders on the computer
A feature to add a photo to a slide background
A feature to organise files in a folder
explanation: Photo Album (Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album) is a wizard that bulk-imports photos from your computer and creates a new presentation with photos laid out automatically across slides — one; two; or four pictures per slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT A PHOTO ALBUM in PowerPoint 2016; you go to?
options: Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album
explanation: Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album opens the Photo Album dialog where you select photos; choose layout; add captions; apply frames; and create the album as a new presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Photo Album dialog; what PICTURE LAYOUT options are available?
options: Fit to slide; 1 picture; 2 pictures; 4 pictures; 1 picture with title; 2 pictures with title; 4 pictures with title
explanation: The Photo Album layout dropdown includes: Fit to slide (one full-bleed photo per slide); 1 picture; 2 pictures; 4 pictures; and titled versions (1/2/4 pictures with title placeholders) — letting you control how many photos appear on each slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'ALL PICTURES BLACK AND WHITE' checkbox do in the Photo Album dialog?
options: Prints the photos in black and white
Converts ALL IMPORTED PHOTOS to greyscale (black and white) in the presentation — a quick effect without editing each photo individually
Adds a black frame to each photo
explanation: The 'All pictures black and white' checkbox in the Photo Album dialog applies a greyscale effect to every photo in the album — giving the presentation a uniform monochrome look without needing image editing software.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the PURPOSE of the FRAME SHAPE option in the Photo Album dialog?
options: Adds a digital frame to the presentation background
Applies a decorative border shape (Rectangle; Rounded Rectangle; Simple Frame; Shadow Frame; Soft Edge Rectangle; etc.) to EACH PHOTO in the album
Adds a text box around each photo
explanation: Frame Shape applies a visual border/frame style to all photos in the album — options include simple borders; shadow frames; rounded rectangle frames; and soft-edge styles — giving the album a polished look.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'CAPTIONS BELOW ALL PICTURES' option do in Photo Album?
options: Adds a TEXT PLACEHOLDER BELOW EACH PHOTO where you can type a caption for each picture after the album is created
explanation: Captions Below All Pictures adds an editable text box below each photo so you can type captions after the album is inserted — useful for labelling photos in a school project or event slideshow.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To EDIT AN EXISTING Photo Album in PowerPoint?
options: Insert → Photo Album → EDIT PHOTO ALBUM — reopens the Photo Album dialog with the current settings allowing you to add/remove photos; change layout; or update frames
Double-click a photo in the album
explanation: Edit Photo Album (Insert → Photo Album → Edit Photo Album) reopens the Photo Album dialog so you can add or remove photos; change the layout; update the frame style; or reorder images — without recreating the album from scratch.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Photo Album dialog; the UP and DOWN ARROW buttons are used to?
options: REORDER the selected photo in the photo list — moving it higher or lower in the sequence of slides
explanation: In the Photo Album dialog's picture list; the up/down arrows change the order of photos — moving the selected photo earlier or later in the album sequence; which determines its slide position in the final presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: Which BRIGHTNESS and CONTRAST tools appear in the Photo Album dialog?
options: Six small BUTTONS below the preview: decrease/increase Brightness (sun icons) and decrease/increase Contrast (circle icons); plus Rotate Left/Rotate Right
explanation: The Photo Album preview section has six buttons: Rotate Left; Rotate Right; Decrease Contrast; Increase Contrast; Decrease Brightness; Increase Brightness — allowing quick adjustments to each photo before inserting the album.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What file types can be inserted as AUDIO in a PowerPoint 2016 presentation?
options: MP3; WAV; WMA; MIDI; AIFF; AU; and other common audio formats
Only audio bought from the Microsoft Store
explanation: PowerPoint 2016 supports: MP3; WAV; WMA (Windows Media Audio); MIDI; AIFF; AU; and other common formats. The Audio on My PC option (Insert → Audio → Audio on My PC) browses for these local files.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT AUDIO (background music or narration) in PowerPoint 2016?
options: Insert → Audio → AUDIO ON MY PC (browse for a local file) or RECORD AUDIO (record directly with a microphone)
explanation: Insert → Audio has two options: 'Audio on My PC' to browse for a saved audio file; and 'Record Audio' to record directly using the computer's microphone. Online audio was also available in earlier versions.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: After inserting audio; the AUDIO TOOLS tabs appear. What are they called?
options: FORMAT and PLAYBACK — Format handles the audio icon appearance; Playback handles how/when audio plays
explanation: Audio Tools has two tabs: FORMAT (style the speaker icon on the slide — icon size; colour; shape) and PLAYBACK (trim audio; set volume; start options; loop; hide icon during show).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'HIDE DURING SHOW' option do for an audio file?
options: Hides the audio WAVEFORM display on the slide
Hides the SPEAKER ICON on the slide during the slideshow so the audience does not see it
explanation: Hide During Show (Audio Tools Playback → Audio Options) makes the speaker/audio icon invisible during the slideshow — the audio still plays; but the audience only hears the sound without seeing a speaker icon on the slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'PLAY ACROSS SLIDES' mean for an audio file in PowerPoint?
options: The audio plays on one slide only
The audio CONTINUES PLAYING as the presentation advances through MULTIPLE slides without stopping — useful for background music throughout the presentation
The audio plays on every other slide
The audio loops on the current slide
explanation: Play Across Slides (Audio Tools Playback → Start → Play across slides; or Audio Options → Play Across Slides checkbox) keeps the audio playing continuously as slides advance — essential for background music that should run throughout.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'LOOP UNTIL STOPPED' do for audio in PowerPoint?
options: Makes the audio FILE REPEAT CONTINUOUSLY from the beginning when it ends — so background music keeps playing as long as the slide (or presentation) is shown
explanation: Loop Until Stopped (Audio Tools Playback → Audio Options → Loop until Stopped) causes the audio to restart automatically when it finishes — essential for short background music clips that need to fill a long presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To TRIM AN AUDIO FILE in PowerPoint (removing the start or end)?
options: Audio Tools Playback → TRIM AUDIO — opens a dialog with a waveform and sliders to set a new start time and end time for the clip (the original file is unchanged)
Delete and reinsert a shorter clip
explanation: Trim Audio (Audio Tools Playback) opens a waveform editor with green (start) and red (end) trim handles. Drag them to set the clip boundaries — the audio plays only the trimmed portion. The original file is not modified.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the START dropdown (On Click or Automatically) control for audio in PowerPoint?
options: When the audio BEGINS PLAYING — 'On Click' waits for a mouse click; 'Automatically' plays the audio as soon as the slide appears
explanation: Start (Audio Tools Playback → Start): 'Automatically' plays the audio the moment the slide is displayed; 'On Click' waits for the presenter to click the speaker icon. 'In Click Sequence' plays it in the animation sequence order.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What file types can be inserted as VIDEO in PowerPoint 2016?
options: MP4; WMV; AVI; MOV; MPG; SWF (Flash; limited) and other common video formats
explanation: PowerPoint 2016 supports: MP4 (recommended); WMV; AVI; MOV (QuickTime); MPG/MPEG; and others. MP4 with H.264 encoding is the most reliable format for embedding video in PowerPoint.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT A VIDEO FILE from your computer in PowerPoint 2016?
options: Insert → Video → VIDEO ON MY PC — browse for the video file to embed it into the slide
explanation: Insert → Video → Video on My PC opens a browser to locate and embed a local video file. The video appears as a video object on the slide with playback controls.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: After inserting a video; what TWO contextual tabs appear in the ribbon?
options: Video Tools FORMAT and VIDEO TOOLS PLAYBACK — Format controls the video frame appearance; Playback controls how and when the video plays
explanation: Video Tools: FORMAT tab (video border; effects; shape crop; colour; corrections — same as picture formatting) and PLAYBACK tab (trim video; volume; Start options; loop; hide while not playing; rewind after playing).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'PLAY FULL SCREEN' do for a video in PowerPoint?
options: Inserts the video at full size on the slide
During the slideshow; the video EXPANDS TO FILL THE ENTIRE SCREEN when played — then returns to the slide after playback
explanation: Play Full Screen (Video Tools Playback → Video Options) causes the video to maximise to fill the display during playback. When the video ends; the presentation returns to the slide. The video object can remain small on the slide in edit mode.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'REWIND AFTER PLAYING' do for a video in PowerPoint?
options: After the video finishes playing; it AUTOMATICALLY RETURNS TO THE FIRST FRAME (the poster/thumbnail frame) — so the slide looks neat if reviewed again
explanation: Rewind After Playing (Video Tools Playback → Video Options) sends the video back to frame 1 after playback — the slide returns to showing the video's first frame or poster image rather than the video's last frame.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To set a POSTER FRAME (a thumbnail image shown for the video before it plays) in PowerPoint?
options: Right-click the video → Set Poster Frame
Video Tools FORMAT → Poster Frame → Current Frame (use the frame currently shown in the preview) or Image from File (use a separate image file as the thumbnail)
explanation: Poster Frame (Video Tools Format → Poster Frame) sets the image shown for the video before it plays. Options: pause the video to a good frame → 'Current Frame'; or choose 'Image from File' for a custom thumbnail.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To TRIM A VIDEO in PowerPoint (play only a portion of it)?
options: Video Tools Playback → TRIM VIDEO — drag the green (start) and red (end) handles on the timeline; or type precise start/end times
explanation: Trim Video (Video Tools Playback) opens a timeline dialog. Drag the green handle to set the start point and the red handle for the end — only the trimmed segment plays during the presentation. The original file is unchanged.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'BOOKMARK' do for a video or audio file in PowerPoint?
options: Adds a TIME MARKER at a specific point in the playback timeline — can be used to trigger animations when the video reaches that point
explanation: Bookmarks (Video Tools Playback → Bookmarks → Add Bookmark) mark specific time points in a video or audio clip. Animations can be set to trigger 'On Bookmark' — playing when the media reaches that marked time.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does SLIDE SHOW → SET UP SLIDE SHOW control?
options: Advanced SLIDE SHOW options: show type (Presented by speaker; Browsed by individual; Browsed at kiosk); show options (loop; narration; animations); which slides to show; and advance slides (manually or using timings)
explanation: Set Up Slide Show (Slide Show tab → Set Up Slide Show) is the master control for how a presentation runs: full-screen vs. window; whether to loop; whether to use recorded timings; which slides to include (all; a range; or a custom show); and how slides advance.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'BROWSED AT A KIOSK' show type do in Set Up Slide Show?
options: Runs the slideshow in a small window
Locks the presentation in a FULL-SCREEN LOOP — the slideshow runs continuously; automatically loops when it ends; and viewers cannot exit by pressing Esc (only Ctrl+Break)
Plays the slideshow in a browser
explanation: Kiosk mode (Set Up Slide Show → Browsed at a kiosk) creates a self-running presentation that loops automatically and cannot be closed by pressing Esc — designed for information displays; museum exhibits; or unmanned booths.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'REHEARSE TIMINGS' feature in PowerPoint?
options: Records HOW LONG YOU SPEND ON EACH SLIDE while you rehearse the presentation — then saves these timings so the presentation can run AUTOMATICALLY without presenter input
Sets a countdown timer on slides
explanation: Rehearse Timings (Slide Show → Rehearse Timings) records the time you spend on each slide as you rehearse — a timer shows in the top-left corner. At the end; you choose to save timings; enabling automatic advancement for self-running presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: After REHEARSING TIMINGS; where can you see the recorded time for each slide?
options: Under each slide thumbnail in SLIDE SORTER view (the time appears below the slide thumbnail next to the transition star)
explanation: After rehearsing; saved timings appear in Slide Sorter view below each slide thumbnail — the time spent on that slide during rehearsal. This helps identify slides where too much or too little time was spent.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of 'RECORD SLIDE SHOW' in PowerPoint 2016?
options: Records NARRATION (voice-over using the microphone) and TIMINGS simultaneously as you present — syncing the audio narration to each slide for automated playback
Records the video from a camera
explanation: Record Slide Show (Slide Show → Record Slide Show) captures microphone narration; webcam video; ink annotations; laser pointer movements; and slide timings simultaneously — creating a fully self-contained presentation with voice-over.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the file extension for a POWERPOINT SHOW file (a file that opens directly in Slideshow mode)?
options: .ppsx (or .pps for older formats) — opens directly as a slideshow without showing the editing interface
explanation: A .ppsx file (PowerPoint Show) opens directly in Slideshow mode — the audience sees only the presentation without the PowerPoint editing ribbon. Students in Book 5 learn to save as .ppsx for sharing with audiences.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To save a presentation as a POWERPOINT SHOW (.ppsx) file?
options: File → Save As → change file type to 'PowerPoint Show (*.ppsx)'
explanation: File → Save As → in the 'Save as type' dropdown → choose 'PowerPoint Show (*.ppsx)'. The file saves with a show-runner icon and opens directly in Slideshow mode when double-clicked.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the PRESENTER VIEW in PowerPoint (Slide Show → Presenter View)?
options: A dual-monitor mode where the AUDIENCE sees the full-screen slide on the external screen; the PRESENTER sees current slide; next slide preview; speaker notes; and timer on their own screen
A view that shows all slides simultaneously
explanation: Presenter View (Slide Show → Monitor group → Use Presenter View) requires two monitors (or a projector). The presenter's screen shows: current slide + next slide + speaker notes + elapsed time; while the audience sees only the full-screen current slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'USE TIMINGS' checkbox in Set Up Slide Show control?
options: Whether the presentation uses the REHEARSED/RECORDED SLIDE TIMINGS for automatic advancement — unchecking it requires manual clicks even if timings were saved
explanation: Use Timings (Set Up Slide Show → Advance Slides section): when checked; the presentation advances automatically using recorded timings. When unchecked; the presenter must click to advance even if timings are saved (override for manual control).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'LOOP CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL ESC' checkbox do in Set Up Slide Show?
options: Makes the ENTIRE PRESENTATION start again from slide 1 automatically when it reaches the last slide — pressing Esc stops the loop
explanation: Loop Continuously Until Esc (Set Up Slide Show → Show Options) causes the presentation to cycle back to slide 1 when it reaches the last slide — creating a continuous loop for kiosk or display purposes.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'SHOW WITHOUT NARRATION' checkbox do in Set Up Slide Show?
options: MUTES recorded narration during this playback of the presentation — the narration audio is still saved but will not play during this show
Shows a warning before the presentation
explanation: Show Without Narration (Set Up Slide Show → Show Options) silences any recorded narration for this slideshow run — useful when presenting to a live audience that doesn't need the recorded voice-over.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is an 'ONLINE PRESENTATION' in PowerPoint 2016?
options: Broadcast the presentation LIVE over the Internet using Microsoft's Office Presentation Service so remote viewers can follow along in their browser without PowerPoint installed
Embedding the file in a website
explanation: Slide Show → Online Presentation (or Present Online) uses Microsoft's service to broadcast the slideshow live — remote viewers receive a link and watch in their browser in real time as the presenter advances slides.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To ADD SPEAKER NOTES to a slide in PowerPoint?
options: In Normal view; click the NOTES PANEL at the bottom of the screen (below the slide) and type notes there — if the panel is hidden; click 'Notes' in the status bar to show it
explanation: The Notes panel (in Normal view; below the slide) is where presenters type speaker notes — reminders; key points; extra information not shown on the slide. Notes are visible in Presenter View and can be printed as handouts.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does PRINT → NOTES PAGES print in PowerPoint?
options: One page per slide: the SLIDE IMAGE at the top and the SPEAKER NOTES TEXT at the bottom of each page — useful for presenter handout sheets
explanation: Notes Pages print format (File → Print → Settings → Notes Pages) prints each slide with its notes below — the slide thumbnail at the top half of the page and the associated speaker notes text at the bottom.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'HANDOUTS' print in PowerPoint?
options: Multiple slides per page (1; 2; 3; 4; 6; or 9 slides per page) as small THUMBNAILS — for giving audience members a paper reference
Only the title of each slide
explanation: Handouts (File → Print → Layout → Handouts) prints multiple slide thumbnails per page — 1; 2; 3; 4; 6; or 9 per page. The 3-per-page option adds lines next to each thumbnail for audience note-taking.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is OUTLINE VIEW in PowerPoint?
options: A view that shows slide thumbnails only
A view that shows ALL TEXT from all slides in an OUTLINE FORMAT (by heading and bullets) with no images — useful for quickly editing text content across all slides
explanation: Outline View (View → Outline View) displays the text content of all slides in a hierarchical outline — slide titles as top-level items; bullets as indented items. Good for quickly editing text without scrolling through individual slides.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the LASER POINTER during a slideshow in PowerPoint?
options: Pressing and holding CTRL+L (or the laser pointer button in Presenter View) turns the cursor into a bright red dot for POINTING at elements on the slide during the presentation
explanation: During a slideshow; Ctrl+L or right-click → Pointer Options → Laser Pointer creates a bright dot that the presenter can use to point at specific areas of the slide — visible to the audience on the projected screen.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the PEN tool do during a slideshow in PowerPoint?
options: Allows the presenter to DRAW or ANNOTATE DIRECTLY ON THE SLIDE during the presentation — right-click → Pointer Options → Pen (or press Ctrl+P)
explanation: The Pen (Ctrl+P during slideshow; or right-click → Pointer Options → Pen) lets the presenter draw on slides in real time — circling key points; underlining important text. After the show; PowerPoint asks if you want to save the annotations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT ONLINE VIDEO (from YouTube) into a PowerPoint slide?
options: Drag the URL onto the slide
Insert → Video → ONLINE VIDEO — paste the YouTube or other video URL and it embeds as a linked video (requires Internet connection during presentation to play)
explanation: Insert → Video → Online Video opens a search box (searches YouTube/Bing Video) or an 'Enter embed code' or URL field. The video is linked (streams from the Internet) rather than embedded — the presentation requires an Internet connection to play it.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'EMBED VIDEO' mean vs 'LINK TO VIDEO' in PowerPoint?
options: EMBED: the video file is saved INSIDE the PowerPoint file (larger file; plays without Internet); LINK: only a shortcut to the file is saved (smaller file; requires the original file path to be unchanged)
Embed is for online videos; link is for local files
explanation: Embed (Insert → Video → Video on My PC) saves the video data inside the .pptx file — portable but large. Link keeps only a pointer to the original file — smaller .pptx but breaks if the video file moves. 'Video on My PC' gives the option to Embed or Insert as Link.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'COMPRESS MEDIA' feature in PowerPoint (File → Info → Compress Media)?
options: Reduces the FILE SIZE of embedded audio and video files by re-encoding them at a lower quality — options: Presentation Quality; Internet Quality; Low Quality
explanation: Compress Media (File → Info → Compress Media) re-encodes embedded media at lower bitrate/resolution to reduce the presentation file size. Three quality levels: Presentation Quality (1080p); Internet Quality (720p); Low Quality (480p).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the EXPORT TO VIDEO feature do in PowerPoint 2016?
options: Embeds a video on a slide
EXPORTS THE ENTIRE PRESENTATION as a VIDEO FILE (File → Export → Create a Video) — all animations; transitions; timings; and narration are rendered into an .mp4 or .wmv file
explanation: Create a Video (File → Export → Create a Video) renders the entire PowerPoint presentation — including all animations; transitions; recorded timings; and narration — into a standalone video file (.mp4 or .wmv) playable without PowerPoint.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What RESOLUTION options are available when exporting a presentation as video in PowerPoint?
options: Ultra HD (4K); Full HD (1080p); HD (720p); and Standard (480p)
Only the screen resolution of the computer
explanation: PowerPoint 2016's Create a Video dialog offers: Ultra HD (4K; 3840×2160); Full HD (1080p; 1920×1080); HD (720p; 1280×720); and Standard (480p; 852×480). Higher resolution = larger file size and longer rendering time.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: After exporting to VIDEO; an audience member can watch the PowerPoint presentation?
options: Only if they have PowerPoint installed
In any video player (Windows Media Player; VLC; YouTube; etc.) — NO PowerPoint needed — making it the best format for sharing with anyone
explanation: A presentation exported to .mp4 video plays in any video player on any device — no PowerPoint licence required. This is ideal for sharing presentations with people who don't have Microsoft Office.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the 'SECTIONS' feature in PowerPoint?
options: Divides a long presentation into NAMED SECTIONS (groups of slides) for easier navigation; organisation; and collaboration on large multi-topic presentations
explanation: Sections (Home → Section → Add Section; or right-click between slides) group slides into named sections — like chapters. In Slide Sorter view; sections are colour-coded; can be collapsed; and can be moved as a unit. Great for long presentations.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5 Chapter 5; what TYPE OF PRESENTATION do students build using Photo Album; audio; and slideshow features?
options: A PHOTO ESSAY or DIGITAL STORY — combining imported photos; background music; and automatic slide timings to create a self-running multimedia presentation
explanation: Book 5 Chapter 5's practical activity combines Photo Album (photos); Insert Audio with Play Across Slides and Loop (background music); Rehearse Timings (automatic advancement); and save as .ppsx — creating a complete self-running multimedia show.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the 'SLIDE SHOW' tab → 'HIDE SLIDE' do to a presentation?
options: Marks the selected slide to be SKIPPED during the standard slideshow — the slide number shows with a diagonal cross in the Slides panel; it can be un-hidden any time
explanation: Hide Slide (Slide Show tab → Hide Slide) excludes the selected slide from normal playback. The slide stays in the file (shown with a struck-through number in the panel) and can be revealed by un-hiding or by typing its number during the show.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To navigate DIRECTLY TO A SPECIFIC SLIDE during a running slideshow?
options: TYPE THE SLIDE NUMBER then press ENTER — the presentation jumps directly to that slide number
explanation: During a slideshow; typing a slide number and pressing Enter jumps to that slide directly. Alternatively; right-click → Go to Slide → slide name. This is useful for skipping sections or responding to audience questions.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the 'BLACK SCREEN' shortcut during a PowerPoint slideshow?
options: B or . (full stop) — pressing B or period makes the screen go BLACK; hiding the current slide from the audience (press again to return to the slide)
explanation: During a slideshow; pressing B (or . period) switches the audience's screen to solid black — useful when the presenter wants the audience to focus on discussion rather than the slide. Press B again to return to the slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; students learn to save a presentation as PDF. What is the advantage of PDF over PPSX?
options: A PDF DOES NOT REQUIRE POWERPOINT to open — it shows slides as fixed images in any PDF viewer; on any device; with no animation or interactivity but guaranteed visual fidelity
explanation: File → Export → Create PDF/XPS saves slides as PDF. Advantages: opens on any device/OS in any PDF viewer; layout is fixed (fonts; images stay exactly as designed); no PowerPoint needed. Trade-off: no animations; no interactive features.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a CUSTOM SLIDE SHOW in PowerPoint?
options: A SUBSET of slides from a presentation that you can name and run independently — (Slide Show → Custom Slide Show → Custom Shows → New) — useful for tailoring presentations for different audiences without duplicating the file
A show with a custom background
explanation: Custom Slide Shows (Slide Show → Custom Slide Show) let you select specific slides from the main presentation and save them as a named sub-show. You can then run just that subset for a particular audience without changing the original file.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What keyboard shortcut STARTS a PowerPoint slideshow from SLIDE 1?
options: F5 — starts from the very first slide regardless of which slide is currently selected
explanation: F5 starts the slideshow from Slide 1. Shift+F5 starts from the CURRENT slide. Esc ends the show. These are the standard slideshow keyboard shortcuts in PowerPoint 2016.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What keyboard shortcut STARTS a PowerPoint slideshow from the CURRENT SLIDE?
options: Shift+F5 — starts the slideshow from whichever slide is selected in Normal view
explanation: Shift+F5 starts the slideshow from the currently selected slide — useful for testing a specific slide's animations or transitions without sitting through the whole presentation from the start.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To ADD AUDIO that plays AUTOMATICALLY when a specific slide appears?
options: Insert → Audio → Audio on My PC → after inserting; set Audio Tools Playback → Start → Automatically
explanation: After inserting the audio clip; select it and go to Audio Tools Playback → Start dropdown → choose 'Automatically'. The audio will play the moment that slide appears during the show.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the AUDIO ICON that appears on a slide after inserting audio?
options: A SPEAKER ICON (loudspeaker symbol) — the default visual marker for an embedded or linked audio clip on a slide
explanation: PowerPoint displays a small speaker/loudspeaker icon on the slide to represent the embedded audio clip. You can move; resize; or format this icon; or hide it during the show using 'Hide During Show' in Playback settings.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To make background music FADE IN at the beginning of an audio clip in PowerPoint?
options: Audio Tools Playback → FADE IN (set a duration in seconds) — the audio will gradually increase from silence to full volume over the specified time
explanation: Fade In (Audio Tools Playback) smoothly increases the audio from zero to full volume over the specified number of seconds — creating a professional fade-in effect without needing separate audio editing software.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To make background music FADE OUT at the end of an audio clip?
options: Audio Tools Playback → FADE OUT (set a duration in seconds) — the audio gradually decreases to silence at the end of the clip
explanation: Fade Out (Audio Tools Playback) gradually decreases the audio to silence at the end. Combined with Loop Until Stopped and Play Across Slides; this creates professional background music that fades in at the start and out at the end.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the VOLUME control for audio in PowerPoint's Playback tab?
options: A dropdown with four settings: Low; Medium; High; and Mute — sets the default playback volume for the clip
explanation: Volume (Audio Tools Playback → Audio Options → Volume) has four settings: Low; Medium; High; and Mute. This sets the clip's default volume level within the presentation; separate from the computer's system volume.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What file format does PowerPoint EXPORT to when creating a video using 'Create a Video' (File → Export)?
options: .mp4 (MPEG-4 Video) or .wmv (Windows Media Video) — both are standard video formats
explanation: Create a Video (File → Export) offers two format options: .mp4 (recommended; widely compatible with most devices and platforms) and .wmv (Windows Media Video; legacy format for Windows Media Player). MP4 is the modern standard.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: When inserting a VIDEO from a local file; what does PowerPoint do with the video file by DEFAULT?
options: EMBEDS it inside the .pptx file — the video data is copied into the presentation so it plays even if the original video file is deleted or moved
explanation: By default; PowerPoint embeds video files inside the .pptx archive. This makes the presentation portable (plays anywhere) but increases file size. Use File → Info → Compress Media to reduce the size.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What SECTION of the RIBBON appears when you click on an embedded VIDEO object on a slide?
options: Video Tools — with FORMAT and PLAYBACK tabs that are specific to video objects
explanation: Clicking a video object selects it and displays the VIDEO TOOLS contextual tabs: FORMAT (for visual appearance — border; colour; crop; shape) and PLAYBACK (for how/when the video plays; volume; trimming; bookmarks).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'HIDE WHILE NOT PLAYING' do for a video in PowerPoint?
options: Makes the VIDEO INVISIBLE on the slide EXCEPT when it is actively playing — the slide shows a blank space in the video's position between playbacks
Hides the video from the slide panel
Removes the video from the file
explanation: Hide While Not Playing (Video Tools Playback → Video Options) makes the video object transparent/invisible when it is not playing. The video appears only when it starts playing. This prevents an awkward black or thumbnail rectangle from showing when the video is paused.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the DURATION field in the TRANSITIONS tab control?
options: The LENGTH OF TIME (in seconds) the transition ANIMATION takes to complete — for example; a Duration of 01.00 means the transition takes one second
The time before the transition starts
explanation: Duration (Transitions tab → Timing group) sets how long the transition animation lasts — the speed of the wipe; fade; push; etc. A longer duration makes the transition slower and smoother; a shorter duration makes it snappier.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the MORPH TRANSITION in PowerPoint 2016?
options: A SMART TRANSITION that moves; scales; and transforms objects that appear on BOTH the current and next slide — creates smooth animated motion without complex animation settings
explanation: Morph (Transitions → Morph) automatically animates the movement; scaling; and reshaping of objects that appear on consecutive slides. If an object is on slide 5 and slide 6; Morph smoothly animates it from its position/size on slide 5 to its position/size on slide 6.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: For MORPH transition to work correctly with text or images; what must be TRUE about objects on consecutive slides?
options: They must have the same font
Objects must share the SAME NAME in the Selection Pane (Format → Arrange → Selection Pane → rename objects) OR be duplicated slides — Morph then knows which object maps to which
They must be the same colour
They must be in the same position
explanation: Morph identifies which objects to animate between slides by matching their names in the Selection Pane. If you simply duplicate a slide and change positions; Morph works automatically. For objects added separately; rename them identically in the Selection Pane.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is SLIDE SORTER VIEW in PowerPoint (View → Slide Sorter)?
options: A view for editing slide content
A view showing ALL slides as small thumbnails — useful for REORDERING slides by dragging; DELETING; DUPLICATING; and seeing rehearsal timings below each thumbnail
explanation: Slide Sorter (View → Slide Sorter) shows all slides as a grid of small thumbnails. It is the best view for reorganising a long presentation — drag slides to new positions; delete or duplicate; and see timing information below each slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What keyboard shortcut DUPLICATES a slide in PowerPoint?
options: CTRL+D — duplicates the selected slide(s) as a copy inserted immediately after the selected slide
explanation: Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide(s) immediately — a duplicate is inserted right after the original. This is faster than Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V for copying slides within the same presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'APPLY TO ALL' in the Transitions tab do?
options: Applies the SELECTED TRANSITION (including its settings: effect options; duration; sound; advance timing) to EVERY SLIDE in the presentation — a one-click way to set a consistent transition throughout
Applies the theme to all slides
Applies the layout to all slides
explanation: Apply To All (Transitions → Timing group) copies the currently selected transition and all its settings (duration; sound; advance slide timing) to every slide — saving time when you want a consistent transition style throughout the entire presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the READING VIEW in PowerPoint?
options: A simplified SLIDESHOW VIEW within the PowerPoint window (not full-screen) — useful for reviewing the presentation with all animations and transitions playing; without switching to full-screen mode
A view that shows only text
explanation: Reading View (View → Reading View; or the Reading View button in the status bar) runs the slideshow within the PowerPoint window rather than full-screen — you can see the taskbar and switch to other apps while reviewing animations and transitions.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does FILE → INFO → CHECK COMPATIBILITY do in PowerPoint 2016?
options: Checks whether the presentation uses features that are NOT supported by OLDER versions of PowerPoint (2003; 2007; 2010) — and lists any potential issues
Checks if the file is corrupted
explanation: Check Compatibility (File → Info → Check for Issues → Check Compatibility) scans the presentation for features that would not display correctly in older PowerPoint versions — such as certain animations; transitions; or SmartArt — and gives you a report of potential issues.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'INSPECT DOCUMENT' (File → Info → Check for Issues → Inspect Document) do?
options: Searches for HIDDEN DATA in the presentation — such as speaker notes; comments; hidden slides; author metadata; personal information; and invisible objects — so you can remove them before sharing
explanation: Document Inspector finds hidden or personal information embedded in the file: comments; speaker notes; hidden slides; author name; company name; revision history; and invisible objects. Use it before sharing a presentation to ensure sensitive information is removed.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What PRINT LAYOUT prints slides with LINES for audience notes in PowerPoint?
options: HANDOUTS 3 PER PAGE — prints three slide thumbnails on the left with three horizontal lines to the right of each thumbnail for audience note-taking
explanation: Handouts 3 per page is the unique layout that adds note lines: three slide thumbnails on the left half of the page with a lined area on the right for the audience to write notes during the presentation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the DEFAULT FILE FORMAT for saving a PowerPoint 2016 presentation?
options: .pptx (PowerPoint Presentation — XML-based format introduced in Office 2007) — this is the default when you press Ctrl+S in PowerPoint 2016
explanation: PowerPoint 2016 saves in .pptx format by default — the Open XML format introduced with Office 2007. It is a compressed ZIP archive containing XML files and media. The older .ppt format (PowerPoint 97–2003) must be chosen explicitly.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Photo Album dialog; what is 'FIT TO SLIDE' layout?
options: Makes all photos the same size
ONE PHOTO PER SLIDE filling the entire slide — the photo is stretched or cropped to fill the full slide area with no margins
explanation: Fit to Slide places one photo per slide with the image filling the entire slide background — no white borders or margins. It is ideal for a dramatic full-bleed photo presentation or slideshow of large landscape images.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What type of audio file is BEST for background music in a PowerPoint presentation?
options: MP3 — a good balance of quality and FILE SIZE; widely supported by PowerPoint; small enough not to inflate the presentation file excessively
explanation: MP3 is the recommended audio format for PowerPoint presentations: it offers good audio quality at small file sizes; is universally supported; and keeps the .pptx file manageable. WAV files are very large. MIDI is low quality. FLAC is not always supported.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To INSERT AUDIO FROM A MICROPHONE directly in PowerPoint without a separate app?
options: Insert → Audio → Record Audio — opens a recording dialog where you click the red dot to start recording; then the square to stop; then name the clip and click OK to insert
explanation: Insert → Audio → Record Audio opens PowerPoint's built-in recording dialog. Click the record button (red circle); speak into the microphone; click stop (square) when done; name the clip; click OK — the audio is inserted directly on the slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: After recording audio with 'Record Audio' in PowerPoint; where does the audio appear?
options: As a SPEAKER ICON on the slide — the same as any other embedded audio; with the same Audio Tools FORMAT and PLAYBACK tabs available
explanation: Recorded audio appears as a speaker icon on the slide — identical in behaviour to inserted audio files. It has the same Audio Tools Format and Playback tabs; and the same options for trimming; volume; start settings; hiding during show; etc.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To REORDER photos in a Photo Album AFTER the album has been created?
options: Insert → Photo Album → Edit Photo Album → select a photo in the list → use the Up/Down ARROW buttons to move it; then click Update
Drag slides in Slide Sorter view
explanation: Edit Photo Album (Insert → Photo Album → Edit Photo Album) reopens the album builder. Select the photo in the list and use the Up/Down arrows to reorder it; then click Update to rebuild the album with the new order.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does SLIDE SHOW → PLAY NARRATIONS checkbox control?
options: Whether PREVIOUSLY RECORDED NARRATIONS play during the slideshow — unchecking it silences narrations so a live presenter can speak without the recording playing over them
explanation: The Play Narrations checkbox (Slide Show tab → Set Up group) toggles whether saved narration audio plays during the show. Deselect it when presenting live to an audience who should hear the presenter directly; not the recorded narration.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5; students learn to insert a VIDEO from their computer. What FORMAT is recommended for reliable playback in PowerPoint 2016?
options: .MP4 (H.264 video codec with AAC audio) — the most universally compatible video format for PowerPoint 2016 on Windows
explanation: MP4 with H.264 encoding is the recommended video format for PowerPoint 2016. It offers excellent compatibility; smaller file sizes than AVI or WMV; and smooth playback. Students are advised in Book 5 to convert videos to MP4 if they have compatibility issues.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What happens when you DOUBLE-CLICK a .ppsx file in Windows?
options: OPENS DIRECTLY in SLIDESHOW MODE — the presentation plays immediately without showing the PowerPoint editing interface
Opens in PowerPoint as a normal .pptx
Asks the user whether to edit or show
explanation: A .ppsx file (PowerPoint Show) bypasses the editing interface entirely — double-clicking it starts the slideshow from slide 1 immediately. This is the intended behaviour for distributing presentations to audiences who should only view; not edit.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the SCREEN RECORDING feature do in PowerPoint 2016 (Insert → Screen Recording)?
options: Records a PORTION OF THE COMPUTER SCREEN (you drag to select the area) as a VIDEO clip that is inserted directly on the slide — useful for software tutorials embedded in a presentation
Records the entire presentation as a video
explanation: Screen Recording (Insert → Screen Recording) opens a selection bar; you drag to choose the screen region to capture; then click Record. The recording (with audio/mouse clicks optionally included) embeds as a video clip on the slide.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does clicking 'SAVE AS' (.ppsx) do differently from normal 'SAVE' (.pptx) in PowerPoint?
options: Creates a FILE THAT OPENS DIRECTLY IN SLIDESHOW MODE — saved as a PowerPoint Show (.ppsx) rather than an editable presentation (.pptx)
explanation: Save As → PowerPoint Show (.ppsx) creates a file that is functionally identical to .pptx but with a flag that tells Windows to open it directly in Slideshow mode. The original .pptx file is preserved as the editable version; the .ppsx is for distribution.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What SLIDE SHOW → MONITOR setting does when you have TWO DISPLAYS connected?
options: Lets you specify WHICH MONITOR shows the audience view (full-screen slides) and which shows Presenter View — ensuring the audience sees slides and the presenter sees notes + controls
explanation: The Monitor dropdown (Slide Show tab → Monitors group) lets you assign which connected monitor shows the full-screen audience slides and which shows Presenter View with notes and controls — essential for dual-monitor/projector setups.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of the TIMER DISPLAY in Presenter View during a slideshow?
options: Shows BOTH the current clock time AND the ELAPSED TIME since the show started — helping the presenter stay on schedule
Shows the countdown to the next slide
explanation: Presenter View displays: elapsed time (how long since the show started — a running stopwatch) and optionally the current clock time. This helps presenters track time against their planned schedule without checking their phone or watch.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5's practical exercise; students create a multimedia presentation. What is the CORRECT ORDER of steps?
options: Save as .ppsx → Insert Audio → Rehearse Timings → Insert Photos
Insert Photo Album → Insert Audio (set to Play Across Slides and Loop) → Rehearse Timings → Save as .ppsx — completing the multimedia show
Rehearse Timings → Insert Photos → Insert Audio → Save
Insert Video → Insert Audio → Photo Album → Save as .pdf
explanation: The logical sequence is: Insert Photo Album first (creates the presentation structure with slides); Insert Audio with appropriate settings; Rehearse Timings to set automatic advance timings; Save as .ppsx for distribution.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a TRANSITION SOUND in PowerPoint (Transitions → Timing → Sound)?
options: A SOUND EFFECT played DURING the slide transition — for example: a camera click; applause; whoosh; drum roll — chosen from PowerPoint's built-in sounds or from an audio file on the computer
The audio clip inserted on the slide
explanation: Transition Sound (Transitions tab → Sound dropdown) plays a built-in or custom audio effect (camera; applause; chime; whoosh; etc.) during the transition animation. It is separate from any audio clip embedded on the slide itself.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does 'ADVANCE SLIDE: AFTER' (a set time) do in the Transitions tab?
options: Automatically ADVANCES THE SLIDE to the next one after the specified time elapses — enabling self-running presentations without the need for manual clicks
Shows the slide for that number of minutes
Fades the slide after the time
explanation: Advance Slide → After (Transitions → Timing) sets the slide to automatically advance after the specified time (e.g. 00:05:00 = 5 seconds). This is what Rehearse Timings records — the saved time for each slide appears in this field.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the purpose of LINKING a video file in PowerPoint (rather than embedding it)?
options: Linking keeps the video file SEPARATE from the .pptx — the presentation stores only a pointer to the file; resulting in a SMALLER .pptx file; but the video file must always stay in the same relative location
explanation: When you choose 'Insert and Link' instead of 'Insert' for a video; PowerPoint stores only the path to the video file. The .pptx stays small but requires the linked video file to be in the same folder whenever the presentation is opened.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the REMOVE BACKGROUND feature do in PowerPoint (available for images via Picture Tools → Format → Remove Background)?
options: Automatically removes the background from a PHOTO on a slide — keeping the main subject and making the rest transparent — using AI-based detection with pink highlights
explanation: Remove Background (Picture Tools Format → Remove Background) uses automatic detection to identify and remove the photo background — the background turns pink/magenta in the edit view. You can mark areas to keep or remove; click Keep Changes to apply.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: When a SLIDE TRANSITION is set to 'ON MOUSE CLICK' and the presenter presses the SPACEBAR during a show; what happens?
options: The spacebar ADVANCES the slide — it acts like a mouse click; progressing to the next slide or the next animation on the current slide
explanation: During a PowerPoint slideshow; pressing the SPACEBAR is equivalent to a left-click — it advances the slide or triggers the next animation. This is useful when the presenter cannot reach the mouse or is using a remote without a dedicated 'next' button mapping.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does pressing RIGHT ARROW key do during a PowerPoint slideshow?
options: Advances to the next slide or next animation — the same as a mouse click or spacebar press
explanation: Right Arrow (and Down Arrow; Enter; Page Down) all advance the slideshow forward — next animation or next slide. Left Arrow (and Up Arrow; Page Up; Backspace) go backwards. These are the standard keyboard navigation keys during a slideshow.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What VIEW shows ALL SLIDES as equal-sized thumbnails and is most useful for REORDERING a long presentation?
options: SLIDE SORTER VIEW (View → Slide Sorter) — shows all slides as a grid; drag to reorder
explanation: Slide Sorter (View → Slide Sorter) is the purpose-built view for managing the order of slides. Drag any slide to a new position. Slides can also be selected with Ctrl+Click and moved as a group; or deleted; or duplicated.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the PAPER CLIP icon on a slide thumbnail in the slide panel indicate in PowerPoint?
options: A FILE ATTACHMENT — a file has been attached to the slide using Insert → Object or as a linked object
An audio clip is on that slide
explanation: Actually in standard PowerPoint 2016; a speaker icon on a slide thumbnail in the slide panel indicates an AUDIO clip on that slide. The paper clip icon indicates an OLE-embedded object or file attachment. Students should know that audio on a slide shows a speaker in the panel.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In Book 5 Chapter 5; after the multimedia presentation is complete; students are asked to share it. What is the BEST way to share so the recipient does NOT need PowerPoint installed?
options: Export as VIDEO (.mp4) — plays in any video player on any device without PowerPoint; OR Export as PDF — opens in any PDF viewer
explanation: Exporting as .mp4 video is the best sharing method: plays in any video player; on any operating system; on any device; without Microsoft Office. PDF is the second option for static slide viewing. Both are better than .ppsx (which still requires PowerPoint or a compatible app).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the INTERNET?
options: A single computer owned by a company
A GLOBAL NETWORK of millions of interconnected computers and devices that share information and resources using agreed-upon protocols (rules)
A wireless signal from a router
explanation: The Internet is the world's largest network — a vast collection of interconnected computers; servers; routers; and devices spanning the globe; communicating using shared protocols (especially TCP/IP).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the WORLD WIDE WEB (WWW)?
options: A COLLECTION OF WEBSITES and web pages stored on web servers and accessed via the Internet using a web browser — it is only one part of the Internet
A type of cable used to connect computers
explanation: The WWW is a SERVICE that runs on the Internet — a system of interlinked web pages and websites using HTTP/HTTPS. The Internet also carries email; file transfers; streaming; gaming; etc. — the Web is just one of these services.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a WEB BROWSER?
options: A SOFTWARE APPLICATION (e.g. Microsoft Edge; Google Chrome; Mozilla Firefox; Safari) used to ACCESS and DISPLAY websites and web pages on the Internet
explanation: A web browser is an application that sends requests to web servers; receives HTML/CSS/JavaScript files; and renders them as visual web pages for the user. Popular browsers include Microsoft Edge; Google Chrome; Firefox; and Safari.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is MICROSOFT EDGE?
options: Microsoft's built-in WEB BROWSER included with Windows 10 and 11 — it replaced Internet Explorer as Microsoft's default browser; built on the Chromium engine
explanation: Microsoft Edge (introduced with Windows 10) is Microsoft's modern browser. Since 2020 it has been built on the Chromium engine (the same open-source engine as Chrome) while remaining distinct from Chrome.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a URL (Uniform Resource Locator)?
options: The UNIQUE WEB ADDRESS of a page or resource on the Internet — for example: https://www.bbc.com/news — that browsers use to locate and retrieve it
explanation: A URL is the complete address that uniquely identifies a resource on the Web. Parts include: protocol (https://); domain name (www.bbc.com); path (/news). Typing or clicking a URL takes the browser to that exact resource.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does HTTP stand for?
options: HyperText Transfer Protocol — the rules for transmitting web pages between servers and browsers over the Internet
explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the foundational protocol of the Web — the set of rules governing how a web browser requests a web page and how a web server responds. HTTPS adds encryption (SSL/TLS) for security.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does HTTPS mean and why is it important?
options: HyperText Transfer Protocol SECURE — an ENCRYPTED version of HTTP that protects data exchanged between your browser and the web server using SSL/TLS; shown as a padlock in the address bar
explanation: HTTPS encrypts all data between the browser and server; so passwords; payment details; and personal information cannot be intercepted by third parties. Websites without HTTPS show 'Not secure' in modern browsers.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a SEARCH ENGINE?
options: A website that stores files for download
A WEB SERVICE (e.g. Google; Bing; Yahoo) that crawls the Internet to index web pages and then lets users find relevant pages by typing SEARCH QUERIES (keywords)
explanation: A search engine uses automated programs called 'crawlers' or 'spiders' to index web content; then provides a search interface where users type keywords and receive ranked results — web pages that match the query.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is GOOGLE?
options: The world's most popular SEARCH ENGINE — accessed at www.google.com — that uses complex algorithms to rank billions of web pages by relevance to search queries
explanation: Google Search (www.google.com) is the dominant search engine; used for the majority of web searches globally. It also offers many other services (Gmail; Maps; Drive; YouTube); but its core product is the search engine.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is MICROSOFT BING?
options: Microsoft's SEARCH ENGINE (www.bing.com) — built into Windows and Microsoft Edge as the default search engine; with features like image search; video search; and news search
explanation: Bing (www.bing.com) is Microsoft's search engine; integrated as the default in Microsoft Edge and Cortana. It offers web; image; video; and news search; and powers some other search services.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: In the Microsoft Edge ADDRESS BAR; you can BOTH type a URL to go directly to a website AND type a search query. When you type a search term without a URL; Edge does what?
options: Sends the search query to the DEFAULT SEARCH ENGINE (Bing by default in Edge; or whichever is set) and shows results
explanation: Edge's address bar (also called Omnibox) handles both URLs and search queries. If you type a website address; it navigates there. If you type search terms; it passes them to the default search engine (Bing by default) and shows results.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is the HOMEPAGE in a web browser?
options: The WEB PAGE that opens automatically when you launch the browser or click the Home button — set in browser Settings
explanation: The homepage is the page a browser loads on startup or when the Home button is clicked. Users can set it to any URL (e.g. a school website; Google; a news site) in the browser's Settings.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a FAVOURITE / BOOKMARK in a web browser?
options: A SAVED SHORTCUT to a website or web page that lets you return to it quickly without retyping the URL — saved via the star icon in Edge or Ctrl+D
explanation: Favourites (called Bookmarks in Chrome/Firefox; Favorites in Edge) save URLs of web pages you want to return to. In Edge; click the star icon in the address bar or press Ctrl+D to save a favourite.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the BACK BUTTON (←) do in a web browser?
options: Goes BACK to the PREVIOUS web page in the current tab's history
explanation: The Back button (← arrow; or Alt+Left Arrow; or Backspace) navigates to the previously visited page in the current tab's browsing history — undoing the last navigation.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does the REFRESH / RELOAD button do in a web browser?
options: Goes back to the previous page
RE-LOADS the CURRENT web page — downloading a fresh copy from the server; updating any content that may have changed since the page was last loaded
explanation: Refresh (F5; Ctrl+R; or the circular arrow button) reloads the current page from the server — useful when content has changed (a news site; a live score) or a page did not load correctly.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a BROWSER TAB?
options: A SEPARATE BROWSING SESSION within the same browser window — each tab shows an independent web page; letting you open multiple websites simultaneously without opening multiple windows
A section of a web page
explanation: Browser tabs allow multiple web pages open in one browser window. Click the + button to open a new tab; Ctrl+T is the keyboard shortcut. Each tab has its own address bar; back/forward history; and can be refreshed independently.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What keyboard shortcut opens a NEW TAB in most web browsers?
options: Ctrl+T — opens a new empty tab in the same browser window
explanation: Ctrl+T opens a new tab in most major browsers (Edge; Chrome; Firefox; Safari). Ctrl+N opens a new browser window. Ctrl+W closes the current tab.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does CTRL+W do in a web browser?
explanation: Ctrl+W closes the current active tab in most browsers. If it's the only tab; some browsers close the entire window. Use Ctrl+Shift+T to reopen a recently closed tab.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is PRIVATE BROWSING (InPrivate in Edge; Incognito in Chrome)?
options: Browsing that is invisible to the internet
A BROWSING MODE where the browser does NOT save the browsing history; cookies; form data; or passwords from that session — closed when the window is closed
explanation: Private/InPrivate/Incognito mode prevents the browser from saving local history; cookies; and login info from that session. However; websites; ISPs; and network administrators can still see your activity — it only prevents LOCAL storage of data.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To open an INCOGNITO window in Microsoft Edge (called InPrivate)?
options: Ctrl+Shift+N — opens a new InPrivate (private browsing) window where browsing history; cookies; and site data are not saved locally
explanation: Ctrl+Shift+N opens a new InPrivate window in Microsoft Edge. The window is marked with an InPrivate badge. All browsing done there is not saved to the local profile when the window closes.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is an EMAIL ADDRESS? Give an example of its structure.
options: A unique IDENTIFIER for an email account in the format: username@domain.com — for example: student@school.edu — where @ separates the username from the domain
explanation: An email address has two parts separated by @: the username (before @) and the domain (after @). For example: john.doe@gmail.com — 'john.doe' is the username; 'gmail.com' is the email service domain.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is CYBERBULLYING?
options: Using digital technology (social media; messaging; gaming; email) to REPEATEDLY HARASS; THREATEN; HUMILIATE; or EMBARRASS another person — a form of bullying that occurs online or via devices
explanation: Cyberbullying is online bullying: sending mean messages; spreading rumours digitally; posting embarrassing content; impersonating someone; or excluding someone deliberately online. It can occur on any digital platform and has serious effects on mental health.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What should you do if you experience or witness CYBERBULLYING?
options: DO NOT respond to the bully; SAVE EVIDENCE (screenshots); BLOCK the bully; and TELL A TRUSTED ADULT (parent; teacher; school counsellor) immediately
explanation: The recommended response to cyberbullying: (1) Don't respond or retaliate — it can make things worse. (2) Save/screenshot evidence. (3) Block the person on the platform. (4) Report to the platform (most have reporting tools). (5) Tell a trusted adult immediately.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a PHISHING ATTACK?
options: A FRAUDULENT ATTEMPT to steal personal information (passwords; credit card numbers; etc.) by disguising as a TRUSTWORTHY source — usually through fake emails; websites; or messages that look legitimate
A way to speed up internet connections
explanation: Phishing uses deceptive emails; fake websites; or messages that appear to be from banks; government agencies; or known companies to trick people into revealing passwords; financial details; or personal information. Always check the actual email address and URL carefully.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is SPAM?
options: UNSOLICITED (unwanted) BULK EMAIL — usually commercial advertising; scams; or phishing attempts — sent to large numbers of recipients without their consent
explanation: Spam is junk email sent in bulk — typically advertising products; promoting scams; or attempting phishing. Email providers use spam filters to identify and divert suspected spam to the Junk/Spam folder automatically.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is MALWARE?
options: Malicious Software — programs designed to HARM; DISRUPT; or GAIN UNAUTHORISED ACCESS to a computer system — types include viruses; worms; Trojans; ransomware; and spyware
explanation: Malware (Malicious Software) is any software intentionally designed to cause harm — including viruses (spread by replication); Trojans (disguised as legitimate software); worms (spread across networks); ransomware (encrypts files for ransom); and spyware (monitors user activity).
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a COMPUTER VIRUS?
options: A TYPE OF MALWARE that ATTACHES ITSELF to legitimate files and REPLICATES — spreading to other files and computers when infected files are shared; it can damage data; slow the system; or cause other harm
explanation: A computer virus is malware that inserts its code into legitimate programs or files. When the infected file is run; the virus replicates and may deliver its 'payload' — deleting files; corrupting data; or creating backdoors. It spreads via file sharing; email attachments; or downloads.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is ANTIVIRUS SOFTWARE?
options: Software that speeds up the internet
A SECURITY PROGRAM that detects; prevents; and removes malware (viruses; worms; Trojans; etc.) from a computer — examples include Windows Defender; Avast; Norton; and Kaspersky
explanation: Antivirus software scans files; email attachments; and downloads for known malware signatures and suspicious behaviour. It provides real-time protection; scheduled scans; and quarantine features. Windows 10/11 includes Windows Defender Antivirus built in.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is a STRONG PASSWORD? Which of these is strongest?
options: P@55w0rd!#X9qR — long; uses uppercase; lowercase; numbers; and special characters; making it very hard to guess or crack
explanation: A strong password: at least 8–12 characters (longer is better); mixes uppercase and lowercase letters; numbers; and special characters (! @ # $ % etc.); does not use obvious words; names; or dates. Never reuse passwords across accounts.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What is TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION (2FA)?
options: A SECURITY METHOD that requires TWO forms of verification to log in — typically a PASSWORD (something you know) plus a SECOND FACTOR such as a code sent to your phone (something you have)
explanation: 2FA adds a second layer of security: even if someone steals your password; they still need the second factor (a phone-sent code; a fingerprint; or a security key) to access your account. Most websites offer 2FA in account security settings.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: Why should you NEVER share personal information (full name; address; phone; school name) with strangers ONLINE?
options: Because it is against the law
Because strangers online may not be who they claim to be — sharing personal information with strangers online puts you at risk of identity theft; stalking; fraud; or other harms
Because the internet is always slow
explanation: Personal information shared online can be used for: identity theft (using your details fraudulently); location tracking (address/school reveals where you are); targeted scams; or contact from dangerous strangers. Never share personal details in public online spaces.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: What does CTRL+F do in a WEB BROWSER or document?
options: Finds (SEARCHES) for a word or phrase within the current web page or document — opens a search bar where you type the text and the browser highlights all matching instances on the page
explanation: Ctrl+F opens the 'Find' bar in browsers and most applications. Type a word or phrase; the browser searches the current page and highlights all matches; showing how many were found (e.g. '3 of 17'). Press Enter or F3 to jump between matches.
subject: Grade 5 Computing

text: To DOWNLOAD A FILE from the Internet in Edge or Chrome?
