explanation: DIV performs integer division, e.g. 7 DIV 3 = 2.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a variable in an algorithm?
options: To store data that may change during execution
explanation: A variable is a named storage location whose value can be read or changed during algorithm execution.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which algorithm type repeatedly halves the data set?
explanation: Binary search repeatedly halves the search space, giving O(log n) efficiency.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: An algorithm's correctness can be verified by:
options: Testing with trace tables and sample data
explanation: Trace tables and test data allow manual verification that the algorithm produces the correct output for given inputs.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In Cambridge pseudocode, ELSE is used with:
explanation: ELSE is part of an IF … THEN … ELSE … ENDIF construct, providing an alternative branch.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A nested loop means:
explanation: A nested loop has one loop placed inside another; the inner loop completes all its iterations for each iteration of the outer loop.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the time complexity of searching an unsorted list of n elements using linear search?
explanation: Linear search must check up to n elements in the worst case, giving O(n) time complexity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is an example of a counting algorithm?
options: Counting how many even numbers are in a list
explanation: A counting algorithm iterates through data and increments a counter each time a condition (e.g. even number) is met.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Totalling algorithm means:
options: Adding up all values in a list
explanation: A totalling algorithm sums all values in a dataset.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is "stepwise refinement" in algorithm design?
options: Running the algorithm step by step on hardware
Gradually adding more detail to each step of an outline algorithm
explanation: Stepwise refinement (top-down design) starts with a high-level description and progressively adds more detail to each step.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which operator checks equality in Cambridge pseudocode?
explanation: In Cambridge IGCSE pseudocode, = is the equality comparison operator (e.g. IF x = 5 THEN).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does an algorithm with O(n²) complexity mean practically?
options: Execution time grows quadratically with input size
It is always faster than O(n)
It requires n bytes of memory
explanation: O(n²) complexity means doubling the input size quadruples the execution time — it grows quadratically.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: The "mid" index in binary search is calculated as:
explanation: The midpoint is (low + high) DIV 2, the integer average of the current search boundaries.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a constant in an algorithm?
options: A value that changes during execution
A value that stays the same throughout execution
explanation: A constant holds a fixed value that does not change while the algorithm runs, unlike a variable.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of these is the BEST definition of computational thinking?
options: Using a computer to solve problems
A way to think about problems so that a computer can help solve them
explanation: Computational thinking is an approach to problem solving that uses concepts like decomposition, abstraction, pattern recognition and algorithms — making problems solvable by computers.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a variable in programming?
options: A fixed value that never changes
A named memory location that stores a value which can change
explanation: A variable is a named memory location whose stored value can be read and modified during program execution.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which data type stores whole numbers?
explanation: An integer data type stores whole numbers (positive, negative, or zero) with no fractional part.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does the Boolean data type store?
explanation: A Boolean variable holds only one of two values: TRUE or FALSE.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is concatenation?
explanation: Concatenation joins (links) two or more strings end-to-end to form a single string.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an array?
options: A single variable storing one value
A collection of values of the same type stored under one name
explanation: An array is a data structure that stores multiple values of the same type under a single identifier, accessed by index.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In most programming languages, what index does the first element of an array have?
explanation: Most languages (Python, Java, C) use zero-based indexing, so the first element is at index 0.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a function (or procedure) in programming?
options: A named, reusable block of code
explanation: A function/procedure is a named block of code that performs a specific task and can be called multiple times.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does the term "parameter" mean in a function?
options: A variable declared outside the function
A value passed into the function when it is called
explanation: A parameter is a variable in the function's definition that receives the value (argument) passed when the function is called.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a RETURN statement in a function?
options: To send a value back to the calling code
explanation: RETURN sends a computed value back to the code that called the function.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a local variable?
options: A variable accessible throughout the whole program
A variable defined inside a function, accessible only within it
explanation: A local variable exists only within the function or block where it is declared and cannot be accessed elsewhere.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a global variable?
options: A variable only inside one function
A variable accessible from anywhere in the program
explanation: A global variable is declared outside any function and can be read (and usually modified) from any part of the program.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: String LENGTH function returns:
options: The number of characters in the string
explanation: LENGTH (or LEN) returns the total number of characters in a string, including spaces.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does SUBSTRING(str, 2, 3) typically return?
explanation: SUBSTRING extracts a portion of a string; here, 3 characters beginning at position 2.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of INPUT in a program?
options: To read data entered by the user
explanation: INPUT reads a value supplied by the user (or another source) and stores it in a variable.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does the operator AND do in a condition?
options: Returns TRUE if either operand is TRUE
Returns TRUE only if both operands are TRUE
explanation: AND returns TRUE only when both conditions on either side are TRUE.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does the NOT operator do?
explanation: NOT flips a Boolean: NOT TRUE → FALSE, NOT FALSE → TRUE.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a syntax error?
options: A violation of the grammar rules of the programming language
explanation: A syntax error occurs when code breaks the language's grammar rules (e.g. missing colon, misspelled keyword) and prevents compilation/interpretation.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A logic error causes:
options: The program to refuse to run
The program to run but produce wrong results
explanation: A logic error allows the program to run without crashing but the output is incorrect due to a flaw in the algorithm.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a runtime error?
options: An error in the algorithm design
An error that occurs while the program is executing
explanation: A runtime error (e.g. division by zero, out-of-bounds access) happens during execution and causes the program to crash.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which type of testing uses all possible input values?
explanation: Exhaustive testing tests every possible input, which is theoretically ideal but often impractical for large input sets.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Boundary testing tests:
options: Values at or just inside/outside the limits of valid input
explanation: Boundary (boundary-value) testing focuses on the edges of valid input ranges, where errors most commonly occur.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the Real (Float) data type used for?
explanation: A real (floating-point) number stores values with a decimal component, e.g. 3.14.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does UCASE("hello") return?
explanation: UCASE (or UPPER) converts all characters in a string to uppercase.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does LCASE("WORLD") return?
explanation: LCASE (or LOWER) converts all characters in a string to lowercase.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A FOR loop is best used when:
options: The number of iterations is unknown
The number of iterations is known in advance
You need to check a condition first
You want to define a function
explanation: A FOR loop (count-controlled loop) is ideal when the number of repetitions is known before the loop begins.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an ELSE IF (ELIF) clause used for?
options: Testing additional conditions after an initial IF
explanation: ELSE IF tests another condition when the initial IF condition is false, providing multiple alternative branches.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the difference between = and == in many languages?
options: = assigns a value; == compares two values for equality
explanation: In languages like Python and Java, = is the assignment operator and == is the equality comparison operator.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a 2D array?
options: An array stored as rows and columns (a matrix)
A function that returns two values
explanation: A 2D array organises data in rows and columns, accessed by two indices (row, column), like a table.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a comment in code?
options: To make the program run faster
To explain the code for human readers without affecting execution
explanation: Comments are lines of text in code (ignored by the interpreter/compiler) that explain the code's purpose to human readers.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is valid pseudocode for a FOR loop?
options: FOR x ← 1 TO 10 DO … NEXT x
explanation: The Cambridge IGCSE pseudocode syntax for a FOR loop is: FOR var ← start TO end DO … NEXT var.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the ASCII code of character 'A'?
explanation: The ASCII decimal code for uppercase 'A' is 65.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: CHR(65) returns:
explanation: CHR converts an ASCII/Unicode code point to its corresponding character; CHR(65) = 'A'.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: ASC("B") returns:
explanation: ASC returns the ASCII code of the first character; ASC("B") = 66.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does it mean when a variable is "declared"?
options: Its name and data type are defined so memory can be reserved
It is printed to the screen
explanation: Declaring a variable tells the compiler/interpreter its name and data type so the appropriate amount of memory can be allocated.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is modular programming?
options: Breaking a program into separate, independent modules or functions
Writing code on a mobile device
explanation: Modular programming decomposes a program into smaller, self-contained modules (functions/procedures), making it easier to write, test, and maintain.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does casting mean in programming?
options: Converting a value from one data type to another
explanation: Casting (type conversion) converts a value from its current data type to another, e.g. INT("42") converts the string "42" to integer 42.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is a valid reason to use functions?
options: To make code harder to read
To avoid rewriting the same code multiple times
explanation: Functions promote code reuse — define once, call many times — reducing repetition and making maintenance easier.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the difference between a function and a procedure?
options: A function returns a value; a procedure does not
A procedure returns a value; a function does not
Functions use loops; procedures do not
explanation: In most contexts, a function returns a value to the caller while a procedure (void function) performs actions without returning a value.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: An infinite loop occurs when:
options: A loop's termination condition is never met
A loop skips its first iteration
explanation: An infinite loop happens when the exit condition is never satisfied, causing the loop to run indefinitely.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the scope of a variable?
options: The region of the program where it is accessible
explanation: Scope defines which parts of a program can access (read/modify) a particular variable — local vs. global scope.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a sentinel value?
options: A special value used to signal the end of input
The first value in an array
explanation: A sentinel value is a special marker (e.g. -1 or "STOP") that signals the end of input data, terminating a loop.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: INT(3.9) returns:
explanation: INT truncates toward zero, returning 3 for INT(3.9).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: ROUND(3.567, 2) returns:
explanation: ROUND(3.567, 2) rounds to 2 decimal places, giving 3.57.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a CASE (SELECT CASE) statement used for?
options: Choosing between multiple specific values of a variable
explanation: A CASE statement tests a variable against several specific values and executes the matching branch, as an alternative to many IF/ELSE IF chains.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Robust programming means:
options: Running programs only on powerful hardware
Writing code that handles invalid/unexpected inputs without crashing
explanation: Robust programs validate input and handle edge cases gracefully, preventing crashes from unexpected user input.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of input validation?
options: To ensure user input meets expected criteria before processing
explanation: Input validation checks that data entered by the user is of the correct type, format, and range before using it in the program.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "dry run" mean in the context of programming?
options: Manually tracing through code to check logic
explanation: Dry running means manually executing code on paper (or mentally), tracking variable values step by step, to verify correctness.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which operator is used for integer division in Cambridge pseudocode?
explanation: DIV performs integer division in Cambridge IGCSE pseudocode, e.g. 10 DIV 3 = 3.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a stack overflow error related to?
options: Excessive recursion that exhausts the call stack
explanation: Stack overflow occurs when recursive calls (or deep function calls) exceed the call stack's capacity, crashing the program.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the benefit of using named constants instead of "magic numbers" in code?
options: Easier to understand and maintain — one place to change the value
explanation: Named constants (e.g. MAX_SIZE = 100) make code self-documenting and easier to update — change the constant once instead of finding every hard-coded number.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does a truth table show?
options: The output of a logic gate for every combination of inputs
explanation: A truth table lists all possible input combinations and their corresponding outputs for a logic expression or circuit.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: An AND gate outputs 1 only when:
explanation: An AND gate produces output 1 only when all its inputs are 1.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: An OR gate outputs 1 when:
explanation: An OR gate produces output 1 when one or more of its inputs are 1.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A NOT gate:
explanation: A NOT gate (inverter) has one input and one output; it outputs the logical complement (1→0, 0→1).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: How many rows does a truth table with 2 inputs have?
explanation: With 2 inputs, there are 2² = 4 possible combinations (00, 01, 10, 11).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: How many rows does a truth table with 3 inputs have?
explanation: With 3 inputs, there are 2³ = 8 possible input combinations.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the Boolean expression for an AND gate with inputs A and B?
explanation: AND is represented as A · B (multiplication dot) or A AND B in Boolean algebra.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the Boolean expression for an OR gate with inputs A and B?
explanation: OR is represented as A + B (addition) or A OR B in Boolean algebra.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does the bar over a variable (Ā) represent?
explanation: A bar over a variable (Ā) denotes logical NOT — the complement of A.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A NAND gate outputs:
options: The same as an AND gate
The opposite of an AND gate (NOT AND)
The same as an OR gate
explanation: A NAND gate is a NOT-AND; it outputs 0 only when all inputs are 1, and 1 otherwise.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A NOR gate outputs:
options: 1 only when all inputs are 0 (NOT OR)
explanation: A NOR gate is a NOT-OR; it outputs 1 only when all inputs are 0.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: An XOR (exclusive OR) gate outputs 1 when:
explanation: XOR outputs 1 when the inputs are different (one 0 and one 1), and 0 when they are the same.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which logic gate is used to implement addition in an Arithmetic Logic Unit?
explanation: XOR is used for the sum bit in a binary half-adder because it outputs 1 when inputs differ, matching binary addition of unlike bits.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the output of NOT 1?
explanation: NOT 1 = 0; the NOT gate inverts 1 to 0.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Evaluate: 1 AND 0
explanation: 1 AND 0 = 0 because both inputs must be 1 for AND to output 1.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Evaluate: 0 OR 1
explanation: 0 OR 1 = 1 because at least one input is 1.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is De Morgan's first law?
options: NOT(A AND B) = NOT A AND NOT B
NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B
NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B
A AND B = A OR B
explanation: De Morgan's first law: NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B. It converts a NAND to NOT-OR.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is De Morgan's second law?
options: NOT(A OR B) = NOT A OR NOT B
NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B
NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B
A OR B = A AND B
explanation: De Morgan's second law: NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B. It converts a NOR to NOT-AND.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which law states A AND 1 = A?
explanation: The identity law for AND states A · 1 = A; ANDing with 1 leaves a value unchanged.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which law states A OR 0 = A?
explanation: The identity law for OR: A + 0 = A; ORing with 0 leaves a value unchanged.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Simplify: A AND 0
explanation: A · 0 = 0 (null law for AND): ANDing anything with 0 gives 0.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Simplify: A OR 1
explanation: A + 1 = 1 (null law for OR): ORing with 1 always gives 1.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Simplify: NOT(NOT A)
explanation: Double negation: NOT(NOT A) = A.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the complement law for AND?
explanation: Complement law for AND: A · Ā = 0; a variable ANDed with its complement is always 0.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the complement law for OR?
explanation: Complement law for OR: A + Ā = 1; a variable ORed with its complement is always 1.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In a logic diagram, which symbol represents an AND gate?
options: A flat-backed shape with a curved front
A D-shaped gate with a flat back
explanation: The AND gate uses a D-shape with a flat input side; the OR gate uses a curved (shield) shape.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: How is a NOT gate shown in a logic diagram?
options: A triangle with a bubble (small circle) on the output
explanation: A NOT gate (inverter) is drawn as a triangle pointing right with a small circle (bubble) on the output.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the idempotent law for AND?
explanation: Idempotent law for AND: A · A = A; ANDing a variable with itself gives the same variable.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the idempotent law for OR?
explanation: Idempotent law for OR: A + A = A.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Evaluate: (1 AND 1) OR (0 AND 1)
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which gate can be used to build any other gate (universal gate)?
explanation: NAND is a universal gate — any other Boolean function can be implemented using only NAND gates.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A half adder adds two bits and produces:
options: A sum bit and a carry bit
explanation: A half adder takes two 1-bit inputs and produces a Sum bit (XOR) and a Carry bit (AND).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: The Sum output of a half adder is produced by:
explanation: The Sum bit = A XOR B; the XOR gate produces 1 when the inputs differ.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: The Carry output of a half adder is produced by:
explanation: The Carry bit = A AND B; carry is only generated when both bits are 1.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does it mean to "simplify" a Boolean expression?
options: Reduce it to the simplest equivalent form using fewer gates
explanation: Boolean simplification uses laws (identity, De Morgan's, etc.) to find a logically equivalent but simpler expression, reducing circuit complexity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Evaluate: NOT(1 AND 0)
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Evaluate: NOT(0 OR 0)
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the absorption law (first form)?
options: A AND B = B AND A
explanation: Absorption law first form: A · (A + B) = A. The OR term is "absorbed" by A.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: The commutative law of Boolean algebra states:
options: A AND B = B AND A (and A OR B = B OR A)
A AND B = A OR B
A AND (B AND C) = (A AND B) AND C
explanation: The commutative law: A · B = B · A and A + B = B + A — order of operands does not affect the result.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: The distributive law (AND over OR) states:
options: A AND (B OR C) = (A AND B) OR (A AND C)
A OR (B AND C) = (A OR B) AND (A OR C)
explanation: Distributive law for AND over OR: A · (B + C) = A·B + A·C, analogous to arithmetic distribution.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Logic gates are built from:
explanation: Modern logic gates are constructed from transistors (usually MOSFETs) acting as fast electronic switches.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A complete truth table for a circuit with 4 inputs has how many rows?
explanation: With 4 inputs, there are 2⁴ = 16 possible input combinations.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which law allows: A OR (A AND B) = A?
explanation: Absorption law second form: A + (A · B) = A.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Evaluate: (A AND NOT A) OR B where A=1, B=0
explanation: A AND NOT A = 1 AND 0 = 0; 0 OR 0 = 0.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of drawing a logic diagram?
options: To show the physical size of components
To represent the logical structure of a circuit using gate symbols
To create a truth table automatically
explanation: A logic diagram uses standard gate symbols and connecting wires to visually represent how a Boolean function is implemented in hardware.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: NOR is known as another universal gate. This means:
options: Any logic function can be built using only NOR gates
It produces the same output as XOR
explanation: Like NAND, NOR is universal — every Boolean function (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) can be constructed from NOR gates alone.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Simplify: A AND NOT A OR B (evaluate AND before OR)
explanation: A · Ā = 0 (complement law); 0 OR B = B (identity law). Result: B.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Boolean algebra uses which number system?
explanation: Boolean algebra operates on binary values: 0 (FALSE) and 1 (TRUE).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In logic circuit design, minimising the number of gates achieves:
options: Lower cost, less power consumption, and higher reliability
explanation: Fewer gates mean cheaper hardware, less power usage, less heat, and fewer failure points.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Evaluate: 1 XOR 1
explanation: XOR outputs 0 when both inputs are the same (1 XOR 1 = 0).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a programming language?
options: A formal notation used to instruct a computer to perform tasks
explanation: A programming language is a formal set of instructions, syntax, and semantics used to write programs that a computer can execute.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is machine code?
options: Binary instructions directly executed by the CPU
explanation: Machine code is the lowest-level language — sequences of binary (0s and 1s) directly understood and executed by the CPU.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is assembly language?
options: A low-level language using mnemonics (e.g. ADD, MOV) for machine instructions
explanation: Assembly language uses human-readable mnemonics (ADD, MOV, JMP) that correspond one-to-one with machine code instructions.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What converts assembly language to machine code?
explanation: An assembler translates assembly language source code into machine code (binary) that the CPU can execute.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a high-level language?
options: A language that runs directly on hardware
A language closer to human language, independent of hardware architecture
explanation: A high-level language (Python, Java, C++) uses English-like syntax and abstracts away hardware details, making programming easier.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a compiler?
options: A program that executes code line by line
A program that translates the entire source code into machine code before execution
explanation: A compiler translates the complete high-level source code into machine code (or bytecode) in one step before the program runs.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an interpreter?
options: A program that translates and executes source code line by line at runtime
explanation: An interpreter reads, translates, and executes source code one instruction at a time during runtime, without producing a separate compiled file.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is one advantage of a compiled program over an interpreted one?
options: Faster execution at runtime (no translation overhead)
explanation: Once compiled, the program runs as native machine code without re-translation, making execution faster than interpretation.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is one advantage of an interpreter over a compiler?
options: Easier to test and debug interactively; immediate feedback
explanation: Interpreters allow interactive testing and give immediate feedback on errors, making development and debugging more convenient.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is source code?
options: The human-readable program written in a high-level or assembly language
explanation: Source code is the human-readable text of a program written in a programming language, before translation.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is object code?
options: The machine code output produced by a compiler
explanation: Object code is the low-level (usually machine) code produced by a compiler from source code, ready to link and execute.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is a high-level language?
explanation: Python is a high-level language with human-readable syntax; assembly and machine code are low-level.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does an IDE (Integrated Development Environment) provide?
options: A combined editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger, and other tools in one application
explanation: An IDE integrates a code editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger, syntax highlighting, and other developer tools into a single application.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is syntax highlighting in an IDE?
options: Coloring different parts of code (keywords, strings, etc.) to improve readability
explanation: Syntax highlighting uses colors to differentiate keywords, strings, comments, and other code elements, making code easier to read.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a debugger used for?
options: Finding and fixing errors by allowing step-by-step execution and variable inspection
explanation: A debugger lets programmers pause execution, step through code one line at a time, and inspect variable values to find and fix bugs.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a low-level language?
options: A language closely tied to the hardware architecture (machine code or assembly)
explanation: Low-level languages (machine code, assembly) closely map to CPU instructions and are hardware-specific.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is an advantage of low-level languages?
options: Direct hardware control and maximum execution speed
explanation: Low-level code runs directly on hardware with no abstraction overhead, giving maximum speed and direct hardware control.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which is a disadvantage of low-level languages?
options: They are harder to write, read, and maintain than high-level languages
explanation: Low-level code is complex, harder to understand, and machine-specific, making development slow and maintenance difficult.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "portability" mean for a programming language?
options: The ability to run the same source code on different hardware/OS without change
explanation: A portable language allows the same source code to run on different platforms (Windows, Linux, Mac) with little or no modification.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which type of language is generally more portable?
explanation: High-level languages are hardware-independent and portable; machine code and assembly are specific to a CPU architecture.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a linker?
options: A program that combines object code files and libraries into a single executable
explanation: A linker joins compiled object code files with required library files to create a complete, runnable executable program.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A loader in computing:
options: Loads an executable program into RAM for execution
explanation: A loader copies an executable program from secondary storage into RAM and prepares it for execution by the CPU.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a library in programming?
options: A collection of pre-written, reusable code (functions/modules)
explanation: A library is a collection of pre-written, tested functions and routines that programmers can import and call, saving time.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is pseudocode?
options: An informal, structured English-like notation for describing algorithms before coding
explanation: Pseudocode is an informal, human-readable description of an algorithm using structured constructs, not tied to any specific language.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is bytecode?
options: An intermediate code (e.g. Java bytecode) executed by a virtual machine
explanation: Bytecode is an intermediate representation compiled from source code, executed by a virtual machine (e.g. JVM for Java) rather than directly by hardware.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a virtual machine (in the context of languages)?
options: Software that executes bytecode, abstracting the underlying hardware
explanation: A language VM (e.g. Java Virtual Machine) is software that runs bytecode, providing platform independence across different hardware.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of these is an example of a scripting language?
explanation: JavaScript is a scripting language — typically interpreted at runtime, used for web page interactivity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the main difference between compiled and interpreted execution?
options: Compiled: whole program translated before running; Interpreted: translated line-by-line during running
explanation: A compiler translates the whole program once before execution; an interpreter translates and executes one line at a time during runtime.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "syntax" of a programming language mean?
options: The rules governing the structure and format of valid code
explanation: Syntax defines the rules for writing valid code — correct grammar, punctuation, and structure that the translator can parse.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "semantics" of a programming language refer to?
options: The grammar rules of the language
The meaning of syntactically correct statements
explanation: Semantics describes what syntactically valid code actually means — what actions it causes when executed.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which translator is used for Java source code?
options: Compiler to bytecode, then JVM interpreter/JIT
explanation: Java source is compiled to bytecode by javac; the JVM then interprets (or JIT-compiles) bytecode at runtime.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is JIT (Just-In-Time) compilation?
options: Compiling code before it is written
Compiling bytecode to native machine code at runtime, improving speed
explanation: JIT compilation translates bytecode to native machine code during execution, combining portability with near-native speed.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a markup language (e.g. HTML)?
options: A language that annotates text to describe its structure/presentation
explanation: A markup language uses tags to annotate text, defining structure and formatting (e.g. HTML for web pages, XML for data).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which feature of an IDE helps catch syntax errors before running?
explanation: Modern IDEs highlight syntax errors in real time as you type, allowing immediate correction before compilation.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a breakpoint in debugging?
options: A point where the program crashes
A marker set by the programmer to pause execution at a specific line
explanation: A breakpoint pauses program execution at a chosen line, letting the programmer inspect variables and step through code.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "stepping through" code mean in a debugger?
options: Executing one line at a time to observe behavior
explanation: Stepping executes code one statement at a time, allowing the programmer to observe each change in state.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an IDE's auto-complete feature?
options: Suggesting code completions as the programmer types
explanation: Auto-complete (IntelliSense) suggests valid completions for variable names, functions, and keywords as the programmer types, speeding up coding.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a scripting language typically used for?
options: Automating tasks and web scripting, usually interpreted
explanation: Scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, Bash) are typically interpreted and used for automation, rapid prototyping, and web development.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What are keywords (reserved words) in a programming language?
options: Words with special meaning that cannot be used as identifiers (e.g. IF, WHILE, PRINT)
explanation: Keywords are reserved words with predefined meaning in the language (e.g. if, while, for); they cannot be used as variable names.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which is an advantage of using an IDE over a plain text editor?
options: Provides debugging, syntax checking, and code completion in one tool
explanation: An IDE integrates multiple developer tools — editor, debugger, syntax checker, auto-complete — improving productivity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "portability" problem exist with low-level languages?
options: They are too easy to learn
Code written for one CPU architecture will not run on a different architecture without rewriting
explanation: Low-level code is architecture-specific; assembly for an Intel x86 CPU won't run on an ARM CPU without rewriting.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a one-to-one relationship in assembly language?
options: Each mnemonic corresponds to exactly one machine code instruction
explanation: Assembly mnemonics have a one-to-one correspondence with machine code instructions, unlike high-level statements that expand to many instructions.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What are comments in code?
options: Non-executing text added to explain the code to human readers
explanation: Comments are ignored by the translator and serve only to explain the code's purpose, improving maintainability.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is structured programming?
options: A programming approach using sequence, selection (IF), and iteration (loops) as building blocks
explanation: Structured programming builds programs from three control structures: sequence, selection, and iteration, avoiding unstructured jumps (GOTO).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an event-driven programming paradigm?
options: Programs run from top to bottom only
Program flow is determined by user actions or system events (clicks, key presses)
explanation: Event-driven programs wait for events (mouse clicks, keypresses, network messages) and execute handlers in response, common in GUIs.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of these best describes object-oriented programming (OOP)?
options: Organising code around objects that combine data (attributes) and behaviour (methods)
explanation: OOP models the world as objects with attributes and methods, supporting encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a class in OOP?
options: A blueprint or template that defines the attributes and methods of objects
explanation: A class defines the structure (attributes) and behaviour (methods) that its instances (objects) will have.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an object in OOP?
options: An instance of a class with specific attribute values
explanation: An object is an instance of a class — it has the structure defined by the class but with its own specific data values.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is encapsulation in OOP?
options: Hiding internal implementation details and exposing only what is necessary
explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and methods together inside a class and restricts direct external access to internal state, exposing only a defined interface.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of these is a feature shared by most high-level languages?
options: They execute directly on CPU hardware
They provide abstractions like variables, loops, and functions
explanation: High-level languages provide human-friendly abstractions: named variables, control structures, functions, and data types, hiding hardware details.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an embedded system?
options: A computer system designed for a specific, dedicated function within a larger device
explanation: An embedded system is a specialised computing system built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function (e.g. microwave controller).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of these is an example of an embedded system?
options: The control system inside a washing machine
explanation: A washing machine's control board is an embedded system — dedicated hardware and software performing a fixed task.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a microcontroller?
options: A small, single-chip computer combining CPU, memory, and I/O, used in embedded systems
explanation: A microcontroller is a compact integrated circuit containing a CPU core, program memory (ROM/Flash), data memory (RAM), and I/O interfaces on one chip.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a sensor in the context of embedded systems?
options: An output device that controls actuators
A device that detects physical conditions (temperature, light, pressure) and converts them to electrical signals
explanation: A sensor detects a physical quantity in the real world (temperature, light, humidity) and converts it to an electrical signal the microcontroller can read.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an actuator?
options: A device that reads sensor data
A device that converts an electrical signal into a physical action (movement, heat, light)
explanation: An actuator receives a signal from the microcontroller and performs a physical action — e.g. a motor turns, a heater heats, an LED lights.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which memory type stores the program in a microcontroller?
explanation: Program code in a microcontroller is stored in non-volatile ROM or Flash memory so it persists when power is off.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the role of RAM in a microcontroller?
options: Temporary working storage for variables and runtime data
explanation: RAM provides temporary storage for variables, stack, and working data during program execution; it loses data when power is removed.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does the term "real-time" mean in embedded systems?
options: The system has no delays at all
The system responds to inputs within defined, predictable time constraints
The system uses the internet clock
explanation: A real-time system guarantees responses within specific time deadlines — critical for safety systems like airbags or medical devices.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a feedback loop in a control system?
options: A loop that runs forever in code
The process of using sensor output to adjust the system's behaviour
explanation: Feedback uses sensor readings to continuously correct a system's output — e.g. a thermostat reads temperature and adjusts heating.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following best describes an open-loop control system?
options: It uses sensor feedback to adjust output
It executes a fixed set of actions without measuring output (no feedback)
It always runs in real time
explanation: An open-loop system performs actions without checking the result — e.g. a toaster on a fixed timer.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following best describes a closed-loop control system?
options: It uses feedback from sensors to continuously adjust its output
It requires human input every cycle
explanation: A closed-loop (feedback) system monitors its output with sensors and adjusts behaviour accordingly — e.g. a thermostat, cruise control.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a GPIO pin on a microcontroller?
options: A General Purpose Input/Output pin that can be configured to read (input) or control (output) signals
explanation: GPIO (General Purpose Input/Output) pins are programmable digital pins that can be set as inputs (reading sensors) or outputs (driving actuators).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the clock speed of a microcontroller?
options: How fast it accesses the internet
The number of instruction cycles executed per second (measured in Hz/MHz)
explanation: Clock speed (Hz or MHz) determines how many basic operations the microcontroller executes per second.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a Raspberry Pi?
options: A single-board computer (SBC) used for general computing and embedded/IoT projects
explanation: Raspberry Pi is a single-board computer running a full OS (Linux), used in education and IoT/embedded projects that need more computing power.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an Arduino?
options: A low-cost open-source microcontroller board used for physical computing and prototyping
explanation: Arduino is an open-source microcontroller platform designed for easy prototyping of interactive hardware projects.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the Internet of Things (IoT)?
options: A network of physical devices embedded with sensors and connectivity to exchange data online
explanation: IoT refers to everyday physical devices (thermostats, cameras, appliances) connected to the internet, sharing data and enabling remote control.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which component converts an analogue sensor signal to digital data a microcontroller can process?
explanation: An ADC converts a continuous analogue voltage from a sensor into a discrete digital number the microcontroller can process.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does a DAC do?
options: Converts digital signals to analogue (e.g. to drive a speaker)
explanation: A DAC converts digital values from the microcontroller to an analogue voltage, used for audio output or analogue control signals.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) used for in embedded systems?
options: Controlling analogue-like output (motor speed, LED brightness) using digital switching
explanation: PWM varies the duty cycle (on/off ratio) of a digital signal to simulate analogue control — used to vary motor speed or LED brightness.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a typical application of an embedded system in a car?
options: Engine control unit (ECU) managing fuel injection and emissions
explanation: An ECU is an embedded system that reads sensors (oxygen, throttle) and controls actuators (fuel injectors) to optimise engine performance.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a watchdog timer in an embedded system?
options: A hardware timer that resets the system if the software becomes unresponsive
explanation: A watchdog timer resets the microcontroller if the program fails to "kick" (reset) the timer within a set period, recovering from software lockups.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is EEPROM?
options: Erasable Programmable ROM that retains data without power and can be rewritten electrically
explanation: EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM) is non-volatile memory that can be erased and rewritten electrically, used for storing settings/configuration.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is interrupt-driven programming?
options: A technique where an event (interrupt) pauses normal execution to run a handler routine
explanation: An interrupt causes the CPU to pause its current task, execute an interrupt service routine (ISR) to handle the event, then resume the original task.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an interrupt service routine (ISR)?
options: A short function executed in response to a hardware interrupt
explanation: An ISR is a special function that the CPU calls automatically when a specific interrupt occurs (e.g. a button press or timer overflow).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Why are embedded systems often programmed in C or C++?
options: For direct hardware control, small memory footprint, and high execution speed
explanation: C/C++ provides low-level hardware access, deterministic performance, and generates compact machine code — critical for resource-constrained embedded systems.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the main difference between a microcontroller and a microprocessor?
options: A microcontroller integrates CPU, memory, and peripherals on one chip; a microprocessor is CPU only
A microcontroller needs external RAM always
explanation: A microcontroller is a complete system-on-chip (CPU + memory + I/O); a microprocessor is just the CPU, requiring external memory and peripherals.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "bare-metal" programming mean?
options: Writing code that runs directly on hardware without an operating system
explanation: Bare-metal programming involves writing code that runs directly on hardware with no OS layer, giving maximum control and performance.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is RTOS (Real-Time Operating System)?
options: An OS designed for predictable, time-constrained embedded applications
explanation: An RTOS provides deterministic task scheduling for embedded systems where response times must be guaranteed within strict deadlines.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is a common communication protocol used in embedded systems?
explanation: I²C, SPI, and UART are common embedded communication protocols for connecting microcontrollers to sensors and peripherals over short distances.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an embedded system's firmware?
options: Software permanently stored in non-volatile memory that controls the hardware
explanation: Firmware is software embedded in ROM/Flash that provides low-level hardware control — it persists across power cycles.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a bootloader in an embedded system?
options: To run the main application directly
A small program that initialises hardware and loads the main application firmware
explanation: A bootloader is the first code that runs on power-up; it initialises hardware and loads the main firmware from Flash into RAM for execution.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What type of sensor measures temperature in an embedded system?
explanation: A thermistor (resistance changes with temperature) or thermocouple is commonly used to measure temperature in embedded systems.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does a PIR sensor detect?
options: Infrared radiation from moving warm bodies (motion detection)
explanation: A PIR (Passive Infrared) sensor detects changes in infrared radiation caused by movement of warm bodies — used in burglar alarms and lighting.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a relay in an embedded system?
options: An electrically controlled switch that allows a low-power signal to control a high-power circuit
explanation: A relay is an electromagnetic switch; a small control signal from the microcontroller opens/closes a contact that controls a high-power circuit.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "latency" mean in embedded systems?
options: The delay between an input event and the system's response
explanation: Latency is the time delay between an event occurring (e.g. button press) and the system producing its response — minimising it is critical in real-time systems.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a voltage regulator in an embedded system?
options: To provide a stable, constant voltage to the microcontroller regardless of supply variations
explanation: A voltage regulator ensures the microcontroller receives a steady supply voltage (e.g. 3.3V or 5V), protecting it from supply fluctuations.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does duty cycle mean in PWM?
options: The percentage of time the signal is HIGH in one period
explanation: Duty cycle is the ratio of the ON time to the total period, expressed as a percentage — 50% means the signal is HIGH half the time.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the role of a crystal oscillator in a microcontroller?
options: To provide a precise clock signal that synchronises all operations
explanation: A crystal oscillator generates a precise, stable frequency used as the system clock to synchronise all microcontroller operations.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is debouncing in embedded systems?
options: Filtering out rapid, spurious signals (e.g. mechanical switch bounce) to detect a single clean event
explanation: Mechanical switches bounce (rapidly open/close) when pressed; debouncing (in hardware or software) filters this noise to register only one clean press.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a state machine in embedded programming?
options: A model where the system moves between defined states based on inputs/events
explanation: A finite state machine (FSM) models system behaviour as a set of states with transitions triggered by inputs/events — common in embedded control logic.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is polling in embedded systems?
options: Continuously checking the status of an input in a loop rather than using interrupts
explanation: Polling repeatedly reads an input status in a loop; simple but wastes CPU cycles. Interrupts are more efficient for infrequent events.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is power management important for in embedded systems?
options: Extending battery life by reducing energy consumption in battery-powered devices
explanation: Many embedded devices are battery-powered; efficient power management (sleep modes, clock gating) extends battery life significantly.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is an I/O port on a microcontroller?
options: A set of pins through which the microcontroller communicates with external devices
explanation: I/O ports are groups of pins that the microcontroller uses to send or receive data to/from external components like sensors, displays, and motors.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which embedded system application requires the most stringent real-time guarantees?
options: An airbag deployment system in a car
explanation: An airbag system must detect a crash and deploy within milliseconds — missing this deadline could cost lives, making it a hard real-time system.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) do?
options: A synchronous serial communication protocol for microcontrollers to communicate with peripherals at high speed
explanation: SPI is a synchronous, full-duplex serial protocol using four lines (MOSI, MISO, SCLK, SS) for fast communication between a microcontroller and peripherals.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter)?
options: An asynchronous serial communication protocol using TX (transmit) and RX (receive) lines
explanation: UART is a simple asynchronous serial protocol using TX and RX lines, commonly used for communication between microcontrollers and devices like GPS, Bluetooth modules.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a pull-up resistor on a GPIO pin?
options: To ensure the pin reads a defined HIGH level when no device is driving it
explanation: A pull-up resistor connects the pin to VCC, ensuring it reads HIGH when floating (no active driver), preventing undefined/noisy readings.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a smart home system an example of?
options: An IoT-enabled embedded system network controlling home devices
explanation: Smart home systems use networked embedded devices (thermostats, cameras, locks) connected via IoT protocols to enable remote monitoring and control.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the main advantage of embedded systems over general-purpose computers for specific tasks?
options: They are optimised for their specific task: lower cost, size, power consumption, and higher reliability
explanation: Embedded systems are purpose-built — optimised hardware and software deliver lower cost, smaller size, less power, and higher reliability than a general PC for that task.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is a characteristic of most embedded systems?
options: Dedicated function, limited resources, often real-time requirements
explanation: Embedded systems are dedicated to one task, have limited CPU/memory resources, often must meet real-time deadlines, and frequently run on battery power.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a parity bit?
explanation: A parity bit is added so the total number of 1-bits is even (even parity) or odd (odd parity), allowing single-bit errors to be detected.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In even parity, the byte 1011001 has how many 1-bits before the parity bit is added?
explanation: Counting: 1+0+1+1+0+0+1 = 4. Since 4 is already even, the parity bit would be 0.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which error detection method adds together all data values and sends the total?
explanation: A checksum sums all bytes in a block of data. The receiver recalculates and compares; a mismatch indicates an error.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does ARQ stand for in error control?
explanation: ARQ is a protocol where the receiver requests retransmission when an error is detected, ensuring reliable delivery.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In an echo check, the receiver sends the data back to the sender. What does the sender do?
explanation: The sender compares the echoed data to what was sent. Any difference indicates a transmission error.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which check digit scheme is used on barcodes (EAN-13)?
explanation: EAN-13 barcodes use a modulo 10 check digit scheme where alternate digits are multiplied by 1 or 3 and summed.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A check digit detects which type of error most effectively?
explanation: Check digits are specifically designed to catch transposition errors (e.g. swapping two adjacent digits), which are common in manual data entry.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the main limitation of a parity bit?
options: It only detects odd numbers of errors
explanation: A parity bit detects an odd number of bit errors (1, 3, 5…). An even number of errors cancel out and go undetected.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A block checksum of 0xFF is sent. The receiver calculates 0xFE. What should the receiver do?
explanation: A checksum mismatch means an error occurred. The receiver requests the block be resent (ARQ).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which method can both detect AND correct errors?
explanation: Hamming codes add multiple parity bits at specific positions, enabling the receiver to locate and correct single-bit errors.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is "odd parity"?
options: The total number of 1s including the parity bit is odd
The data byte has an odd number of bits
explanation: In odd parity, the parity bit is set so the total count of 1-bits in the byte plus parity bit is an odd number.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A 7-bit data value 1100110 is sent with even parity. What is the parity bit?
explanation: 1100110 has four 1-bits. Four is already even, so the parity bit is 0 to maintain even parity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which error detection method is most suitable for detecting errors in streamed video data?
explanation: For streaming, packet checksums detect errors; unlike ARQ, retransmitting would cause stuttering, so corrupted frames are often dropped.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a VRC (Vertical Redundancy Check)?
options: A parity bit check on each byte
explanation: VRC adds a parity bit to each character/byte, checking each "vertical" column of bits.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: LRC (Longitudinal Redundancy Check) adds parity for which direction?
explanation: LRC calculates parity across all bytes at each bit position in a block, catching errors that VRC alone might miss.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A check digit of 7 is expected but 9 is received. What most likely happened?
options: A digit was transposed during transmission
explanation: Check digits are designed to detect transposition errors — one of the most common data entry mistakes.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does CRC stand for?
explanation: CRC is a powerful error-detection method using polynomial division, widely used in network protocols and storage.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In ARQ, what is a NAK?
options: Negative Acknowledgement — data received with error
explanation: A NAK (Negative Acknowledgement) signals the sender that data was received incorrectly and must be retransmitted.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which check digit method is used for ISBN-10 book codes?
explanation: ISBN-10 uses modulo 11, which is why the final check digit can be X (representing 10).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A forward error correction (FEC) scheme differs from ARQ because:
options: FEC uses checksums, ARQ uses parity
FEC only works on text data
explanation: FEC embeds enough redundancy for the receiver to correct errors independently, ideal for one-way links (e.g. satellite broadcast).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: The Luhn algorithm is primarily used to validate:
explanation: The Luhn check digit algorithm is the standard validation method for credit card numbers.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Odd parity is used for a byte. The received byte 10110111 has how many 1-bits?
explanation: Counting: 1+0+1+1+0+1+1+1 = 6. For odd parity the total should be odd, but 6 is even — an error is detected.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a sequence number in ARQ protocols?
options: To detect duplicate or out-of-order packets
explanation: Sequence numbers let the receiver detect missing, duplicate or out-of-order packets and request the correct retransmission.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which term describes the extra bits added purely for error detection/correction?
explanation: Redundant/overhead bits are the additional bits added for error detection and correction; they add bandwidth cost.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A double-bit error occurs during transmission with parity checking. What happens?
options: The error is detected and corrected
The error is detected but not corrected
explanation: A single parity bit cannot detect an even number of bit errors because they cancel out — the parity still looks correct.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is data integrity?
options: Ensuring data remains accurate and unaltered
explanation: Data integrity means that data is complete, accurate and has not been corrupted during storage or transmission.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A checksum is calculated BEFORE transmission and again AFTER. Why?
explanation: Comparing before-and-after checksums confirms the data arrived intact.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which term describes errors caused by electrical interference over a transmission line?
explanation: Electrical interference (noise) can flip bits during transmission, causing noise errors.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What kind of parity system uses both VRC and LRC together?
explanation: 2D parity checks each row (VRC) and each column (LRC), allowing single-bit error correction.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following is NOT a method of error detection?
explanation: Data compression reduces file size but does not detect errors. Parity, checksum and CRC are all error-detection methods.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In a network, the sending device calculates a checksum and appends it. What does the receiving device do first?
options: Store the checksum in a database
explanation: The receiver independently recalculates the checksum and compares it to the received value to detect corruption.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "data validation" check, as opposed to "data verification"?
options: That data is entered correctly twice
That data is reasonable and within allowed limits
explanation: Validation checks rules (range, type, format). Verification checks the same data was entered twice consistently.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which error detection method is most commonly used in Ethernet frames?
explanation: Ethernet frames use CRC-32, a 32-bit cyclic redundancy check, as it provides very strong error detection.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A "burst error" affects:
explanation: A burst error corrupts a sequence of consecutive bits, often caused by lightning strikes or brief signal loss.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Echo check is mainly used in:
explanation: Echo check (loopback) was historically used in terminal/mainframe sessions to verify each keystroke was received correctly.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which is a hardware solution to data integrity over time?
explanation: RAID stores redundant data across multiple drives so if one fails, data can be reconstructed — maintaining integrity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What happens in a "stop-and-wait" ARQ scheme?
options: Sender sends all data then waits
Sender sends one frame and waits for ACK before sending the next
Sender and receiver swap roles after each byte
Data is sent in full-duplex only
explanation: Stop-and-wait ARQ sends one frame at a time, waiting for acknowledgement, making it simple but inefficient.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which scenario best demonstrates a check digit being useful?
options: Entering a credit card number manually
explanation: Check digits are designed for manual data entry where transposition mistakes are common, such as typing a credit card number.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A parity error is detected. What does this tell you?
options: An ODD number of bits were flipped
An EVEN number of bits were flipped
explanation: Parity detects only an odd number of flipped bits. An even number cancels out and appears correct.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What additional function can a CRC perform that a simple checksum cannot?
options: Locate the position of an error
explanation: Advanced CRC variants can not only detect but pinpoint where errors occurred, unlike simple additive checksums.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Data is transmitted as: 10101010. With even parity, what is the parity bit?
explanation: 10101010 has four 1-bits. Four is even, so the parity bit is 0 to keep the total even.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is "data verification" in data entry?
options: Checking data is within a valid range
Re-entering data to confirm it was typed correctly
explanation: Verification involves entering data twice and comparing both entries to catch keyboarding mistakes.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A length check is a type of:
explanation: A length check is a validation rule ensuring a value (e.g. a password) contains the correct number of characters.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which best describes "data accuracy"?
options: Data is stored in the smallest possible space
Data correctly represents the real-world value it is meant to hold
Data is readable by any device
explanation: Data accuracy means the stored data matches the actual real-world facts it represents.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In networking, a "frame check sequence" (FCS) is:
options: A CRC value appended to a frame
explanation: The FCS is typically a CRC value at the end of an Ethernet frame used by the receiver to verify integrity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which method provides the STRONGEST error detection for large data blocks?
explanation: CRC using polynomial division provides the strongest error detection for large blocks, detecting burst errors that simpler methods miss.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: An ISBN-13 check digit is calculated using modulo:
explanation: ISBN-13 uses a modulo 10 algorithm (similar to EAN-13) with alternating weights of 1 and 3.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the overhead of adding error detection to transmitted data?
options: Increased data size and bandwidth usage
explanation: Error detection bits add extra data (overhead), increasing transmission size and reducing usable bandwidth.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the key difference between error detection and error correction?
options: Detection is faster, correction is slower
Detection identifies errors exist; correction fixes them without retransmission
Detection uses CRC, correction uses parity
explanation: Error detection only flags a problem; error correction (FEC) has enough redundancy to fix it without a resend.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A "presence check" validation rule ensures:
options: Data is within a numeric range
A required field is not left empty
Data is of the correct type
explanation: A presence check verifies that a mandatory field contains a value, preventing empty/null entries.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is malware?
options: Software designed to harm or exploit systems
explanation: Malware (malicious software) is any program intentionally designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorised access to computer systems.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which type of malware replicates itself by attaching to legitimate programs?
explanation: A virus attaches itself to a host program and replicates when that program runs, spreading to other files.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A worm differs from a virus because:
options: A worm needs a host file to spread
A worm spreads across networks independently
A worm is a type of encryption
explanation: Unlike a virus, a worm is a standalone program that self-replicates across networks without needing a host file.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a Trojan horse?
options: A virus that spreads via email
explanation: A Trojan pretends to be useful software but contains malicious code that runs when the user installs or runs it.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is phishing?
options: Tricking users into revealing credentials via fake websites/emails
explanation: Phishing uses deceptive emails or websites that mimic legitimate services to steal usernames, passwords and payment details.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does DoS stand for?
explanation: A Denial of Service attack floods a system with traffic to make it unavailable to legitimate users.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A DDoS attack uses:
explanation: A Distributed DoS uses a botnet — many compromised computers — to amplify the attack volume.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is SQL injection?
options: A method to speed up database queries
Inserting malicious SQL code into input fields to manipulate a database
A way to back up databases
explanation: SQL injection exploits poor input sanitisation to run unauthorised SQL commands, potentially exposing or destroying data.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: The CIA triad in cybersecurity stands for:
explanation: The CIA triad is the core model: Confidentiality (only authorised access), Integrity (data unchanged), Availability (systems accessible when needed).
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which CIA property ensures that data has not been tampered with?
explanation: Integrity means data remains accurate and unmodified — checksums, hashing and digital signatures help protect it.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does TLS protect in web communications?
options: Data in transit between browser and server
explanation: TLS (Transport Layer Security) encrypts data between a web browser and server, indicated by HTTPS.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a VPN?
options: An encrypted tunnel between a device and a remote server
explanation: A Virtual Private Network creates an encrypted tunnel, masking the user's IP and securing traffic on public networks.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which attack captures network traffic to steal credentials?
explanation: A man-in-the-middle or packet sniffing attack intercepts network traffic to read unencrypted credentials.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is ransomware?
options: Malware that encrypts files and demands payment to restore them
explanation: Ransomware encrypts a victim's files, making them inaccessible until a ransom (usually cryptocurrency) is paid.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a firewall's primary purpose?
options: To filter incoming and outgoing network traffic based on rules
explanation: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic, blocking unauthorised access while allowing legitimate traffic.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is spyware?
options: Malware that secretly monitors and sends user data to attackers
A legitimate monitoring tool for parents
explanation: Spyware runs secretly, logging keystrokes, capturing screenshots or tracking browsing to steal personal information.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A brute force attack on a password tries:
options: All possible character combinations until the correct password is found
explanation: Brute force systematically tries every possible combination of characters until the correct password is found.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is two-factor authentication (2FA)?
options: Requiring something you know AND something you have/are
explanation: 2FA adds a second verification step (e.g. a code sent to your phone) on top of a password.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of HTTPS?
options: To encrypt web traffic using TLS/SSL
explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) uses TLS to encrypt data between the browser and the web server, protecting it from interception.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A zero-day vulnerability is:
options: A virus that activates on a specific date
A newly discovered flaw with no available patch
A firewall rule that blocks all traffic
explanation: A zero-day exploit targets a vulnerability before the developer has created and distributed a patch.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is social engineering?
options: Manipulating people into revealing confidential information
explanation: Social engineering exploits human psychology rather than technical vulnerabilities — phishing is a common example.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which CIA property is most affected by a DoS attack?
explanation: A DoS attack makes systems unavailable to legitimate users, directly targeting the Availability property of the CIA triad.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does a digital certificate verify?
options: The identity of a website and its public key
The file size of web pages
explanation: A digital certificate is issued by a Certificate Authority (CA) and verifies that a website is who it claims to be.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is encryption?
options: Converting plaintext into unreadable ciphertext using an algorithm and key
explanation: Encryption transforms readable data into ciphertext; only holders of the decryption key can read it.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is symmetric encryption?
options: Encryption using the same key for both encryption and decryption
explanation: Symmetric encryption (e.g. AES) uses one shared key. It's fast but requires secure key exchange.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: In asymmetric encryption, what is the public key used for?
options: Encrypting messages to be sent to the key owner
explanation: Anyone can use the recipient's public key to encrypt a message; only the recipient's private key can decrypt it.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a botnet?
options: A network of infected computers controlled by an attacker
explanation: A botnet is a collection of compromised devices ("bots") controlled remotely by an attacker for DDoS attacks, spam, etc.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of an intrusion detection system (IDS)?
options: To monitor network traffic and alert on suspicious activity
explanation: An IDS monitors network or system events and alerts administrators to potential security breaches.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: SQL injection can be prevented by:
options: Validating and sanitising all user inputs (parameterised queries)
explanation: Using parameterised queries / prepared statements ensures user input is never executed as SQL code.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a keylogger?
options: A program that speeds up keyboard input
Malware that records every keystroke and sends it to an attacker
explanation: A keylogger silently records all keystrokes — capturing passwords, messages and credit card numbers.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does the term "authentication" mean in cybersecurity?
options: Verifying the identity of a user or system
explanation: Authentication confirms that someone is who they claim to be — using passwords, biometrics or tokens.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is "authorisation" in cybersecurity?
options: Determining what an authenticated user is allowed to do
explanation: Authorisation defines access rights and permissions AFTER identity has been verified.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which is an example of a "strong" password?
explanation: A strong password uses upper and lowercase letters, numbers and symbols, is long, and avoids dictionary words.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a "honeypot" in cybersecurity?
options: A decoy system designed to lure and detect attackers
explanation: A honeypot is a trap system that mimics real infrastructure to attract attackers and study their techniques.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which attack embeds malicious scripts in web pages that execute in other users' browsers?
explanation: XSS injects malicious JavaScript into web pages that runs in victims' browsers, stealing cookies or performing actions.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network security?
options: To provide a buffer zone between the internet and internal networks
explanation: A DMZ (demilitarised zone) is a network segment that houses publicly accessible servers, isolated from the internal network.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "principle of least privilege" mean?
options: Users should only have the access rights they need for their job
All users should share one account
Passwords should be as short as possible
explanation: Least privilege limits each user's permissions to only what is necessary, reducing damage from breaches.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: A hacker uses a tool to test all words in a dictionary as passwords. This is called:
explanation: A dictionary attack uses a list of common words and phrases, which is faster than pure brute force.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is HTTPS port number?
explanation: HTTPS uses port 443; HTTP uses port 80. Knowing default ports is important for firewall configuration.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is the role of a Certificate Authority (CA)?
options: To issue and verify digital certificates confirming website identities
explanation: CAs are trusted organisations that sign digital certificates, allowing browsers to verify website authenticity.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which type of malware is designed to generate revenue by displaying unwanted advertisements?
explanation: Adware displays unsolicited advertisements; while not always malicious, it can degrade performance and privacy.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a rootkit?
options: Malware that hides its presence by modifying OS functions
explanation: Rootkits hide deeply in the OS, often at the kernel level, making them very difficult to detect and remove.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What security measure should be taken when using public Wi-Fi?
options: Use a VPN to encrypt traffic
explanation: Public Wi-Fi is unencrypted and monitored; a VPN protects your data by encrypting it before it leaves your device.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "patching" software mean?
options: Installing updates that fix security vulnerabilities
explanation: Security patches fix known vulnerabilities; unpatched software is a major target for attackers.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: Which of the following describes a "man-in-the-middle" attack?
options: An attacker physically between two users
An attacker intercepts and possibly alters communication between two parties
A DoS attack on a router
explanation: MITM attacks secretly intercept traffic between two parties, enabling eavesdropping or data manipulation.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What does "non-repudiation" mean in cybersecurity?
options: The ability to deny sending a message
The assurance that a sender cannot deny sending a message
explanation: Non-repudiation uses digital signatures to prove a message was sent by a specific party, preventing false denial.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is a "data breach"?
options: Unauthorised access to or disclosure of sensitive data
explanation: A data breach occurs when confidential data is accessed, stolen or exposed without authorisation.
subject: CS (IGCSE 0478)

text: What is "access control" in cybersecurity?
options: Managing who is allowed to use which resources
